SYRACUSE, NY - Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today announced that he is cosponsoring H.R. 5487, the Keep the Lights Local Act, legislation to prohibit foreign ownership of American public utilities.

The bill would help protect ratepayers, strengthen accountability, and keep more of the money families pay through their monthly utility bills invested in American communities instead of supporting profits overseas.

Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) said, “Families in Central New York and the Mohawk Valley are paying too much to power their homes and businesses, and they shouldn’t be forced to subsidize the profits of foreign corporations. The Keep the Lights Local Act will help lower costs and keep more ratepayer dollars here at home - supporting grid reliability, infrastructure improvements, and local workers. Keeping control of energy production and transmission is essential to American energy and national security. I’ll keep fighting for affordable, reliable energy and real accountability for ratepayers.”

Under current federal law, foreign corporations and foreign governments are not prohibited from owning public utility holding companies in the United States. The Keep the Lights Local Act would close that gap by barring foreign corporations and governments from owning American public utility holding companies. The legislation was introduced by Representative Josh Riley (NY-19).

Mannion has made energy affordability and ratepayer protection a priority in Congress. He recently voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act to prevent data centers from shifting their electricity costs to families and small businesses, cosponsored legislation to end special federal tax breaks for data centers, and has called for data centers to mitigate impacts on local air quality, drinking water and water supplies.
title: Representative John Mannion Cosponsors the ‘Keep the Lights Local Act’ to Prohibit Foreign Ownership of American Utilities and Keep Ratepayer Dollars Invested at Home

Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke to reporters following a roundtable in Providence with Representatives Seth Magaziner (RI-02) and Gabe Amo (RI-01) and local healthcare union leaders about how House Democrats are committed to ending the Republican healthcare crisis and building a healthcare system that works for everyday Americans.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good afternoon, everyone. It’s an honor and a privilege to be here in the great state of Rhode Island. Thank you, Congressman Magaziner for convening us and for your incredible leadership in the healthcare area and in many other areas on behalf of the people of the Ocean State. And I want to thank, of course, Congressman Magaziner and Congressman Amo, just for their partnership, their tremendous commitment to improving the lives of the people of Rhode Island and the American people and for the work that they have done and will continue to do to address the healthcare crisis that exists in the United States of America right now. Certainly want to thank Jesse and Lynn and Pat, of course, SEIU 1199, United Nurses, the AFL-CIO—all of the wonderful practitioners and healthcare providers who joined us at a very robust, comprehensive, thoughtful roundtable discussion where I learned a lot about the challenges that the people of Rhode Island are confronting in the midst of a Republican healthcare crisis that is worsening their ability to provide comprehensive and compassionate care to the people that they so ably serve.

And unfortunately, it’s a familiar conversation that I’ve had—as I’ve traveled the country—with people all throughout America. The Republican healthcare crisis is devastating the ability of healthcare providers to serve our families, our loved ones, our friends and our neighbors in the way that they are committed to doing, particularly in an environment now where you have so many healthcare providers who are overworked and underpaid, as well as, of course, far too often underappreciated. House Democrats appreciate the work of our healthcare heroes and are committed to making sure that we provide them with the support necessary to enable them to provide the best possible care to people here in Rhode Island and all throughout America.

As House Democrats, our core principle is that when you work hard and play by the rules, you should be able to live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. And that includes access to high-quality, affordable healthcare. It cannot be the situation where, in this country—the wealthiest country in the history of the world—accessing high-quality, affordable healthcare is simply a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. No, it has to be a right available to every single person here in Rhode Island, every single American. That is our commitment. A lot of work that needs to be done because of the Republican healthcare crisis. So we’re committed, as a top priority as House Democrats, to reversing these Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And then getting to work together with providers, like those we had an opportunity to talk with today, to construct the best possible healthcare ecosystem, a system that the American people deserve so they can go see a nurse and go see a doctor and get high-quality healthcare whenever and wherever they need it.

Republicans have made a lot of promises to the American people, and they’ve broken them all. Donald Trump promised to lower costs on day one, but costs haven’t gone down in the United States of America. Costs have gone up as a direct result of policies, including the Trump Tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans and the people of Rhode Island by thousands of dollars per year. Donald Trump promised not to start endless wars in the Middle East, but to stop them, and then turned around and has gotten us involved in a reckless and costly war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the people here in Rhode Island and beyond.

It was Donald Trump who promised to love and cherish Medicaid and then turned around, along with House Republicans and Senate Republicans, and enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, putting a target on hospitals here in Rhode Island, putting a target on nursing homes here in Rhode Island, putting a target on home care workers here in Rhode Island and putting a target on community-based health centers. Enough with this Republican assault on healthcare. We’re committed, as House Democrats, to turning it around.

Full press availability can be watched here.

###
title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN PROVIDENCE: “AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE HAS TO BE A RIGHT AVAILABLE TO EVERY SINGLE AMERICAN”

(Towson, MD) – Maryland Congressman Johnny Olszewski today issued the following statement after President Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO from the White House and confiscated the press credentials of their journalists. The three outlets announced today they are suing the Trump Administration over the ban.

“A free and independent press is fundamental to our democracy. President Trump’s attack on news organizations he doesn’t like is outrageous and unconstitutional.

This issue is bigger than any one news outlet. It’s about whether the President of the United States gets to decide which journalists are allowed access to him based on favorable coverage. He doesn’t.

Unfortunately, this is part of a broader pattern from the Trump Administration — using the power of the federal government to punish journalists and restrict the ability of the press to hold those in power accountable. That is the kind of overreach we associate with authoritarian regimes, not a healthy democracy. I commend other, competing news organizations for standing in solidarity to defend the First Amendment.

The White House belongs to the American people. They have a right to an independent press that asks tough questions, reports the facts, and holds their government accountable.”
title: Olszewski on Trump’s Attack on the Press: “Outrageous and Unconstitutional”

GLEN COVE, NY — Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-03) was recognized today by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce with its “Advocate for American Business” Award during a stop of the Chamber’s national Free Enterprise Express Opportunity Tour at Standard Bots in Glen Cove.

U.S. Chamber Executive Vice President and Chief Policy Officer Neil Bradley presented Suozzi with the award, recognizing his bipartisan, commonsense approach to governing, his leadership as Democratic Co-Chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus, and his work on affordability, immigration reform, and other issues affecting American families and businesses.

Suozzi is the first Democratic Member of Congress to receive the award during the Chamber’s national Opportunity Tour.

“The U.S. Chamber is proud to recognize Rep. Tom Suozzi as the first Democratic Member of Congress to receive this award on the Free Enterprise Bus Tour. Rep. Suozzi has been a steadfast defender of free market capitalism and his approach to policy prioritizes real solutions for American families and businesses. We look forward to continuing to work with him to advance free enterprise policies that allow businesses, workers, and communities to grow and thrive,” said Bradley.

“I want to thank the U.S. Chamber of Commerce for this recognition and for bringing the Free Enterprise Express here to Glen Cove,” said Suozzi. I’ve always believed that the best way to grow our economy is to give people the opportunity to work hard, build something, create jobs, and succeed. Companies like Standard Bots are doing exactly that right here on Long Island. We need to work together — Democrats and Republicans — to bring down costs, support our small and growing businesses, and create an environment where American innovation can thrive. That’s how we grow our economy, create opportunity, and keep the American Dream alive for the next generation.”

The event was held at Standard Bots, a growing Glen Cove company that designs and assembles industrial robotic arms in the United States. The company provided a local example of the entrepreneurship, innovation, and job creation the Chamber’s nationwide tour is seeking to highlight.

“We’re proud to welcome Congressman Suozzi and the U.S. Chamber’s Free Enterprise Express to Standard Bots here in Glen Cove,” said Evan Beard, Co-Founder and CEO of Standard Bots. “We believe America can and should lead the world in advanced manufacturing and robotics. By encouraging innovation, investment, and entrepreneurship, we can build many more things in America, create good jobs, and compete globally.”

The Chamber also cited Suozzi’s leadership of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, his five-point affordability plan, his leadership on the Promise to America, and his efforts to advance bipartisan immigration reform.

The Free Enterprise Express Opportunity Tour is traveling across the country for six weeks, visiting 20 states and holding more than 50 events highlighting local businesses, employers, workers, and community leaders. The tour is designed to showcase the role of entrepreneurship, innovation, competition, and economic growth in creating jobs and opportunity.

The tour is part of the U.S. Chamber’s New Fight for Free Enterprise, a multi-year initiative to promote free enterprise and highlight businesses and entrepreneurs in communities across the country.

###
title: Suozzi Recognized as First Democratic Member of Congress To Be Awarded U.S. Chamber’s “Advocate for American Business” Award

Projects will test next-generation geothermal technologies and explore promising resources to support affordable, reliable, secure American energy
September 21, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced more than $99 million for 21 projects selected to advance geothermal energy development across the United States. The projects will conduct field-scale tests of next-generation geothermal technologies and exploration drilling to characterize and potentially confirm promising geothermal resources.
Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the Energy Department is advancing American geothermal innovation to unlock the nation’s abundant domestic energy resources. Geothermal can provide reliable, around-the-clock power to help meet growing demand while strengthening U.S. energy security.
“These projects will empower American innovators to unlock the tremendous geothermal resources beneath our feet,” said DOE Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we’re advancing next-generation geothermal technologies that can lower costs, strengthen American energy dominance, and turn more of our vast domestic geothermal resources into reliable and affordable power.”
The 21 projects will advance geothermal development in two key areas. Five projects will conduct field-scale enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) tests to validate technologies under real-world conditions, while 16 additional projects will conduct exploration drilling to identify and characterize promising next-generation geothermal resources. Together, these efforts will help reduce technical and development risk and provide the information needed to support future commercial projects and investment.
Data generated by these projects will be publicly available through DOE’s Geothermal Data Repository (GDR), giving industry, researchers, and other stakeholders access to information from the field tests and geothermal exploration activities. Making these data available can extend the value of the projects beyond individual sites by helping inform future technology development and geothermal exploration across the industry.
Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment by DOE to issue an award or provide funding. Before funding is issued, DOE and the applicants will undergo a negotiation process, and DOE may cancel negotiations and rescind the selection for any reason during that time.
title: Energy Department Announces $99 Million for 21 Projects to Advance U.S. Geothermal Energy Development

Two Granddaughters, Two Tattoos

Today, Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) announced she received another tattoo to mark her granddaughter Sadie’s 18th birthday:

“One tattoo was a story – two is now tradition, and one I am so happy to carry on to show my love for my grandchildren. After my first tattoo for my granddaughter Rigby’s 18th birthday, my granddaughter Sadie asked that I get another for hers. I said absolutely. When Sadie was a baby, she'd lift her head like a little bird coming out of a nest, my le petit oiseau, French for little bird. That is why my new tattoo is a swallow.”

Joe Capobianco, owner of Hope Tattoo Gallery in New Haven, gave DeLauro the new ink. DeLauro received her first tattoo in 2023 with her granddaughter Rigby. “I am thankful to Joe and Hope Tattoo Gallery for a beautiful new piece of body art,” DeLauro said.

“People keep asking me if there will be more tattoos to come. I have more grandchildren, so the answer is probably yes. And every one of them will be worth it.”

text:
Transcript of Ranking Member Ro Khanna’s Remarks at Asia Society on U.S.-China AI Agreement Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
NEW YORK – Today, Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, delivered remarks outlining his vision for the future of U.S. strategy toward China, including U.S.-China safeguards to prevent the loss of human control of AI, American economic competitiveness, effective deterrence, and the role of diplomacy in managing strategic competition.
Khanna delivered the remarks at Asia Society in New York on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, as leaders from around the world gather to address shared global challenges and the future of international cooperation. His remarks also addressed the need for economic rebalancing and moral leadership in diplomacy and development around the world.
Following his remarks, Ranking Member Khanna joined the Hon. Dr. Kevin Rudd AC, Global President and CEO of Asia Society and the 26th Prime Minister of Australia, for a fireside conversation on how the United States and China can manage sustained strategic competition, reduce the risks of conflict, identify areas of practical cooperation, and navigate their respective roles in an increasingly competitive and multipolar international environment.
A full transcript of Ranking Member Khanna’s remarks is below.
Over the last few months, we’ve seen shocking polls from some of our closest allies and partners around the world in terms of the trust they have in the United States versus China.
In Canada, our closest ally in the Western Hemisphere, 44 percent of Canadians view China favorably, up from just 14 percent three years ago. In contrast, only 33 percent have a favorable view of the United States, down from 57 percent in 2023.
Germany is hemorrhaging ten thousand manufacturing jobs per month in large part because its industry is getting crushed by heavily subsidized Chinese imports. And yet, 33 percent of Germans view China favorably, compared to just 27 percent who have a positive view of America.
In Italy, Prime Minister Meloni once fancied herself a friend of President Trump, but today 51 percent of Italians view China favorably, compared to 31 percent for the U.S.
In the UK, with whom America has had a “special relationship” since at least the days of Winston Churchill, 46 percent of Brits have a favorable view of China versus only 41 percent who are favorable toward the United States.
These numbers are even worse across much of the Global South, including in many countries in South and Southeast Asia that are frequent targets of China’s bullying, but are now being bullied even more by our own country.
Because of this bullying, the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, recently suggested making Canada the EU’s first “associate member.” Leaders across Europe are planning for a post-American world because they don’t trust the American electorate to not vote for another Trump-like leader in the future.
During Donald Trump’s first term, around 2017, Xi Jinping started describing the world order as going through what he called “great changes unseen in a century.”
He was referring to the political turmoil in the United States and many other democracies that led to “Brexit” in 2015 and to Donald Trump’s first election in 2016. He was also referring to China’s own extraordinary rise in economic and military power.
The world is experiencing changes unlike any we have seen in a very long time, perhaps in the lifetimes of any of us here in this room.
So, what has changed?
Americans have made clear that we reject the unfettered globalization that deindustrialized our country and hollowed out once-thriving communities like Johnstown, PA and Middletown, OH. I saw Fairless Works shut down where I grew up in Bucks County.
Deindustrialization and economic dislocation have rippled across much of the world. Populist anger contributed to Brexit and the electoral success of far-right parties across Europe from France and Germany to Austria and Croatia.
Almost one in four Europeans now vote for far-right parties, almost five times more than the proportion in the mid-1990s.
In the United States, we are trying to do something historically unprecedented in becoming the first cohesive multiracial democracy in the world. We have the highest foreign-born percentage of our population in America since 1924, and no nation comes close to our diversity with our African-American, Latino, Asian, and Native American populations.
China is the polar opposite in its campaign of forced and often brutal assimilation of its Tibetan, Uyghur, Southern Mongolian, and other non-Han communities, including through its so-called “Ethnic Unity Law.”
And finally, the AI revolution is transforming our economy, creating unprecedented wealth but also creating real risks for society in the loss of control, misalignment, the loss of jobs and staggering wealth inequality.
The safety risks are so severe that the founders of three major American AI companies recently called for “pacing the frontier” to make sure that the rate of advancement in AI doesn’t outpace humanity’s ability to control it. I’ve called on the major Chinese labs to make the same pledge.
So, the question now is, what comes next?
Will China lead the world, or will America lead it?
We live in a time devoid of statesmanship.
Ironically, the only American providing global leadership these days is Pope Leo, who I went to see this summer and who has written a marvelous treaty on AI, Magnifica Humanitas. Last month, I wrote letters to American AI companies asking them to commit to its principles.
I want America to be a moral leader in the world again.
But to do this, we need a new generation offering a new doctrine for American foreign policy.
First, a new generation must make clear that we renounce and categorically reject the doctrine of “might makes right,” which President Trump has recklessly applied to his Iran war and in the Caribbean.
Instead, America must lead and be a friend to the world, standing up for freedom and human rights.
We should remember President Kennedy’s famous words from his address to the nation during the Cuban Missile Crisis, where he reminded Americans that:
“Our goal is not the victory of might, but the vindication of right […] here in this Hemisphere, and, we hope, around the world.”
A generation earlier, FDR announced his “good neighbor” policy in his first inaugural address, where he pledged America to “the policy of the good neighbor—the neighbor who resolutely respects himself and, because he does so, respects the rights of others.”
We can even go back to the Founding Fathers themselves, like Thomas Jefferson, who called for “peace, commerce, and honest friendship with all nations” to be one of the essential principles of American governance.
These principles must be cornerstones of our foreign policy once again. We must restore our alliances with nations working to become pluralistic democracies and work with them in good faith to advance human and economic rights and democracy around the world.
This includes ending our hypocrisy and supporting self-determination for the Palestinians living side-by-side with a secure Israel as the Arab Peace Plan has long called for.
We must not take a hectoring tone. Instead, we must work diplomatically, including with NGOs, to stand up for the universal truths that are enshrined in the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
And like President Kennedy, we should not mistake rejecting the principle of “might makes right” for neglecting the importance of might itself.
We must ensure that America retains naval and air superiority in the Pacific to counterbalance China’s rapid build-up of military power.
We must invest in attritable drones and autonomous vehicles to make sure that our military can prevail on the battlefield of the future, and does not just keep fighting yesterday’s wars.
This brings me to the second principle for a new foreign policy doctrine, which is that we need an America that uses its power to help solve the world’s problems, not to militarily threaten and bully other countries.
When the world thinks of us, they shouldn’t think of the size of our military or the destructive power of our bombs. Instead, they should think of America as a peacemaker and leader who can convene others to resolve humanity’s biggest issues.
We should lead in addressing the climate crisis, global poverty, ending war, and illiteracy.
But today, let’s start with AI.
We can begin by showing American leadership on the issue of AI safety.
Winning an AI war is like winning a nuclear war. It is catastrophic for civilization.
America’s AI labs might be winning today, but nobody wins if humans lose control of AI or if bad actors use AI to unleash a chemical or biological attack.
We must lead the way by showing the world what responsible AI regulation looks like. This starts by establishing a federal AI Safety Agency and imposing strict liability on labs that fail to follow the rules or unleash catastrophic harm.
Rule Number One must be a ban on recursive self-improvement. This is when AI develops AI— and it is the clearest path to humans losing control of this technology.
Rule Number Two is mandatory certifications and inspections to prevent misuse and misalignment.
Once we’ve led the way at home, we need the world to follow. Our President should pursue a binding agreement with China to keep humans in control, which must be enforceable and verifiable.
The third principle for a new foreign policy is to build a fresh economic vision for the world that replaces corporate-dominated globalization. We must build the economy of the future for every American in every place, not just for a few billionaires.
This starts with what I call a New Economic Patriotism.
After World War II, European industry lay devastated by half a decade of total war. Public discontent was rising, which American leaders feared would lead to radical and destabilizing ideologies.
In response, the Marshall Plan helped rebuild Europe’s economy and shore up public support for capitalism and democracy.
Today, American industry lies devastated by five decades of offshoring and financial engineering by private equity. Populist anger is rising at the elites who chased low wages overseas and shut down factories to maximize shareholder value.
We need a Marshall Plan for America to achieve economic renewal across our nation, with high-paying industrial and service jobs in every community.
Rebuilding our economy at home is not isolationism. It promotes economic and national security and helps overcome the anger so many Americans feel about deindustrialization.
We can combine this strategy with policies that help other nations, especially in Latin America and the Global South, to develop their own economies in ways that don’t compete with our jobs.
The Development Finance Corporation and USAID can and should support this effort in developing nations.These countries in turn will be better markets for American exports. Our assistance can also help rebuild trust in places that have been courted by Chinese gifts and attention.
We would not do this in China’s way of seeking dominance and control. We would do it because we want to see the spread of free enterprise and democracy.
If we focus on rebuilding American factory towns and rural communities, and if we deliver on shared prosperity within our country, Americans will see that economic engagement with the world need not be zero sum.
Americans will support the economic development of other nations so long as we trust that it won’t lead to foreign goods being dumped back into our market or happen at the expense of our working class.
My final principle for a new American foreign policy is that at home, America must strive to become a cohesive multiracial nation, and in doing so, become a model for the world.
I have often spoken of my deep admiration for Frederick Douglass, whose 1867 speech “Composite Nation” ranks as one of the greatest in American history. In it, he calls on America to celebrate immigrants and become what he called a “composite nation”: taking the best from the ways of life of different people, from different parts of the world, and melding it into something beautiful here.
After fifteen years in bondage, he still believed that in the free air of America the best ideas of different traditions would emerge, and that we could become a shining pluralistic democracy with shared prosperity for all.
That is the America I see emerging after Donald Trump. It will be born if we build economic security and dignity for every American in every community.
To be Douglass’s composite nation, we must guarantee economic dignity in Johnstown and Middletown, in Downriver Detroit, in Milwaukee Orangeburg, Las Vegas; and Lordstown for Black, Latino, and white Americans alike.
Building a multiracial democracy will require the greatest economic mission in generations. An America that is economically resilient across geographies will be more likely to be an outward-facing, confident nation that once again leads the free world.
I want an America that rejects Donald Trump’s philosophy, which preys on our worst fears to divide us, and emulates dictators who build a world of domination and dependence.
I want an America that rediscovers the decency, the positive outlook, and the can-do pragmatism our Founders brought into the world 250 years ago.
Those capacities are still in us. We simply have to make sure this nation is not enriching a few, but working for the people I grew up with in Pennsylvania and working for all Americans.
If we provide economic opportunity everywhere, we can become the world’s first cohesive multiracial democracy, a nation that carries the freedom struggles of every corner of the earth, and is a moral light to the aspirations of free people.
This is our duty and our calling.
Thank you.
###
title: Transcript of Ranking Member Ro Khanna’s Remarks at Asia Society on U.S.-China AI Agreement Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting

EPA Advances Cosmo Specialty Fibers Cleanup Work, Continues Treatment Operations
SEATTLE— U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s time-critical removal action at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site in Cosmopolis, Washington, has reached multiple milestones over the past two weeks, including the completion and commissioning of a chemical treatment plant designed to neutralize corrosive waste before it is shipped for disposal. To date, over 222,000 gallons of acidic waste have been treated, and over 180,000 gallons have been shipped off-site. EPA anticipates removing over 1 million gallons of waste from the site.
“The Trump EPA remains firmly committed to advancing this removal action safely while keeping the local community informed as work continues at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site,” said EPA Regional Administrator Emma Pokon. “This effort shows our commitment to clean air, land, and water, and to a safe, transparent cleanup process for all Americans.”
EPA began site mobilization in early August, coordinating with local fire, law enforcement, emergency management, and environmental health officials. The removal action is a proactive measure intended to safely eliminate potential environmental hazards and reduce future risk to the surrounding community. EPA’s work at the site is expected to be completed this calendar year.
“We are making steady progress at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site, and the treatment system is now fully operational,” said EPA On-Scene Coordinator Thomas Vroman. “By treating waste on site before shipment, we are improving safety and lowering disposal costs.”
For the past two years, EPA and Washington State Department of Ecology have worked closely to assess conditions at the non-operational facility and identify actions needed to reduce potential risks to the community and the environment. In April 2026, the Department of Ecology, the long-term lead agency for the site, requested EPA assistance with the removal of the remaining chemicals in tanks and containers.
For additional information, visit:
- Cosmo Specialty Fibers Time Critical Removal Action
- EPA's Removal Action Memorandum (pdf) - June 2, 2026
Members of the public with questions regarding the cleanup effort are encouraged to contact the EPA Region 10 Press Team at R10_Press_Team@epa.gov.
title: EPA Advances Cosmo Specialty Fibers Cleanup Work, Continues Treatment Operations

text:
Press Statement

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

September 21, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Malta as you celebrate the anniversary of your independence.

The U.S.-Malta partnership continues to deliver meaningful results. This year Malta became the 65th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, expanding our cooperation in space exploration. Bilateral trade reached $2.6 billion in 2025, as American companies continue to find opportunities in Malta. Our countries have also strengthened security cooperation through Malta’s entry into the Registry Information Sharing Compact, an important tool for maritime security and countering sanctions evasion.

Our growing ties in education and culture, including advanced cultural and professional exchanges, new Fulbright research partnerships, and expanded university cooperation, further strengthen the connections between our people. The United States looks forward to expanding practical cooperation that advances the security and prosperity of both the American and Maltese people.

Above: Gottheimer and Lawler discuss their bipartisan AI legislation.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Mike Lawler (NY-17) held a press conference to amplify the importance of their bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act, legislation that would establish clear, practical guardrails for the powerful new AI “agents” now operating inside America’s networks. This commonsense legislation ensures that businesses and agencies have the ability to see and stop rogue agents before they cause real damage. The Representatives also highlighted several other bipartisan actions they’ve led this Congress on AI — including legislation to protect consumers, develop America’s workforce, and boost innovation.

Watch Gottheimer and Lawler’s remarks here.

“You can’t drive a car in this country without a license plate, without insurance, without some way for a cop — or the person you just rear-ended — to know who’s behind the wheel and who’s responsible,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy. “AI agents right now don’t have any of that. Our bill puts a driver’s license on every AI agent operating in this country — so organizations can find every agent on their network, verify who built it, watch it in real time, and cut off its access the second something looks wrong. That means putting humans back in the driver’s seat. It’s time for Congress to get back to work and get this done.”

“This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation. It is about making sure we can safely deploy AI. A pause is not a safeguard. Some states have put a moratorium on the infrastructure that powers this technology. That does not invent a kill switch. It does not inventory the agents already on a hospital network or a utility system,” said Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17.) “If the United States taps the brakes while others floor it, we do not get safer AI. We get someone else’s AI. We are not going to regulate ourselves into second place.”

Right now, most organizations have no reliable way to know how many unauthorized AI agents are running in their systems, who built them, or what they have access to. AI agents can be activated by employees, embedded in third-party software, or deployed by vendors — often with little to no visibility for the organization whose networks they’re operating on to know that they are there. That blind spot is becoming more dangerous by the day. The recent Hugging Face incident and other autonomous cyberattacks have shown AI systems are being used to hack organizations at scale, without a person ever watching or stepping in.

Drafted and introduced by Gottheimer and Lawler, the Stop Rogue AI Act would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop national standards, guidelines, and best practices for discovering, verifying, monitoring, and controlling AI agents.

Other Bipartisan AI Initiatives from Gottheimer and Lawler include:

AI Workforce Training Act (H.R. 7576) — Helps workers upgrade their AI skills without leaving their jobs. More than 60% of small businesses now use AI — double the share from 2023 — and the challenge isn’t that AI is replacing workers, it’s that workers need help keeping up with the tools their employers are already using. The bill provides a 30% tax credit, capped at $2,500 per employee, for training in practical AI skills. The goal: help workers adapt to AI, not get replaced by it.

Advancing American Quantum Leadership Act of 2026 (H.R. 9585) — Expands the definition of “quantum” under the Export-Import Bank’s China and Transformational Exports Program, broadening “quantum computing” to “quantum information science and technology.”

No Rigged Grocery Prices Act (H.R. 8895) — Bans grocery stores and delivery apps from using AI-driven personal data to charge different customers different prices for the exact same item.

The two members have also pressed the administration and industry on AI accountability — urging the Federal Trade Commission to protect anti-discrimination measures for AI systems; calling on the CEOs of leading AI companies to ensure voters get accurate, unbiased information ahead of the 2026 midterms; and urging DHS, DOJ, CISA, and the FEC to coordinate against AI-related threats to the 2026 elections.

Below: Gottheimer and Lawler discuss their AI legislation.
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer, Lawler Push Bipartisan Plan on AI Safety

EPA Begins Lead Cleanup at Former Friction Materials Site in Huntington, Indiana
CHICAGO (September 21, 2026) – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) began a cleanup of lead-contaminated soil from the former Friction Materials site at 1849 East Sabine St. in Huntington, Indiana. The cleanup is expected to take approximately 60 days.
During the cleanup, EPA will secure the site and excavate lead-contaminated soil before backfilling with clean soil. Crews will transport lead-contaminated soil offsite for disposal at an EPA-approved facility. EPA will conduct air monitoring throughout the cleanup to ensure dust does not leave the site.
The 11.7-acre former Friction Materials site contains the remnants of a large automotive parts manufacturing facility. Operations at the site began in the early 1900s and continued for nearly a century. The site’s ownership changed hands several times before Friction Materials acquired the property in the late 1960s. The company used the site to manufacture automotive brake parts until ceasing all operations and declaring bankruptcy in 2000. The site sat vacant for more than a decade before the City of Huntington acquired the property via tax lien in 2014.
EPA has previously conducted two cleanups at the site:
- In 2017 and 2018, EPA removed and disposed of approximately 2,000 gallons of hazardous liquid waste and approximately 3,000 pounds of hazardous solid waste from the site, including asbestos-containing material.
- In 2022 and 2023, EPA removed more than 2,350 tons of lead-contaminated soil from 11 residential properties surrounding the site and some of the most highly contaminated areas onsite.
In 2025, an assessment by the Indiana Brownfields Program discovered additional lead contamination present in deeper soil throughout the site. The state referred the site to EPA for further assessment and removal. Earlier this year, EPA sampling confirmed the program’s findings.
For more information about the response, visit the Friction Materials removal website.
###

title: EPA Begins Lead Cleanup at Former Friction Materials Site in Huntington, Indiana

Washington, D.C.—Congressmen Vicente Gonzalez (D-TX-34) and Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-02) announced the introduction of the bipartisan H.R. 10434, the Empower Energy Exporting Communities Act. This legislation would establish an Oil & Gas Community Trust Fund to support infrastructure and public services in communities near major oil and gas export ports, without creating a new tax. South Texas is home to several major energy export hubs, including the Port of Corpus Christi and the Port of Brownsville.

“South Texas serves as a crucial gateway for the distribution of oil and gas exports to international markets,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “It is only right that our region directly benefits from the operations it supports. The establishment of a trust fund would not burden taxpaying Americans but instead reinvest already existing revenue from oil and gas companies to advance South Texas’s infrastructure of opportunity from our roads, bridges, and clean drinking water to public education and much more.”

"This bill ensures that a portion of the federal revenue already generated by the oil and gas industry is reinvested in the roads, ports, water systems, and other critical infrastructure these communities rely on, all without raising taxes," said Congressman Crenshaw. "I’m proud to join Congressman Gonzalez in supporting the Texas communities that help make America an energy superpower."

Specifically, Congressman Gonzalez’s bill would direct the Oil & Gas Community Trust Fund to be financed by 3% of corporate income tax revenues received from oil & gas companies. These funds would be used to make payments to eligible communities, including counties, parishes, municipalities, or Tribal communities located within 50 miles of a major port of export. The funds can only be used for infrastructure and public service investments, and payments cannot exceed the proportion of total trust fund dollars that matches its share of national exports.
title: Congressmen Gonzalez, Crenshaw Introduce Bipartisan Empower Energy Exporting Communities Act

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) announced that two of his bipartisan bills with Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (IN-09) passed out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee. The bills are as follows:

H.R. 7294, AI for Secure Networks Act (Menendez and Pfluger)

The AI For Secure Networks Act strengthens the cybersecurity of America’s communications networks by promoting the responsible use of artificial intelligence while addressing the risks posed by its misuse.

“As our communications networks face growing threats, we must advance forward thinking solutions to protect the communications, emergency services, critical infrastructure, and financial systems Americans depend on,” said Congressman Menendez. “Our legislation promotes the responsible use of AI while confronting the growing risks posed by its exploitation, including the potential for more sophisticated cyberattacks on the communications systems Americans rely on every day. I look forward to working to pass this legislation and strengthen protections for our networks and the people who depend on them.”

Click here to view Congressman Menendez’s remarks.

H.R. 5967, Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act (Menendez and Houchin)

The Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act establishes a federal task force to develop a national scam prevention strategy that strengthens support for victims, provides local law enforcement stronger tools to stop scams, and lowers the risk of financial losses from fraudulent activity.

“As scams become increasingly more sophisticated, we need a national strategy to protect American families and consumers,” said Congressman Menendez. “The Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act brings together the federal government, law enforcement, and corporations to protect our families and seniors from being targeted by bad actors online and over the phone. I am proud that our legislation has passed the full Committee and is one step closer to becoming law and look forward to its passage through the House.”

Click here to view Congressman Menendez’s remarks.

WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement after an activist court in California ordered an illegal alien and MS-13 gang member to be released from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody.

David Eduardo Mejia-Martinez
On March 9, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California issued a temporary restraining order and a no-transfer order after Mejia-Martinez filed a petition for a writ of habeas corpus. On April 30, a Department of Justice (DOJ) Immigration Judge denied Mejia-Martinez’s request for release on bond, labeling him as a flight risk and a danger to the community. Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who serves as co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Artificial Intelligence (AI) Caucus and represents a Northern Virginia district that includes Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA) in the U.S. House, issued the following statement today on the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) deployment of an AI Strategic Management of Airspace Routing Trajectories (“SMART”) system to manage flights at Washington area airports including DCA:

“The FAA should not use my constituents as guinea pigs for an unproven AI air traffic control system. The safety of the 24 million people traveling through DCA each year must be the top priority. Residents of this region are still uncertain about air safety after last year’s fatal accident, and the Administration did shockingly little to educate the traveling public about this development before implementing it in one of the most complex airspaces in the world.

“Unfortunately, I was informed today that air traffic controllers were not consulted on the ‘SMART’ system’s design and development, and were not trained on using it prior to the system’s adoption at local airports. I was further informed that the air traffic controllers have been told the ‘SMART’ system can adjust schedules and potentially even routes. Despite outward appearances, the airlines reportedly were privately ‘panicking’ about the hasty implementation of this system. I do not know why the Administration felt the need to race it into use, but it is unacceptable to use AI as a substitute for rebuilding the human-directed air traffic controller workforce.

“Dangerously rushing a system that holds Americans’ lives in its hands is not a good use case for artificial intelligence. I call on the FAA to immediately suspend its operation, at the very least until it is clearly established beyond doubt via air traffic controller feedback and independently verified stress testing that the technology is safe.”
title: Beyer Calls For Suspension Of AI System Deployed By FAA At Washington Area Airports

Legislation would establish ambitious energy standard to rapidly reduce emissions and achieve up to 100% renewable energy generation by 2046

WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09) joined U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) and U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in reintroducing the bicameral American Renewable Energy Act (AREA), legislation to establish an ambitious 70% renewable energy resource standard by 2036 to drastically reduce emissions, decrease pollution, and promote community resilience. To achieve this goal, AREA prioritizes the development and implementation of solar, wind, and geothermal energy, as well as marine energy, limited hydropower, and methane digesters for smaller farms and wastewater plants.

The bill also seeks to ensure the equitable distribution of economic, health, and resiliency benefits of renewable energy deployment by establishing an enforcement mechanism that requires at least 50% of collected funds be spent on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and storage projects in impacted communities.

“As we witness the devastating impacts of climate change on communities across our nation, we can no longer afford the luxury of inaction. The choices we make today will determine the world we leave to our children and grandchildren. We have the tools, the technology, and the knowledge to build a cleaner future; we need Congress to act,” said Rep. Clarke. “Investing in renewable energy also means confronting the environmental injustices that have left our nation’s most underserved communities bearing the greatest burden. My legislation puts clean energy technology and innovation to work, reducing emissions, improving air quality and health outcomes, and creating millions of good-paying renewable energy jobs. We cannot leave future generations to pay the price for problems we have the power to solve today.”

“Taking immediate, ambitious action to reduce emissions and build a clean energy future is essential to combating the climate crisis. Now is the time to enact a national renewable energy standard. Vermont has long led the nation in the clean energy transition, passing historic legislation just this summer that puts us on the path to achieve 100% renewable electricity by 2046,” said Senator Welch. “This bill will help the country follow in Vermont’s footsteps to speed the transition to renewables and build energy independence.”

“As Americans face skyrocketing electricity bills and the increasingly harmful impacts of the climate crisis, unleashing the power of clean energy has never been more important. This legislation will help us accelerate bringing cleaner options for consumers online while reducing emissions, lowering our dependence on fossil fuels and volatile global markets, creating new jobs, and cutting costs for working Americans. This is a key step in our fight towards a cleaner, healthier, and more affordable energy future,” said Senator Van Hollen.

AREA would require retail electricity suppliers to achieve at least 20% renewable energy generation in 2027, with an increase to 70% by 2036, and up to 100% by 2046. The bill would also require retail electricity suppliers to strengthen energy resilience by contributing an increasing share of their generation through distributed renewable energy, such as rooftop solar, starting with 15% in 2027, with an increase to 20% deployment requirement after five years.

Additionally, AREA also stipulates that electricity suppliers must meet their requirements by submitting renewable energy credits or paying an alternative compliance payment that begins at $50/megawatts per hour (MWh) and increases with inflation. Compliance with the bill would be facilitated by the creation of six regional credit trading markets to track retail electricity suppliers’ transition to renewable energy and ensure the benefits of renewable energy development are spread across the country.

Further, AREA seeks to ensure the equitable distribution of economic, health, and resiliency benefits and investments created by renewable energy deployment by establishing an enforcement mechanism that requires at least 50% of collected funds to be spent on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and storage projects in impacted communities. The legislation would also require utilities to produce 20% of their energy generation from renewables in impacted communities, reducing the need for polluting fossil fuel power plants in historically marginalized areas.

The American Renewable Energy Act is endorsed by the Chesapeake Climate Action Network; Evergreen Action; Sierra Club; Indivisible; and Vote Solar.

“The American Renewable Energy Act (AREA) is a major step toward building an electric grid that is cleaner, more affordable, and more just. By setting a strong national renewable electricity standard while ensuring that the benefits of the clean energy transition reach frontline and impacted communities, AREA will help reduce harmful pollution, create good-paying jobs, and protect families from the rising costs of fossil fuels. Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) Action Fund proudly supports AREA and urges Congress to move this bill forward to deliver the clean energy future that American families across the country deserve,” said Quentin Scott, Federal Policy Director, CCAN Action Fund.

“Shifting to renewable energy is no longer just an option, it is the necessary next step for the United States to meet the urgency of the climate crisis. The American Renewable Energy Act is the bold legislation we need to meet rising electricity demand, while improving public health, reducing American reliance on fossil fuels, and creating new jobs to supercharge our clean energy economy,” said Lena Moffitt, Executive Director, Evergreen Action. “The transition to clean energy is well underway and the federal government must be a leader in ensuring Americans benefit from the lower energy costs and cleaner air that renewable energy can deliver.”

“In the last year, electricity cost increases rapidly outpaced the rate of inflation while toxic and deadly emissions from coal plants spiked significantly,” said Patrick Drupp, ClimatePolicy Director, Sierra Club. “It is more urgent than ever that we invest in affordable, reliable, and clean energy to relieve families from soaring bills and protect our communities from more deadly pollution. Despite Donald Trump’s persistent attacks on clean energy, it is evident that Americans want more clean energy because of how much cleaner, cheaper, and faster it is. We applaud Senator Peter Welch for his work as a steadfast champion of the American Renewable Energy Act and look forward to working together more in the future.”

“A strong federal renewable energy standard establishes a clear national floor for clean energy while preserving states’ ability to pursue even more ambitious policies,” said Nathan Phelps, Managing Director, Vote Solar. “This legislation provides the certainty needed to accelerate investment in affordable, reliable clean energy, expanding access to solar and the benefits of the clean energy transition. By complementing state renewable energy standards, a federal RPS ensures that communities across the country can benefit from lower energy costs, cleaner air, and a stronger economy.”

Learn more about the American Renewable Energy Act of 2026.

Read the full bill text here.

Washington, D.C.–Today, Congresswomen Deborah Ross (NC-02) and Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Tropospheric Ozone Research Act of 2026 to fund multi-year scientific research on the warming effects of tropospheric ozone. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Brian Schatz (D-HI) introduced companion legislation in the Senate earlier this year.

Unlike the ozone layer that protects the Earth from UV radiation, tropospheric ozone is a major air pollutant and potent greenhouse gas found near the surface of the Earth. It causes an estimated 500,000 premature deaths and up to 26 percent losses in crop yields globally each year. Tropospheric ozone is also the third-largest driver of climate change after carbon dioxide and methane.

Because tropospheric ozone lasts only weeks in the atmosphere, cutting tropospheric ozone could significantly reduce temperatures in the near term, alleviating the severity of climate change effects and reducing the risk of crossing climate tipping points.

The bill would fund a three-year, $10M per year scientific research program on the warming effects of tropospheric ozone. It would also direct EPA to publish a summary report identifying key findings, assessing the costs and benefits of mitigating tropospheric ozone precursors, and providing policy recommendations and future research needs.

The legislation is endorsed by the Clean Air Task Force and the Natural Resources Defense Council.

“For years, we have known that tropospheric ozone pollution is costing lives and driving climate change, but there is still so much we need to understand to effectively address it,” said Congresswoman Deborah Ross. “This bill will empower our scientific community to find solutions to reduce tropospheric ozone’s harmful effects and its contributions to global warming. We need research and information in order to act against super pollutants like tropospheric ozone so we can confront the growing climate crisis.”

"In the wake of continued cuts to climate research funding by the Trump administration, it is now more important than ever to support the efforts at scientific research institutions and universities to better understand the ozone so that municipalities, farmers, and legislatures alike can be better prepared for future events caused by climate change,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “I’m proud to co-lead the Tropospheric Ozone Research Act with Congresswoman Ross to improve scientific understanding of the tropospheric ozone’s warming impacts and inform future strategies to reduce global temperatures.”

“The Tropospheric Ozone Research Act of 2026 and its House companion bill would advance our understanding of ground-level ozone as a climate super pollutant, said Dr. Richie Kaur, Senior Superpollutant Reduction Advocate at NRDC. “Tropospheric ozone is an air pollutant and a fast-acting driver of warming that damages human health, food systems, and ecosystems, with disproportionate impacts on vulnerable communities. At the same time, it represents a great opportunity for near-term progress—where stronger science can inform practical policies that deliver rapid public health, ecosystem, and climate benefits. As the world overshoots 1.5 degrees of warming above pre-industrial levels, we need to examine every tool in the climate toolkit to bend the warming curve.”

“Tropospheric ozone pollution has been neglected by policymakers despite its contribution to roughly half a million premature deaths a year, billions of dollars in economic damages, and about a quarter degree of present-day warming," said Darin Schroeder, Methane Legal and Regulatory Director at Clean Air Task Force. "The research funded by this bill and its companion in the Senate would create the knowledge base to change that inaction. This scientific investment would improve our understanding of how tropospheric ozone moves through and affects our atmosphere, providing a firm foundation for the US to better develop and target the solutions to drive this harmful pollutant down.”

Bill text is available here.

title: Ross + Foushee Introduce Bill Advancing Science to Reduce Warming from Tropospheric Ozone, a Potent Air Pollutant and Greenhouse Gas

The Lowering Commuting Costs Act would create the first personal tax deduction of more than $4,000 a year for commuting costs

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) alongside Congressman Jeff Van Drew (R-NJ-02) and Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (R-NJ-07) introduced the bipartisan Lowering Commuting Costs Act to deliver relief from rising commuting costs for working Americans. This legislation would create a federal income tax deduction, more than $4,000 a year or $340 a month, for personal commuting expenses, including the cost of gas, public transit and tolls such as New York City’s congestion pricing.

“Hardworking Long Islanders are forced to pay skyrocketing costs just to get to work, making the cost of living crisis even worse,” said Rep. Gillen. “With the rising price of gas, LIRR fares and the NYC congestion tax, working families are left with no affordable way to get to their jobs. This bipartisan bill will help families save money as they commute to work and contribute to the economy by creating the first-ever tax credit for personal commuting expenses.”

“For millions of Americans, just getting to work every day is expensive,” said Rep. Van Drew. “Gas is expensive, tolls are expensive, and for a lot of families, those costs add up to thousands of dollars a year. If businesses can deduct the cost of doing business, working people should be able to deduct what it takes to get to and from their jobs. I am proud to join Congresswoman Gillen on this bill and give some of that money back to the people who earn it.”

"Commuting costs strain hardworking New Jerseyans' bottom lines," said Rep. Kean, Jr. "The Lowering Commuting Costs Act would create a new deduction for taxpayers to save thousands of dollars of costs incurred when commuting, whether on train fare, on congestion pricing tolls, and more. I am proud to co-lead this bill to help families keep more of their hard-earned money and reduce the monetary strain of daily commutes."

“New York City Firefighters are struggling with high costs as it is, on top of paying thousands a year just commuting to their stations to save lives,” said Bobby Eustace, President, Uniformed Firefighters Association. “Because they have to carry heavy gear to work every day, taking public transit to work isn't realistic. Rising gas prices and paying the daily congestion tax have been a massive financial burden. We really appreciate Congresswoman Gillen and her colleagues stepping up for our members and trying to make our daily commutes more affordable.”

The IRS currently allows taxpayers to deduct the business use of a car, including driving between work locations and running business errands, but it does not allow a federal income tax deduction for personal commuting expenses.

The Lowering Commuting Costs Act would help relieve rising commuting costs by establishing an above-the-line tax deduction of more than $4,000 a year ($340 a month) for commuting costs, including the cost of gas, public transit, parking and tolls such as New York City’s congestion pricing. The tax credit would also stack with pre-tax commuter “fringe” benefits afforded by employers.

Rep. Gillen has consistently advocated for policies that lower costs and provide tax relief for Long Island families. Since taking office, she has led efforts to restore the full State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction, including a measure to eliminate the SALT cap. She also introduced bipartisan legislation to lower Long Islanders’ taxes by adjusting their federal tax brackets to reflect the local cost of living. Rep. Gillen also recently led bipartisan legislation to help lower car insurance rates by cracking down on staged “crash for cash” schemes.

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

Today, the Department of State is taking steps to impose visa restrictions on 32 individuals responsible for or complicit in defrauding Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled crime, and related activity. The majority of the individuals targeted today are affiliated with the Prince Group, a transnational criminal organization (TCO) that has been the subject of multiple U.S. sanctions actions for its role in defrauding Americans. Any valid visas held by these individuals have been revoked. This action is taken under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Every year, cybercriminals scam Americans out of tens of billions of dollars. In 2025 alone, TCOs in Southeast Asia, like the Prince Group, defrauded Americans out of at least $18.2 billion through cyber-enabled scams. The Department of the Treasury has also acted against the Prince Group, sanctioning 146 members and affiliates in October 2025, followed by an additional 35 in June 2026.

The Trump Administration will use every available tool to protect Americans, dismantle criminal scam networks, and impose costs on those who enable them. Those complicit in devastating families and communities nationwide will be denied entry into the United States.

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

September 21, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America Japan, and Republic of Korea during the United Nations General Assembly.

Begin Text

Secretary of State of the United States of America Marco Rubio, Foreign Minister of Japan Motegi Toshimitsu, and Foreign Minister of the Republic of Korea Cho Hyun met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week in New York. They reaffirmed the U.S.-Japan-ROK joint statement of September 22, 2025, and underscored progress in trilateral cooperation that promotes peace, stability, and economic prosperity to realize a free and open Indo-Pacific, while upholding shared principles including the rule of law.

Addressing North Korea

The Secretary and the Foreign Ministers reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) and the prohibition on support for revenue generation for the DPRK’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs). They also reaffirmed that the path to dialogue remains open and called on the DPRK to resume dialogue, while continuing to make efforts to advance peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula.

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers welcomed the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team’s (MSMT) work on the DPRK’s UNSCR violations and evasions. They welcomed the Alert to Countries, Companies, and Other Entities Regarding North Korean IT Workers issued by like-minded countries, and progress addressing DPRK’s cyber threats including through the trilateral working group meeting in June.

They reiterated their commitment to the immediate resolution of the issues of abductees, detainees, and unrepatriated prisoners of war as well as the issue of separated families.

Enhancing Economic Security and Resilience

Standing firmly against economic coercion and non-market policies and practices (NMPPs) leading to harmful overcapacity and market distortion, including arbitrary export restrictions that disrupt supply chains, the Secretary and the Foreign Ministers resolved to maintain free and transparent trade and secure critical supply chains. To this end, they committed to enhance the trilateral Supply Chain Early Warning System and welcomed the launch of a new trilateral consultation on economic security.

They stressed the need to strengthen regional energy supply resilience, including by increasing oil stockpiles and promoting collaboration between producing and consuming countries. They welcomed regional initiatives such as Japan’s “POWERR Asia”, as well as the ROK’s efforts to enhance energy security through regional cooperation. They committed to a plan to implement the July 7 trilateral Memorandum of Cooperation to accelerate small modular reactor (SMR) deployments in other countries in a mutually beneficial manner and under the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation.

They resolved to cooperatively reinforce advanced-technology stacks and supply chain resilience and to promote and protect critical and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum technology, digital infrastructure, and biotechnology. They welcomed greater cooperation among their economies in the field of semiconductors, and they expressed interest in further promoting trilateral national laboratory cooperation. They welcomed the third annual Young Trilateral Leaders’ Summit held in Honolulu in August to foster security and innovation in AI and emerging technologies.

Strengthening Regional and Global Engagement

The United States reiterated its ironclad commitments to the defense of Japan and the ROK, backed by America’s unmatched military strength, including its nuclear capabilities, and reaffirmed its extended deterrence commitments to Japan and the ROK. The Secretary and Foreign Ministers emphasized their commitment to robust security cooperation.

They emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. The Secretary and Foreign Ministers encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-Strait issues and opposed any attempts to unilaterally change the status quo. They expressed support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in appropriate international organizations. They also underscored their support for preserving freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded lawful commerce, and other lawful uses of the sea for all nations in the Indo-Pacific and globally, in accordance with international law as reflected in the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

They welcomed a new trilateral cooperation with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) to disrupt organized crime, particularly scams centers in Southeast Asia which pose a threat to regional and international peace and security. They welcomed the launch of trilateral consultations on international disaster relief.

They committed to continuing their efforts to advance cooperation under the Trilateral Maritime Security and Law Enforcement Cooperation Framework to address the multifaceted challenges in the maritime domain and provide joint capacity building assistance to partners in the region. The Secretary and Foreign Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to continue trilateral cooperation through close intergovernmental communication on Arctic issues.

Advancing Trilateral Cooperation

The Secretary and the Foreign Ministers committed to strengthening regional and global engagement and to continuing trilateral meetings at all levels.

Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) joined Democratic Women’s Caucus Chair Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), DWC Whip Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), DWC Senate Liaison and Caregiving Task Force Co-Chair Debbie Dingell (MI-06), and Caregiving Task Force Co-Chairs Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) & Lateefah Simon (CA-12) in sending a letter to Health and Human Services (HHS) demanding HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. withdraw their proposed rule to gut 90% of Head Start Program Performance Standards (HSPPS) that would increase costs for families and eliminate educational resources women and families rely on. The letter was signed by 87 House Democrats.

For 60 years, Head Start has served over 40 million families and children with accessible social services, healthcare, and improved early learning standards. The program provides low-income children, children with disabilities, dual language learners, and children experiencing homelessness with the resources needed to succeed in school. Even after six decades, Head Start remains popular, with four in five Americans saying they’re in support of the program evidence that Trump’s efforts to gut it are out of step with what Americans want.

The proposed rule would diminish the quality of Head Start services and undermine its ability to develop evidence-based programs that improve education, health, nutrition, parental involvement, and social services forcing families to either lose these resources or turn to more expensive options elsewhere. Head Start could no longer connect families to jobs, education, and housing opportunities or effectively help children succeed in school.

In the letter, Members highlighted how the proposed rule would undermine Congressional authority and intent:

“The administration claims to be removing red tape and saving money. In reality, this proposed rule would override Congressional intent by removing standards that make Head Start the program that it is today and that Congress explicitly directed HHS to create based on research and consultation with experts.”

The Members also explained how the elimination of National Head Start Standards for education would be detrimental to the programs success:

“Rigorous research has found that Head Start generates substantial long-term economic benefits, including an estimated $1.86 in benefits for every dollar invested. That return depends on strong teachers, strong ratios, and strong services—qualified staff, appropriate classroom size and teacher to child ratios that support learning, developmental screening and follow-up, health and mental health services, family engagement and support services, and evidence-based early learning—not a patchwork of state requirements that would create different standards throughout the country.”

The Members also warned the proposed cuts would erode the safety and the quality of the program and possibly put students in danger:

“The proposed rule would eliminate Head Start’s specific federal requirement that children be supervised at all times, reduce mandatory annual staff training on preventing abuse and neglect, repeal the prohibition on corporal punishment, shaming, humiliation, and seclusion practices, and remove the timelines that ensure a child’s developmental, dental, and medical needs are actually screened and followed up on.”

Lastly, the Members explain how the cuts would roll back its strict student support systems that keep children in school:

“This proposed rule would strip Head Start’s ban on expelling children and its strict limits on suspension which is deeply concerning. These protections exist because preschoolers are already suspended and expelled at rates far above K-12 students. Additionally, disparities in suspension and expulsion are already significant for children of color, boys, and children with disabilities. Federal data show that children of color account for a disproportionate share of preschool suspensions, while children served under Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) make up 23 percent of enrollment but 74 percent of expulsions.7 Removing these federal protections will not close those gaps. It will widen them.”

Read the full letter here.

The letter was signed by: Amo, Gabe; Ansari, Yassamin; Balint, Becca; Barragán, Nanette; Beatty, Joyce; Bonamici, Suzanne; Brownley, Julia; Brown, Shontel; Budzinski, Nikki; Carbajal, Salud; Carson, André; Castor, Kathy; Chu, Judy; Clarke, Yvette; Craig, Angie; Crockett, Jasmine; Davids, Sharice; Dean, Madeleine; DeGette, Diana; DelBene, Suzan; Dexter, Maxine; Dingell, Debbie; Elfreth, Sarah; Escobar, Veronica; Foushee, Valerie; Frankel, Lois; Friedman, Laura; Garcia, Sylvia; Goodlander, Maggie; Grijalva, Adelita; Hayes, Jahana; Horsford, Steven; Houlahan, Chrissy; Hoyle, Val; Jacobs, Sara; Jayapal, Pramila; Johnson, Julie; Kamlager-Dove, Sydney; Kaptur, Marcy; Kelly, Robin; Lee, Summer; Leger Fernandez, Teresa; Matsui, Doris; McBath, Lucy; McBride, Sarah; McClain Delaney, April; McClellan, Jennifer; McCollum, Betty; McDonald Rivet, Kristen; McIver, LaMonica; Mejia, Analilia; Meng, Grace; Moore, Gwen; Moskowitz, Jared; Ocasio-Cortez, Alexandria; Omar, Ilhan; Pelosi, Nancy; Pettersen, Brittany; Pingree, Chellie; Pou, Nellie; Pressley, Ayanna; Ramirez, Delia; Randall, Emily; Rivas, Luz; Ross, Deborah; Salinas, Andrea; Scanlon, Mary Gay; Schakowsky, Janice; Scholten, Hillary; Schrier, Kim; Sewell, Terri; Simon, Lateefah; Stansbury, Melanie; Stevens, Haley; Strickland, Marilyn; Sykes, Emilia; Titus, Dina; Tlaib, Rashida; Tokuda, Jill; Torres, Norma; Trahan, Lori; Underwood, Lauren; Velázquez, Nydia; Wasserman Schultz, Debbie; Watson Coleman, Bonnie; Williams, Nikema; Wilson, Frederica

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05), Rep. Pablo Hernandez (PR), and Rep. Joe Wilson (SC-02) sent a congressional oversight letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, urging the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to expand colonoscopy access for individuals with a history of polyps as part of preventative screenings in Affordable Care Act (ACA) regulated health plans.

Members urged the HHS to issue new ACA FAQ guidance, stating that a follow-up surveillance colonoscopy is a “screening” and therefore part of the ACA preventive services benefit. Specifically, they suggest the following language to be included in the FAQ guidance:

If a follow-up, screening colonoscopy is scheduled and performed prior to the 10-year window, is it permissible for a plan or issuer to impose cost-sharing for the cost of the procedure and polyp removal during the colonoscopy?

Members wrote:

“Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in the United States and the country’s second leading cause of cancer mortality among women and men combined. However, colorectal cancer is unique in that it is largely preventable. Even when found and treated early, the five-year colorectal cancer survival rate is 90 percent; unfortunately, less than 40 percent of colorectal cancer cases are caught early.”

“According to data released earlier this year, colorectal cancer is now the leading cause of cancer deaths for Americans under 50 years old — a sobering reality which was not initially projected to occur until 2030. It is also expected to be the leading cause of cancer deaths for both men and women aged 20 to 49 by 2030.”

“Affordability and patient cost-sharing are demonstrated barriers to colorectal cancer screening. We must make a concerted effort to address this public health crisis and increase screening rates throughout the continuum of care. This includes patients with a personal history of polyps, but who are otherwise asymptomatic.”

“Based on clinical practice and guidance received from the U.S. Multi-Society Task Force (USMSTF) on Colorectal Cancer, a follow-up screening colonoscopy for asymptomatic patients with a personal history of polyps is an integral part of the continuum of care and should be considered a ‘screening.’ The USMSTF recommends that asymptomatic individuals undergoing screening colonoscopy require repeat screenings to evaluate for new polyps at specific intervals based on the findings of their screening exam, ranging from 1 year to 10 years. These procedures should be treated as preventive services and not subject to patient cost-sharing.”

“We hope that the Secretary will join us in this effort to save lives and thwart this public health crisis.”

This letter was co-signed by Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Rep. Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Rep. Hank Johnson (GA-04), Rep. Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Rep. Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Rep. Steve Cohen (TN-09), Rep. Haley Stevens (MI-11), Rep. John Mannion (NY-22), Rep. Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Rep. Bill Keating (MA-09), Rep. Seth Moulton (MA-06), Rep. Julia Brownley (CA-26), Rep. Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Rep. Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Rep. Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Rep. Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Rep. Kim Schrier (WA-08), and Rep. Don Davis (NC-06).

This letter was endorsed by American College of Gastroenterology, American Gastroenterological Association, American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE), Colon Cancer Coalition, Colorectal Cancer Alliance, Digestive Disease National Coalition, Fight CRC.
