text:
As the United States marks 25 years since September 11, U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) penned an essay recounting her experience on that day and how Americans united the weeks that followed.

"We had been attacked, and we pulled together. For a brief time, the things that divided us seemed smaller than the things that united us. We talked to each other. We listened. We comforted strangers. We checked on neighbors. We reached across differences of faith, race and background. We spent time trying to understand one another rather than turning away,” Congresswoman Dingell wrote. “The Jewish community worked hard to support the Muslim community. Communities reached across lines of faith and ethnicity. People who might never have spoken to one another before stood together. Bridges were built.”

Congresswoman Dingell continued: “Twenty-five years later, I look around our country and worry about how many of those bridges are gone or endangered. Antisemitism is real. Hatred and fear directed at Muslims are real. Racism is real. Political and religious hatred can turn quickly into threats, violence and tragedy. We should be worried ‒ not because America is weak, but because we know how quickly fear can divide us if we allow it to. America did not deserve 9/11. No country deserves terrorism, hatred or violence. And no American should be made to feel unsafe because of their faith, religion, race, ethnicity or heritage. As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we will remember the nearly 3,000 people who were killed, and the countless families whose lives were changed forever. We will remember the firefighters, police officers, first responders and ordinary citizens who showed extraordinary courage. But remembrance must be more than looking backward. We should also remember who we were in the days after.”

Congresswoman Dingell’s op-ed can be found HERE and text is below:

The day, Sept. 11, 2001, is seeded in my mind and soul forever.

I was on one of the few planes still flying that morning. We landed at National Airport around 8 a.m., before the first tower was hit. Then U.S.-Rep. David Camp was sitting next to me. Before we left Detroit, I turned to him and said, "I have the weirdest feeling. If you weren’t sitting next to me, I think I would get off this plane."

We had no idea what was about to happen. As we watched planes crash into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon was attacked, and reports came that another plane might be headed toward the Capitol. But none of us fully understood what we were witnessing.

My husband, John, was in the Capitol. When people were being told to leave, he refused. He said, “No one is going to chase me out of the symbol of our democracy. I fought in World War II, and I’m staying here.”

Friends working at the White House came to my General Motors Foundation office in downtown DC, terrified. Secret Service agents had told women in heels to take off their shoes and run. Everything we knew about safety and normal life seemed to disappear in a matter of hours. No one was able to fly home. A few days later, John and I drove back to Michigan with Ohio Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur. We were deeply worried about Dearborn, our hometown, and about the possibility of backlash and violence against our Muslim neighbors.

President George W. Bush addressed the nation at a Joint Session of Congress on Sept. 20, but we stayed in Dearborn because we believed that in a moment of fear, we had a responsibility to stand with our community and fight hatred wherever we saw it. Bill Ford and John Dingell hosted a candlelight vigil at the Henry Ford Museum. Thousands came. There was fear, and there was faith. There was grief, but there was also an extraordinary sense that we were going to stand together.

Then came the names. Friends who were lost. Sons and daughters of friends. One of John’s dearest friends. Firefighters and police officers who ran into burning buildings to save people and never came home. The grief was overwhelming.

But something else happened in those days that I will never forget: America came together.

It was one of the most horrific times in our nation’s history, and yet, in some ways, it was also one of the most special. We had been attacked, and we pulled together. For a brief time, the things that divided us seemed smaller than the things that united us. We talked to each other. We listened. We comforted strangers. We checked on neighbors. We reached across differences of faith, race and background. We spent time trying to understand one another rather than turning away. The Jewish community worked hard to support the Muslim community. Communities reached across lines of faith and ethnicity. People who might never have spoken to one another before stood together. Bridges were built.

Twenty-five years later, I look around our country and worry about how many of those bridges are gone or endangered. Antisemitism is real. Hatred and fear directed at Muslims are real. Racism is real. Political and religious hatred can turn quickly into threats, violence and tragedy. We should be worried ‒ not because America is weak, but because we know how quickly fear can divide us if we allow it to. America did not deserve 9/11. No country deserves terrorism, hatred or violence. And no American should be made to feel unsafe because of their faith, religion, race, ethnicity or heritage.

As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we will remember the nearly 3,000 people who were killed, and the countless families whose lives were changed forever. We will remember the firefighters, police officers, first responders and ordinary citizens who showed extraordinary courage. But remembrance must be more than looking backward. We should also remember who we were in the days after.

We were frightened, but we did not have to be consumed by fear. We were grieving, but we reached out to one another. We were attacked, but we did not have to turn our anger against innocent people in our own communities. We found strength in coming together. That is the lesson I hope we carry into the next 25 years.

We cannot change what happened on Sept. 11, 2001. We cannot bring back those we lost. But we can decide what their memory asks of us.
title: ICYMI: Dingell Marks 25th Anniversary of September 11

text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement today commemorating the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001:

“September 11, 2001, was a day of tragedy and created a new sense of vulnerability. But it also was followed by a unity of purpose and conviction that the terrorists would not prevail.

“I will never forget standing on the steps of the U.S. Capitol that evening, rallying with colleagues, staff, and fellow citizens who had gathered to show our solidarity with those who had lost loved ones, who were still searching for the missing, and who were working to restore safety. Moved by that moment, we began to sing 'God Bless America,' and soon everyone was joining in. It was a powerful expression of our unity and resolve. It was, too, a reminder that we are, despite our differences and the often-heated rhetoric in our politics, one nation with a common purpose and a shared hope for peace, justice, and the triumph of good over evil.

“The magnitude of this tragedy created great unity. But as it fades from memory, the realization of that unity becomes more difficult to sustain. We must nevertheless strive to recapture it.

“Ground Zero, the west side of the Pentagon, and the hallowed field in Shanksville are now quiet places of peace. Today, bells will be rung, names will be read, and hymns will be sung. But nothing we do today can honor the dead and injured more than to carry on tomorrow, as we have now done for a quarter century, and continue the difficult task of building the America that terrorists tried in vain to dismantle. An America united. An America filled with optimism in devotion its purpose. An America of big hearts and open arms. An America guided by its highest ideals and committed to ensuring equal justice and opportunity for all.

“Let us rededicate ourselves to seeking that unity of purpose today. May the memory of those lost on September 11, 2001, inspire us to that work now and forever.”
title: Hoyer Statement on 25th Anniversary of 9/11

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Rep. Grace Meng (D-NY) released the following statement on the Trump Administration’s latest attempt to include a citizenship question on the 2030 Census form:

“The Constitution requires congressional representation to be based on the ‘whole number of persons in each State’—not only citizens or green-card holders. Every person living in our country must be counted, regardless of citizenship or immigration status.

The Trump administration’s proposal would erase millions of people from the census data used to distribute political representation. It would exclude not only undocumented immigrants, but also refugees, asylum seekers, visa holders, and other people who are lawfully present in the United States but do not have permanent-resident status. This is un-American, unconstitutional, and a direct attack on immigrant communities.

An inaccurate count risks a decade of consequences. Census data help determine representation in Congress, electoral districts, and the allocation of federal resources for health care, education, infrastructure, and other essential services.

When Donald Trump tried to include a citizenship question on the 2020 Decennial Census form during his first term, I fought back and I won. Earlier this year, I co-led a letter with the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) and other Congressional leaders opposing changes to the Census test, which includes the citizenship question.

I’ve never stopped fighting to prevent this and I’m prepared to continue as the Top Democrat on the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies. My message is clear: immigrants are part of our communities, and they will not be rendered invisible. The 2030 Census must remain an accurate count of the people—not a political weapon.”

text:
Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

September 11, 2026

Fresh from his meetings with government partners at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau traveled to the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Solomon Islands, and Kiribati to advance the Trump Administration’s America First economic and security priorities across the Pacific.

The Deputy Secretary reaffirmed our commitment to the FSM in a bilateral meeting with FSM President Wesley Simina. The Deputy Secretary also surveyed the recovery efforts following Typhoon Sinlaku’s damage in Chuuk State where he announced the United States intends to provide over $100 million to support disaster relief and reconstruction in FSM, delivering on U.S. commitments under the Compact of Free Association.

In Solomon Islands, the Deputy Secretary emphasized the bonds forged during World War II and outlined a vision for mutual progress in a free and open Pacific. He paid his respects at Guadalcanal, Red Beach, and Bloody Ridge Memorials where Americans, Solomon Islanders, and other Allied forces sacrificed their lives to turn the tide of the war. The Deputy Secretary announced U.S. support through the Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation for the preservation of the Bloody Ridge battlefield as a site of perpetual remembrance and continuing education. Looking forward, he signed an agreement with Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade Rick Houenipwela for the Peace Corps to return to the Solomon Islands after a 26-year absence. At Honiara Airport, he concluded his visit by announcing that the U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, intends to provide four aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles to enhance the safety of American and international tourists. He also announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a condition assessment to determine the cost of rehabilitating the Solomon Islands Parliament.

In Kiribati, the Deputy Secretary attended the Kiribati Development Partners Forum on Kiritimati Island at the invitation of President Taneti Maamau to emphasize U.S. commitment to partnership with Kiribati on economic development in line with the Kiribati 20-Year Vision. The Deputy Secretary announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a study to update and expand the wharf on Kiritimati Island. This initiative will lay the foundation for a long-term infrastructure investment to increase access to trade and support maritime security and combatting illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing for the peoples of Kiritimati.

Throughout the visit, the Deputy Secretary reaffirmed the United States’ longstanding commitment to partnering with Pacific Island nations to expand economic and commercial opportunities, strengthen digital connectivity, combat transnational criminal activity, and safeguard global health security. Meeting with senior leaders in each country, he unveiled new initiatives to advance a free and open Pacific, expand opportunities for U.S. businesses, and deliver concrete economic results for the American taxpayer.

Tags

HSI confirmed that the suspect had illegally voted in the 2020 election
WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested an alien from the Bahamas with a criminal history that includes armed robbery, domestic violence, and assault on a police officer, and who had illegally voted in past elections.
On September 3, ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Atlanta arrested Anthony Tyrone Higgs, a criminal alien from the Bahamas, in Decatur, Georgia. He is currently in the custody of ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO).
Anthony Tyrone Higgs
Higgs’ criminal history includes convictions for TWO counts of possession of a weapon during a violent crime, TWO counts of grand larceny, armed robbery with a deadly weapon, criminal domestic violence, assault on a police officer, and resisting arrest. In addition to these crimes, HSI Atlanta confirmed via an investigation in August 2026 that Higgs had illegally voted in the 2020 election.
“This criminal alien from the Bahamas has a rap sheet for multiple violent crimes, including armed robbery, domestic violence, and assault on a police officer,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “On top of all of that, he illegally voted in the 2020 election. If even one non-citizen votes in our elections, it cancels out the vote of an American citizen. Thanks to the hard work of the men and women of ICE, this criminal will be removed from our country and can never interfere in our elections again.”
Higgs was admitted to the United States as a Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) in October 1976. DHS has placed him in removal proceedings to revoke his LPR status due to his crimes.
This is part of the Trump Administration’s broader focus on stopping non-citizens from voting in American elections. Recent examples include:
- In August, Carlos Felipe Jaramillo-Grajales, a criminal illegal alien from Colombia, was sentenced to three years in prison after an ICE investigation led to him pleading guilty to committing identity theft to illegally vote in elections for more than 20 years.
- In July, HSI arrested Marian Charitun, an alien from Slovakia who had illegally voted in the 2022 election in New Jersey.
- In July, an HSI investigation led to the arrest of Denise Nataly Migliore, an alien from Australia who illegally voted in the 2022 and 2024 elections in Louisiana.
- In May, DHS and the Department of Justice (DOJ) announced charges against four non-citizens in New Jersey who illegally voted in federal elections and made false statements while applying for U.S. citizenship.
- In April, Jose Ceballos, an alien from Mexico, pleaded guilty to THREE counts of disorderly election conduct after illegally voting multiple times and falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen in Kansas.
- In March, ICE arrested Mahady Sacko, a criminal illegal alien from Mauritania who had been illegally voting in the United States since 2008.
In recent months, DHS has taken additional steps to safeguard the integrity and security of American elections. These measures include:
- In July, Secretary Mullin sent letters to secretaries of state in several states across the country warning that tens of thousands of non-citizens are registered to vote.
- In July, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) announced that grant recipients will be required to take several key actions on election integrity.
- In June, DHS directed ICE to enforce stricter penalties for non-citizens who illegally vote in American elections, including deportation.

title: ICE Arrests Alien from the Bahamas with Lengthy Criminal History Who Voted in Past Elections

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) led his Pennsylvania colleagues Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), and Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12) on a letter to the Acting Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) exposing the lack of data transparency in current ICE records management and reporting. ICE is refusing to document in public records which local law enforcement agencies with a 287(g) agreement are involved in arrests, thereby hiding from public view how local law enforcement is involved in ICE’s mass deportation regime.

Specifically, the Congressmembers are pushing for training records, complaints, and oversight records about 287(g) programs in Pennsylvania to be made public. The 287(g) program sets up partnerships between ICE and state or local law enforcement agencies to authorize selected officers to carry out federal immigration enforcement or deportation. Reps. Deluzio, Dean, Scanlon, and Lee are demanding ICE require its agents to fully complete the 287(g)-designation field in its arrest records and identify the participating agencies involved in arrests. They also make specific demands that more data, details, and records be released to the public.

The Pennsylvania congressmembers write in the letter:

“According to published federal records between January 1 to August 6, 2026, of the 1,227 Pennsylvania 287(g) arrest records, only 12 of those records included the task force designation agency that was involved in arrest. ICE chose to withhold that information more than 1,000 times so far this year despite such information being a designated field included in arrest records. This discrepancy undermines transparency and leaves the public without a clear understanding of which agency or department was involved.

The members continue:

“The public has a right to clear and complete information about the nature of the enforcement activities taking place in our neighborhoods and the departments or agencies responsible for carrying them out. Programs between federal and local law enforcement agencies must meet the highest standards of transparency.”

The full text of the letter is available HERE.

Congressman Deluzio is actively fighting back against Trump’s mass deportation scheme. In May 2026, he and Congresswoman Summer Lee conducted an unannounced oversight visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center in Clearfield County, PA, where they found that the overwhelming majority of people locked up inside the ICE facility were considered low-security level—meaning that they have not been accused of serious, violent crimes or engaged in similar conduct while detained.

During this visit, the two congressmembers were blocked from bringing congressional staff inside the facility. These staff were immigration policy experts and able to provide translation services, limiting the congressmembers’ ability to communicate with people inside Moshannon. After this, Congressman Deluzio introduced the Oversight Access Act, a new bill which would permit Members of Congress to bring one member of their staff inside Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities when conducting oversight, without prior notice.

Rep. Deluzio led and joined his Pennsylvania colleagues on recent letters to ICE and the GEO Group, the for-profit prison corporation that owns and operates the Pennsylvania Moshannon Valley Processing Center to demand answers on GEO’s failure to comply with federal standards of adequate staffing and medical care to detainees and to stop obstructing congressional oversight.

title: Deluzio Leads PA Colleagues in Demanding Stronger Data Transparency from ICE

AKRON, OH – U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) issued the following statement honoring the 2,977 Americans who lost their lives in the World Trade Center attacks, and the resilience of the first responders who answered the call to serve on September 11, 2001.

“September 11th forever changed us as a nation. On the 25th anniversary of this horrific attack, I am remembering those we lost, and reaffirming my commitment to our first responders – including firefighters, police officers, and paramedics – who stand as pillars of courage in our communities, embodying America’s enduring spirit,” said Rep. Sykes. “As we come together to remember the 2,977 Americans lost on this day, I am reflecting on the lasting impact their memories have left on our nation.

“Every generation carries forward its own remembrance. Some are old enough to remember exactly where they stood that morning. Others have only known a world shaped by what came after: the wars, the security measures, and the grief that rippled through families.

“Despite the pain of our collective loss on September 11, I am reminded of the unwavering bravery of both first responders and bystanders who ran toward the destruction to save countless lives that day. Their selfless actions remind us of the deep resilience and unity at the heart of our country.

“If September 11th is remembered for what was lost, September 12th is remembered for what was found. Americans woke up the next morning to a changed country, but also to a shared sense of purpose that cut across every line that divides us. Neighbors checked on neighbors. Strangers gave blood, donated supplies, and stood in line for hours to help however they could. I have often said that Ohio’s 13th District is the Birthplace of Champions precisely because of moments like these, when everyday people choose to show up for one another.

“Twenty five years later, our shared promise is the same as it was on September 12, 2001. We do not forget, and we keep building a country worthy of what was given for it. As your representative in Congress, I remain steadfast in my commitment to fostering the American spirit and to always fighting for those who put their lives on the line to protect their fellow Americans.”

Rep. Sykes joined the City of Canton for the 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb, to honor the first responders who lost their lives in the attacks on September 11, 2001. Participants climbed the equivalent of the 110 stories of the World Trade Center beginning at 8:46 a.m. to coincide with the time the North Tower was struck.
title: Rep. Sykes Honors First Responders on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11

WASHINGTON, DC— Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA), House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (D-NY), and Senior House Democrat of Congress’ Joint Economic Committee Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) released the following statement after Republican leadership scheduled the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act for a vote in the House next week:

“House Democrats are rock solid in our support for Ukraine, but the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would do more harm than good. This bill would dramatically expand presidential tariff authorities while failing to mandate sanctions on Russia, both of which are unacceptable. These flaws would raise Americans’ prices while undermining support for Ukraine in the long term.

“We continue to seek bicameral, bipartisan negotiations to craft a bill that can win strong support in both chambers and deliver on our promise to Ukraine. In the meantime, the President has ample authority to expand sanctions on those fueling Russia’s war machine, including those targeted by this bill, and we renew our call on him to do so without further delay.”

(WASHINGTON) – Today, Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, released the following statement on the 25th Anniversary of the September 11th, 2001 Attacks.

“Twenty-five years later, the pain of September 11th has not faded. We remember the nearly 3,000 people who were taken from their families and the extraordinary courage shown by first responders and ordinary citizens alike. The best way to honor them is to make sure our country never suffers a tragedy like that again.

“After 9/11, we worked across party lines to strengthen our homeland security. Today, those protections are being weakened as threats continue to evolve. Cutting national security staff, undermining cybersecurity, threatening TSA privatization, and withholding counterterrorism funding create dangerous security gaps. We should be working together to close gaps, not senselessly creating new ones.

“We must be clear-eyed about the world we live in – and strive to uphold our American values as we seek to secure our people and our homeland. We owe it to the Americans who lost their lives on 9/11 to ensure our government is focused on the most pressing threats facing the Nation so that, together, we can help defend the homeland against them.”

# # #
title: Thompson Marks 25th Anniversary of the September 11 Attacks

ANNAPOLIS, MD – Yesterday, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) hosted a second Maryland Third Congressional District Constituent Resource Fair in Anne Arundel County. The first Resource Fair was held in Howard County this past May and featured representatives from 19 agencies. Elfreth and her team were joined by 26 federal, state, local, business, and nonprofit partners, covering a range of services from workforce development to health care, veterans affairs, and more.

“First and foremost, my team and I are here to help our neighbors with any issue they face at any level of government, and these resource fairs are just one way we can connect them to the services they need. From our first resource fair to the thousands of cases that my team handles day in and day out – the need for community services and support is clear, especially as we grapple with the aftermath of DOGE, the weaponization of ICE, skyrocketing costs, and so much more,” said Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. “I want to extend a sincere thank you to all of our partners who joined us and for their continued commitment to serving our community on their hardest days. This work is never done alone.”

Elfreth and her team have also provided casework assistance to constituents on a range of issues with federal agencies, including the Department of Veterans Affairs, Social Security, immigration agencies, and the IRS. To date, Congresswoman Elfreth’s team has closed over 3,000 constituent cases and returned over $4 million directly to constituents.

The second Constituent Resource Fair included representatives from Senator Shaneka Henson’s Office, the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland, the Maryland Insurance Administration, the Maryland Department of Labor, the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families, the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development, the Anne Arundel County Community Action Agency, the American Kidney Foundation, Comcast, the City of Annapolis - No Harm, the City of Annapolis - Hispanic Community Services, the City of Annapolis - Naptown Anti-dope Move(meant), BGE, Chamber of Mothers, the Housing Commission of Anne Arundel County, American Red Cross, the Anne Arundel County Mental Health Agency/Crisis Response System, the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities, the Anne Arundel County Office of Community Engagement & Constituent Services, the Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works, the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Anne Arundel County Recreation and Parks, HealthCare Access Maryland, Anne Arundel County’s Sheriff Office, the Chief Administrative Office - Office of Talent and Development, and the Chesapeake Children’s Museum.

“Good governance is about solving problems regardless of which agency's logo is on the door,” said Mayor Jared Littmann. “We're pleased to work with Congresswoman Elfreth to deliver results and one-stop shopping for resources across local, state, and federal agencies.”

“Too often, the biggest barrier between someone and the help they need isn’t a lack of resources-it’s a lack of information. That’s why community collaboration matters so much. My office cannot reach every family on our own. We need neighbors, nonprofits, and local organizations partnering with us to spread the word,” said Senator Shaneka Henson, D30, Annapolis.

“When Marylanders have questions about home loans, student loans, or banking (including online banking apps), they deserve answers,” says Antonio P. Salazar, Commissioner of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor. "Our office helps consumers know their rights, avoid scams, file complaints, and find the right resources. We are pleased to join community partners at events like this to help Marylanders access the support and information they need."

“As the nation's leading nonprofit fighting kidney disease, the American Kidney Fund (AKF) works across the country to engage communities and raise awareness about kidney disease, and we are thankful to have the opportunity to be a part of Rep. Elfreth's community resource fair,” said LaVarne A. Burton, President and CEO of the American Kidney Fund. “With 1 in 7 American adults living with kidney disease and millions more at risk of developing this life-altering condition, events like this are important to our efforts to connect members of the community with valuable resources and ensure people have the knowledge they need to prevent and manage kidney disease.”

“Chamber of Mothers is proud to participate in Congresswoman Elfreth’s Constituent Resource Fair,” said Kelsey McCarthy, Co-Facilitator and Volunteer with the Maryland Chapter of Chamber of Mothers. “Mothers are navigating complex challenges every day, from finding affordable childcare to accessing quality health care and other essential resources. Strong communities are built when we work together to ensure mothers know where they can turn for support. We’re grateful to Congresswoman Elfreth and her team for creating opportunities like this to connect mothers with organizations that are ready to help and to strengthen the community partnerships that make that support possible.”

“AAEDC is grateful to Congresswoman Elfreth for bringing this Resource Fair to Annapolis. Having federal and local resources together in one place makes it easier for residents and businesses to find the support they need. For AAEDC, it is also an important opportunity to hear directly from businesses about the challenges they are facing and connect them with capital, technical assistance, government resources, and other tools that can help them succeed,” said AAEDC President and CEO, Amy Gowan.

"The Anne Arundel County Sheriff’s Office was honored to participate in Maryland’s Third District Constituent Resource Fair, hosted by Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. The Sheriff’s Office values the chance to connect with citizens by sharing resources and information about the services we provide." Anne Arundel County Sheriff Everett Sesker stated, “Our participation in events like this allows us to build positive connections with community members and strengthen our relationship with them. Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth is a dedicated partner to public safety, and we appreciate her efforts to offer resources to the community.”

###
title: Elfreth Hosts Second Constituent Resource Fair in Anne Arundel County

text:
Congresswoman Betty McCollum, Dean of the Minnesota congressional delegation, released the following statement reflecting on the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001. The Congresswoman, who was in Washington that day, is the only member of Minnesota’s 2001 delegation still serving today.

“September 11, 2001: A beautiful blue morning sky being shattered by the horror of two airplanes steered into the World Trade Center towers. Evacuating with my staff from my Longworth House office building. Black smoke rising from the Pentagon across the Potomac River. Seeing a fourth plane crashed into a Pennsylvania field. Along with you, these tragic images are seared in my memory, despite the passage of 25 years.

These scenes have become part of the American psyche, even for those who were not yet born to witness them firsthand. They still fill us with fear, anger, grief, and sadness. In a moment, nearly 3,000 Americans’ lives were ripped away from us. Loved ones who were left behind have endured 25 years without grandfathers, mothers, husbands, sisters, and sons. The pain of their loss does not go away.

Today as a nation, we once again come together to mourn with the families. We remember the steadfast flight attendants, resolute pilots, and selfless passengers, including our fellow Minnesotan, Tom Burnett Jr., who helped lead the effort to retake the cockpit of United Flight 93 from hijackers, and prevented it from hitting its intended target in Washington, D.C.

And of course, we will never forget the courageous First Responders rushed toward toppling buildings, who risked their lives in hope of saving others. We remember the thousands who have faced illness and death from exposure to toxic dust and smoke during the months of recovery. We still feel the loss, the very sad sense of tragedy and hurt that touched us all. For all of us, September 11, 2001 remains a day that changed us and changed our country.

But let us not forget the spirit of unity that was forged in those ashes. We put aside differences and came together as Americans -- far more powerful, resilient, and righteous than the perpetrators of the attack. Our nation emerged stronger.

The anniversary of September 11, 2001 is now a National Day of Service and Remembrance. We come together to give back to our communities across America. This year, volunteers in Saint Paul and cities across the country to help pack 18,000,000 meals that will feed Americans who depend on food assistance.

The 25th anniversary falls during the 250th year of our American journey. From the beginning, America has been tested by events and adversaries, both foreign and domestic. The future of our country is up to each of us. Our nation endures because of the power of individuals uniting to create a more perfect union.

During the long, difficult years since that beautiful, terrible morning, the most important lesson I can draw upon is the profound blessing I feel to be an American and to share this country, our values, and our freedoms with my fellow citizens. There are no guarantees that our future will be free from challenges. But if we continue to build from the unity we shared after 9/11, our nation will not only endure, we will be stronger.”
title: Congresswoman McCollum Reflects on the 25th Anniversary of September 11, 2001

Today, Representative Sharice Davids rode Johnson County United’s Airport Drop & Ride from the Overland Park Convention Center to Kansas City International Airport, highlighting the success of the soon-closing public transit service and the demand for convenient, reliable transportation options in Johnson County.

“People want transportation options that are easy, reliable, and affordable — and this service has shown exactly what that can look like in Johnson County,” said Davids. “More than 6,000 people chose to ride these buses during the World Cup and after, and the overwhelming majority of riders said they had an excellent experience and would recommend the service. We should take what we learned from this pilot and use it to build a stronger public transportation system that works for Johnson County families, workers, and visitors.”

Watch Davids speak on the success of Johnson County United’s Airport Drop & Ride shuttle.

Johnson County United’s Airport Drop & Ride has provided free, direct service between Kansas City International Airport, the Overland Park Convention Center and Lenexa City Center during the summer. The service has provided 6,635 rides through August 31, including more than 4,500 rides through July 16.

According to the Johnson County Public Works & Infrastructure Department, riders gave the service overwhelmingly positive reviews:

96.2 percent rated their experience “excellent,” with another 3.27 percent rating it “good.”

97.57 percent said they were “very likely” to recommend the service.

95.45 percent cited the comfort and cleanliness of the buses as something they liked most.

90.27 percent said the service was easy to use.

88.79 percent cited on-time arrival as a positive.

If the shuttle had not been available, 35.7 percent said they would have relied on a family member or friend for a ride, while 30.3 percent said they would have used Uber or Lyft.

The service was designed as part of Johnson County’s temporary transportation network surrounding the 2026 FIFA World Cup, but county data showed that Johnson County residents used the airport shuttle for more than just World Cup-related travel. In a survey reported by the Johnson County Post, 73 percent of riders said they were using the service for vacation or personal travel, and 12 percent for business travel. County officials have viewed the temporary service as a pilot to gather data and operational experience that could inform the future of transit in the county.

"This pilot program represents an unprecedented investment in Johnson County transit, combining federal, state, and local dollars," said Mike Kelly, Chairman, Johnson County Board of Commissioners. "We built the JoCo United Airport Drop & Ride to move World Cup visitors efficiently, but it's Johnson County residents who have embraced it, using it as a fast, free and convenient way to get to the airport."

Davids has long advocated for federal investment in public transportation and helped pass the bipartisan infrastructure law as a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. The law represents the largest federal investment in public transportation in the nation’s history and delivered record funding to modernize Kansas City’s public transit network.

Davids secured more than $49.3 million in direct federal formula funding for Kansas public transit systems in the first allocation under the bipartisan infrastructure law.
title: Davids Rides Johnson County Airport Shuttle, Highlights Success of Pilot Program

California Man Sentenced to Over 12 Years in Prison for Distributing Sadistic Child Sexual Abuse Material Over the Dark Web
James David Johnson, 58, of Santee, California, was sentenced today to 151 months in prison and 10 years of supervised release for distributing images and videos over the dark web that depicted the sexual abuse of children.
Johnson pleaded guilty to distributing child pornography on Oct. 14, 2025. According to court documents, Johnson was a member of at least five dark web communities dedicated to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and the sexual exploitation of children. He distributed large volumes of CSAM on these websites and provided other users with advice on how to evade law enforcement. On one of these websites, which was in part dedicated to content depicting children being subject to pain and suffering, he rose through the ranks to become a high-ranking staff member. FBI agents executed search warrants at Johnson’s home and place of work and seized computer devices containing more than 260,000 images and videos of apparent child sexual abuse and exploitation, as well as autopsy and crime-scene photos depicting deceased children.
Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon for the Southern District of California; Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI’s San Diego Field Office; and Assistant Director Heith Janke of the FBI’s Criminal Investigative Division made the announcement.
The FBI’s San Diego Field Office and Child Exploitation Operational Section investigated the case.
Acting Deputy Chief Kyle P. Reynolds of the Justice Department’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Griffith for the Southern District of California prosecuted the case.
This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Justice Department. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: California Man Sentenced to Over 12 Years in Prison for Distributing Sadistic Child Sexual Abuse Material Over the Dark Web

Brooklyn Adult Daycare Owner Sentenced to Prison for Leadership Role in $64M Medicaid Fraud Scheme
A Brooklyn woman was sentenced yesterday to 76 months in prison in connection with her leadership of a vast $64 million Medicaid fraud and illegal kickback scheme at her two social adult daycare centers and home health care company. The defendant was also ordered to pay over $56 million in restitution and to forfeit $5 million in fraud proceeds, including two properties, cash, and gold jewelry seized during a search of her home, as pictured below.
“The Fraud Division will relentlessly hold accountable individuals who exploit Medicaid and take advantage of services meant to support our seniors,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “This sentence should put all Medicaid fraudsters on notice — if you steal from Medicaid, we will uncover your conduct, protect the beneficiaries you harm, and ensure you are brought to justice.”
“Yesterday’s sentencing sends a strong message of deterrence in our District,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “Our Office and the Justice Department are focused on protecting American taxpayers from fraudsters and as such, we will vigorously prosecute corrupt health care owners and operators in our district.”
“Social adult day care and home health services are designed to support seniors, not line the pockets of fraudsters,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “Today’s sentence sends an important message that anyone who illicitly exploits the Medicaid program will be held accountable to the full extent of the law.”
“Khan acted with staggering greed, leading a scheme to defraud Medicaid of millions of dollars intended for people in need. She and her co-conspirators set up social adult day cares but, instead of providing care and services to our most vulnerable neighbors, they enriched themselves with cash, gold and property,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Pete Gizas of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New York. “Today’s sentence sends a message: we will be relentless in our pursuit of justice against fraudsters. HSI is working side by side with our law enforcement partners to uncover and dismantle complex fraud networks like this one.”
“Zakia Khan stole $64 million from the Medicaid program through bribes and kickbacks—money meant to support the most vulnerable,” stated NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch. “This was not only deeply illegal but also immoral, and the NYPC will continue to investigate anyone who exploits government programs for personal gain. I thank our NYPD investigators and all our partners in law enforcement for their work in stopping this criminal and bringing this case to a close.”
According to court documents, Zakia Khan, 55, of Brooklyn, New York, owned two social adult daycare centers—Happy Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc. (Happy Family) and Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc. (Family Social). She also owned a home health care fiscal intermediary called Responsible Care Staffing Inc. and an entity she used to receive and disguise fraud proceeds called Tanwee Services Inc.
From approximately October 2017 through July 2024, in exchange for kickbacks and bribes, a web of marketers referred Medicaid recipients to Khan’s social adult daycare centers. As depicted in the pictures below, Khan and the marketers paid kickbacks and bribes to the Medicaid recipients to induce them to sign up for services that Khan then billed to Medicaid. These services were never actually provided as represented to Medicaid.
Between 2017 and 2024, Happy Family and Family Social fraudulently billed Medicaid approximately $64 million. Medicaid paid approximately $56 million based on these false and fraudulent claims. Khan and her co-conspirators used multiple business entities to launder the fraud proceeds and generate the cash used to pay kickbacks and bribes to the marketers and the Medicaid recipients.
In August 2025, Khan pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud and conspiracy to defraud the United States and pay health care kickbacks.
HHS-OIG, HSI New York, and NYPD investigated the case.
Deputy Chief Patrick J. Campbell and Trial Attorney Leonid Sandlar of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case, with the assistance of Assistant U.S. Attorney Claire Kedeshian for the Eastern District of New York who assisted with forfeiture matters.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
Press Release Number: 26-1047
title: Brooklyn Adult Daycare Owner Sentenced to Prison for Leadership Role in $64M Medicaid Fraud Scheme

EPA Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber and U.S. Rep. Clay Fuller to Highlight Significant Brownfield Investments in North Georgia
CHICKAMAUGA, Georgia (Sept. 11, 2026) – On September 18, 2026, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber and U.S. Representative Clay Fuller (GA-14) will join state and local officials to highlight $6 million in brownfield funding. This investment includes $4 million to City of Chickamauga to clean up the former Crystal Springs Print Works site, so it can be returned to productive reuse; $1.5 million to Northwest Georgia Regional Commission to assess properties for potential redevelopment; and $500,000 to Rome-Floyd County Development Authority to expand the inventory of brownfield sites and assess prospective properties.
Who:
Kevin McOmber, Regional Administrator, EPA Region 4
Clay Fuller, U.S. Representative (GA-14)
Jeff Cown, Director, Georgia Environmental Protection Division
Evitte Parrish, Mayor, City of Chickamauga
Boyd Austin, Executive Director, Northwest Georgia Regional Commission
Evie McNiece, board member, Rome Floyd County Development Authority
When:
Friday, September 18, 2026
2 p.m.
Where:
Chickamauga Civic Center
1817 Lee Clarkson Rd.
Chickamauga, GA 30707
RSVP: Credentialed media who wish to attend should sign up no later than 7 p.m. ET, Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026 at: https://www.epa.gov/ga/forms/epa-region-4-event-rsvp-form.
Background: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has announced $13.5 million in Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment and Cleanup (MAC) grants to accelerate the cleanup of polluted sites across Georgia. With these funds, EPA is investing directly in American communities to clean up and redevelop blighted properties, delivering on the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensure that clean air, land, and water go hand-in-hand with economic growth and opportunity.
EPA’s Brownfields Program began in 1995 and has provided over $3 billion in grant funding to assess and clean up contaminated properties and return blighted properties to productive reuse.
To date, brownfields investments leveraged more than $45 billion in cleanup and redevelopment. Over the years, the relatively small investment of federal funding was able to leverage, from both public and private sources, more than 228,900 jobs. Through fiscal year 2025, on average, $19.47 was leveraged for each EPA Brownfields Grant dollar awarded through multipurpose, assessment, revolving loan fund and cleanup cooperative agreements.
###
title: EPA Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber and U.S. Rep. Clay Fuller to Highlight Significant Brownfield Investments in North Georgia

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy urging him to withdraw a proposed rule to cut Head Start funding, which would take away educational opportunities from New Mexico children. The “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs,” rule would rescind over 1,400 regulations for Head Start. Educators warn that this rule would cut services, reduce program quality, and lead to large variations between states, leaving some children with less resources than others.

“Head Start is a critical lifeline for over 7,000 hardworking families in New Mexico,” said Vasquez. “But instead of working with parents and communities to make early childhood education and childcare more affordable and accessible, the Administration has spent two years attacking Head Start and taking money away from children. I’m calling on Secretary Kennedy to rescind this threat — our kids deserve better.”

“While Head Start needs improvements and additional investments, staffing, and capacity, the proposed rule does not effectively address these needs. Instead, it risks gutting the program and sowing chaos across the country at a time when hardworking families are struggling more than ever to cover the cost of childcare,” wrote Vasquez in the letter. “Your agency should be working hand-in-hand with Head Start providers and communities to improve the program, not causing additional concern, chaos, and confusion.”

You can read the full letter HERE.

Rep. Vasquez has consistently fought to secure funding for Head Start programs:

Visiting Isleta Pueblo Head Start to discuss the importance of early childhood education, language and cultural preservation, and securing a key report on effective ways to improve Tribal Head Start programs.

Sending a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services urging action to address the severe impacts of recent federal funding interruptions and the government shutdown risks on Head Start programs in New Mexico and across the country.

Pushing for a $14 billion investment dedicated to Head Start in the Fiscal Year 2027 government funding bill to strengthen early childhood education and expand access for families nationwide.

###
title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Demands Secretary Kennedy Protect Head Start Programs for New Mexico Children

Department of Justice Removes Alien Terrorist in First Use of United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court
In the first-ever case before the United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court (ATRC), Nazira Haji Zada, 47, an Afghan national previously residing in Fort Worth, Texas, was removed from the United States after conceding that she is an alien terrorist. As the matriarch in her family, she supported a plot to commit an ISIS-inspired mass shooting on Election Day in 2024 for which her son, Abdullah Haji Zada, and son-in-law, Nasir Ahmad Tawhedi, were previously arrested and convicted. The ATRC issued an order of removal on Aug. 20 that was unsealed earlier today following her return to her country of origin. This was the first case ever brought before the ATRC, which Congress established decades ago, and which no previous administration had used. Zada is now permanently inadmissible to the United States.
The application to remove Zada, certified by Attorney General Todd Blanche, was filed on July 15, and Zada appeared in open court for the first time on July 30. ATRC Chief Judge Joan N. Ericksen presided over that hearing and later signed the removal order. In compliance with the ATRC statute, the government used classified information to establish that Zada is an alien terrorist. Additionally, the government provided Zada and her lawyers, two federal public defenders, with approximately half a terabyte of documents supporting the government’s case. With her lawyers, Zada conceded that she is an alien terrorist and waived appeal of the removal order, terminating her previous status.
“This landmark case, resulting in the prompt removal of this alien terrorist to her country of origin, is a win for national security and the rule of law,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Those who support and condone terrorism should not be living in the United States, and this first-ever case before the ATRC shows how the Department will use every tool at its disposal to protect our country.”
“This is a historic and vitally important step in our work to protect the U.S. homeland from terrorism,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “An individual who supported a plot by ISIS-sympathizing family members to commit an attack in America has paid the price for that. She came to our country, betrayed it, and has now lost the right to live here and enjoy our democratic freedoms. This FBI and our Justice Department partners will protect the American people from the threat of terrorism, using all means necessary.”
“From the moment President Trump took office, he made clear that his Administration would put the safety and security of the American people first,” said Secretary Markwayne Mullin of the Department of Homeland Security. “The President’s direction to use the Alien Terrorist Removal Court to expel Nazira Haji Zada, an Afghan national who plotted with members of her family to carry out an ISIS-inspired attack on American soil, delivers on that promise. Thanks to the President’s leadership and the coordinated efforts the Departments of Homeland Security, Justice and State, Nazira Haji Zada’s final order of removal is now FINAL. Those who plot acts of terrorism against the United States have no place in our country. We will find them, and we will use every lawful tool available to remove them.”
“Zada supported her sons’ terrorist plot to attack the United States while she enjoyed the privilege of residing here as a resident alien,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “She abused our Nation’s hospitality and represented a clear threat to our national security. The United States is a safer place now that her sons are in custody and she has been deported.”
“Those who support terrorism against the American people will face the consequences,” said State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott. “We will secure our borders, and we will use every tool to stop those who intend us harm from entering or remaining at-large in our country. Under the leadership of President Trump, the State Department, alongside the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security, will always work tirelessly to ensure the safety of our people and the security of our nation.”
Tawhedi and Abdullah Haji Zada were arrested on Oct. 7, 2024, after purchasing firearms and ammunition to be used in an Election Day terrorist attack from an undercover FBI employee. Nazira’s son Abdullah, who was 17 at the time of his arrest, entered his guilty plea as an adult and was sentenced to 15 years in prison. As part of the plea agreement, Abdullah stipulated to the entry of a judicial order of removal from the United States to Afghanistan following his term of incarceration. Abdullah acknowledged that the order of removal would terminate his lawful permanent resident status, and waived his right to appeal the conviction except in limited circumstances or seek any form of appeal or relief from his removal and deportation, including but not limited to, seeking asylum. Tawhedi, 28, pled guilty to two terrorism-related offenses: conspiring and attempting to provide material support and resources to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS), a designated foreign terrorist organization, and receiving, attempting to receive, and conspiring to receive firearms and ammunition in furtherance of a federal crime of terrorism on June 13, 2025, and is awaiting sentencing.
According to court documents, Tawhedi admitted that between June 2024 and October 2024, he conspired with at least one other individual to purchase two AK-47 rifles, 500 rounds of ammunition, and 10 magazines, with the intent to carry out a mass-casualty attack on or around Election Day, Nov. 5, 2024, on behalf of ISIS. According to a criminal complaint affidavit filed in the case, Tawhedi communicated with an ISIS facilitator about his plan to purchase firearms for use in the terror plot, including asking the individual whether 500 rounds of ammunition would be sufficient.
According to the criminal complaint, to raise funds for their attack, in 2024, the family started selling off their property, including furniture, computers, a mobile phone, and the family’s two vehicles. Zada signed a contract to sell the family house. The family also purchased one-way airfare for travel to Kabul, Afghanistan shortly before Election Day 2024 for its members, including for Zada and other minor children but not Abdullah and Tawhedi.
The ATRC is a specialized federal court, which Congress established in 1996. The court has jurisdiction to swiftly remove alien terrorists from the United States when the government establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that an alien is a terrorist. See Title 8 of the United States Code, Sections 1227(a)(4)(B), 1531(1), and 1534(g). It is run and staffed by U.S. federal district court judges confirmed to the judiciary pursuant to Article III of the Constitution and then appointed to the ATRC by the Chief Justice of the United States. See Title 8 of the United States Code, Sections 1531 to 1537.
The court allows the government to use classified information where disclosing that information to the public would pose risks to national security. The statutory provisions that establish the court provide paid counsel to the aliens if necessary and also permit either party to appeal to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.
This removal proceeding reflects the coordinated efforts of multiple federal agencies, including the Department of Justice’s National Security Division, the FBI, and the U.S. Marshals Service, as well as the Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.
Acting Deputy Assistant Attorney General Hayden O’Byrne of the National Security Division led the litigation with assistance from Deputy Chief Larry Schneider and Trial Attorneys Anna Donnell, Garrett Coyle and Evan Schultz.
For more information on the ATRC and to view court documents visit: www.atrc.uscourts.gov/. The Department of Justice previously announced the arrest here: www.justice.gov/opa/pr/department-justice-files-first-case-us-alien-terrorist-removal-court-deport-afghan-alien-who
title: Department of Justice Removes Alien Terrorist in First Use of United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court

Ranking Member Lofgren Condemns Radical Changes to NSF Initiatives
(Washington, DC) — Yesterday, National Science Foundation (NSF) Acting Director Brian Stone released a statement titled “NSF leadership in a new golden age of science,” outlining how NSF is implementing White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Director Michael Kratsios' Science: A New Golden Age and the Fiscal Year 2028 OMB-OSTP R&D Budget Priorities Memorandum. In this statement, Acting Director Stone verifies NSF’s intentions to implement Director Kratsios’ initiatives that will reallocate funding from congressionally approved programs to White House pet projects.
Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren made the following statement:
"I do not know why Acting Director Brian Stone and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios believe they possess the authority to impose such radical changes at America's premier scientific agency without congressional input or authorization. The Trump Administration has profoundly damaged NSF with its repeated attacks against the agency and the scientific community it was created to support. NSF needs to stop, take 10 steps back, and remember the values that made it the envy of the world for 75 years. I do not intend to abandon those values, and I will fight for them as we conduct oversight of these changes in the months to come."

WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement after hosting a successful career expo in Buffalo, New York that drew more than 1,100 attendees.
The DHS Career Expo took place from September 1 to September 2 at the U.S. Coast Guard Sector Eastern Great Lakes in Buffalo, New York.

With more than 1,100 attendees and more than 500 interviews hosted, DHS received more than 600 applications and issued more than 600 tentative job offers,” said a DHS Spokesperson. “This success proves that Americans are answering the call to help protect the homeland by removing illegal aliens, terrorists, and other public safety threats from our country. On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the spirit of bravery and patriotism that has long defined America remains stronger than ever.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representative Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) introduced legislation this week declaring a national housing emergency, incenting housing production to build or restore four million new homes. The National Housing Emergency Act, led by Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) in the Senate, will boost domestically produced materials to support the construction and rehabilitation of housing and push states and localities to cut red tape currently standing in the way of building middle class housing.

“Constituents across my district, from young families to aging seniors and everyone in between, are all facing the same problem: housing is too expensive,” said Rep. Houlahan, “We need to start treating the high cost of housing like the crisis it is, and that’s exactly what the National Housing Emergency Act does. This legislation relieves some of the supply constraints, building and restoring four million homes to stop the cycle of high costs for buyers and renters at every stage of life.”
title: Houlahan Introduces Bill to Build Four Million New Homes, Declare National Housing Emergency
