EVERGREEN – Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (C0-07) today solemnly marked the one year anniversary of the tragic Evergreen High School shooting, introducing a bipartisan congressional resolution signed by all members of the Colorado U.S. House delegation honoring the shooting victims, and expressing gratitude to first responders, law enforcement, educators, faculty, and neighbors who acted swiftly to protect students and staff during last year’s shooting. Senator Michael Bennet (D-CO) is leading a companion resolution in the Senate.

“Today, we honor the students, staff, first responders, families, and entire Evergreen community for their extraordinary resilience in the face of the tragedy after the Evergreen High School shooting one year ago today. Their strength, courage, and resilience continue to inspire all of us but also reminds us of the urgent need for change,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “Our country’s gun violence epidemic has shattered countless lives and is now the leading cause of death for our kids - a reality none of us should accept. As a mom, I understand the fear so many parents live with when they drop their kids off at school. Today, we stand with the Evergreen community and promise to keep fighting in Congress to ensure our kids are safe at school and in our communities. They deserve so much better.”

“One year ago today, the Evergreen community experienced an unthinkable act of gun violence,” said Senator Michael Bennet. “The fear and trauma that Evergreen High School students, families, educators, and first responders experienced that day have not disappeared. We owe it to them – and all of Colorado – to act and to build a future where no child has to experience this kind of violence at school. I am glad to lead the Colorado Congressional Delegation in this resolution, and will continue to fight against senseless acts of gun violence.”

"It is unacceptable that gun violence has become normal in America. A year ago, Coloradans experienced another tragic school shooting, this time at Evergreen High School, which left two students injured and an entire community traumatized. I'm proud to join my colleagues in recognizing the brave first responders and Evergreen’s resilient survivors and residents, but more must be done. Congressional action to stop gun violence is long overdue—it's past time we pass legislation to protect our kids. Enough is enough," said Congresswoman Diana DeGette (CO-01).

“A year later, our hearts remain with the people of Jefferson County as they continue to heal from the tragic shooting at Evergreen High School. No parent should ever have to receive the kind of call that far too many parents in our country have received—and no child should have to be marched out of their classroom, hide under their desk, or fear gunshots in their school. Enough is enough. We must stand together against senseless acts of gun violence,” said Congressman Joe Neguse (CO-02)

“One year after the tragic shooting at Evergreen High School, our heart is with the students, families, and first responders who faced unimaginable horror that day. As a combat veteran and father of two kids, I refuse to accept that our classrooms should function like war zones. We can honor the resilience of the Evergreen community not just with our thoughts, but by elected officials of both parties acting to pass common-sense gun safety laws to protect our children, communities, and Colorado,” said Congressman Jason Crow (CO-06)

“I continue to pray that God strengthens Evergreen High School and the Jefferson County community. I am honored to join my colleagues on the bipartisan memorial resolution and to keep working with them to direct federal dollars toward more School Resource Officers so we can protect our children against evil acts. My heart remains with everyone in Evergreen.” said Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04).

“As a father of five, I cannot imagine the fear and heartbreak the Evergreen community experienced that day. One year later, we remember the victims, stand with the students, families, and educators who still carry the weight of what happened, and recognize the first responders who ran toward danger to protect others. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Pettersen and my colleagues in the Colorado delegation in honoring the strength and resilience Evergreen has shown over the past year,” said Congressman Jeff Hurd (CO-03)

"One year ago, the Evergreen community lived through something no community should. We pray God continues to give them comfort, and we thank the deputies and teachers who ran toward danger and saved lives,” said Congressman Jeff Crank (CO-05)

"Today, we remember the students, their families, and an entire community that continues to heal from the horrific act of violence that took place just one year ago at Evergreen High School. We also honor the first responders, law enforcement officers, educators, health care workers, and neighbors who acted without hesitation to protect students and save lives. As a father and former police officer, I’m proud to join the Colorado delegation in making sure their courage is remembered and that the Evergreen community knows Colorado continues to stand with them,” said Congressman Gabe Evans (CO-08)

Specifically, the resolution honors the two victims who were wounded, and recognizes the lasting trauma carried by students, staff, families, and the broader community. It also pays tribute to the first responders, law enforcement officers, educators, school staff, neighbors, and hospital workers who stepped up with courage and compassion in the aftermath.

See the full text of the resolution here.

This resolution comes after, earlier this year, Congresswoman Pettersen introduced three pieces of legislation responding to the tragedy at Evergreen High School last year:

The Evergreen Community Safety Act which requires social media companies to respond to warrants and subpoena requests regarding potential threats of violence within 72 hours.

Bill text is available HERE.

The Community Firearm Safety Act, which creates a permissible use under the Byrne Justice Assistance Grant Program within the Department of Justice (DOJ) to allow grants for localities to procure and distribute safe firearm storage boxes to community members.

Bill text is available HERE.

The Community Risk Training and Response Act, which creates a grant program through the Office of the Attorney General for up to $500,000 for localities to provide technical assistance and training to law enforcement, prosecutors, judges and court staff, healthcare providers, educators, and agencies designated to coordinate Extreme Risk Order Implementation and to develop standardized extreme risk protection order training and curriculum nationwide.

Bill text is available HERE.

Since the Columbine tragedy in 1999, more than 390,000 students in the United States have experienced gun violence at school, killing at least 203 and injuring 441 students, educators, and other individuals on K-12 campuses. Colorado has been touched by gun violence before, with spaces of community such as schools, movie theaters, night clubs, and houses of worship affected.
title: Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen Solemnly Marks One Year Since Evergreen High School Shooting

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) toured The Avenue at Greenmont, a new housing development in Dracut featuring 56 newly built apartment homes designed for adults aged 62 and older and non-elderly individuals with disabilities. All units are fully affordable to households earning at or below 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI). The project was made possible in part through nearly $7 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, awarded by the Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) through its Community-Based Housing program.

“These 56 homes show what's possible when private partners and every level of government row in the same direction,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Federal resources like ARPA dollars and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits helped make The Avenue at Greenmont a reality, but we can't stop here. We must continue advancing commonsense legislation like the recently passed 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act so more families can afford a home of their own.”

The project also received $3 million from the Town of Dracut's Community Preservation Act, $1.4 million from EOHLC's Housing Stabilization Fund, $825,000 in federal HOME funds, $630,000 through the state's MassWorks program, more than $5.5 million in Massachusetts Housing Tax Credits, and nearly $11.4 million in federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.

The United States continues to face a severe affordable housing and homelessness crisis. According to experts, the U.S. has an estimated shortage of 3.7 million to 5.5 million homes for rent and purchase. The lack of housing, along with other factors, is driving up costs and making housing the single largest expense for Americans across the country. According to a recent poll, half of Massachusetts residents say housing is unaffordable for their household, making it the single biggest financial pressure point.

In 2021, Trahan supported passage of the American Rescue Plan Act to respond directly to the challenges created and worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic. The law invested billions of dollars to expand affordable housing and support Americans experiencing or at risk of homelessness. In Massachusetts, EOHLC put those federal dollars to work through programs like Community-Based Housing, which helped make The Avenue at Greenmont possible.

Earlier this year, Trahan supported passage of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The new law, which took effect despite President Donald Trump’s refusal to sign it, makes it easier to build new homes, expand financing opportunities for housing, and provide new protections for renters. The bipartisan legislation also reduces unnecessary regulatory barriers to new home construction, authorizes the use of federal funds to support the development of affordable housing, and establishes a maximum limit for affordable rents.

###

HOUSTON, TX — Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) is urging Texans to check their voter registration and make sure their addresses are up to date ahead of the October 5 registration deadline for the November 3, 2026, election.

Roughly 1.2 million Texans are currently on the voter suspense list, including approximately 300,000 Harris County residents whose addresses could not be verified. Being on the suspense list does not mean a voter has lost their right to vote, but it may mean completing additional paperwork, including a Statement of Residence, when casting a ballot.

With the registration deadline approaching, Menefee is encouraging Texans to take a few minutes now to check their status and address any issues before Election Day.

“I represent the district of Barbara Jordan and Mickey Leland, and generations of Texans fought hard for the right to vote. We should never take that right for granted,” said Rep. Menefee. “My own grandfather had to pay a poll tax just to cast his ballot. A generation later, his grandson gets to serve in the United States Congress. I carry that history with me every day, and it’s why I want to make sure every eligible Texan knows their rights and is ready to make their voice heard.”

The deadline to register to vote or update an address for the November 3 election is October 5, 2026.

“It only takes a few minutes to check your registration, so I’m asking Texans to do it now instead of waiting until Election Day,” Rep. Menefee said. “Regardless of how you vote, your voice matters. We owe it to the generations who fought before us to make sure our voices are heard at the ballot box.”

For voter registration and election information, visit VoteTexas.gov.

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Museo De Arte De Lima

Lima, Peru

September 10, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you. It is a pleasure to be here with you today in Peru. It is the second time that I am here. I came many years ago as a senator as the first time to – that I am here. We were waiting for Bernie to come. He’s doing a great job. I know of him for many years, and I am not surprised about the work that he has been doing. And I think that he is a perfect person when talking about the relation between Peru and the U.S. because it is a moment of extraordinary opportunities.

First, I wanted to share what I have been saying since I came here. For me – I think not for me but for everyone, the main role of any government is security and stability. It is the most important, right? Without security, you cannot accomplish anything. And unfortunately, not only in Peru but in the region is confronting a very extraordinary threat. Usually, these threats will be – were taking place within national groups. What has changed in the world, what has changed in the region, is that these groups are now transnational, operating from Colombia against Peru, operating in Peru against Bolivia, operating in Bolivia against Ecuador. So a huge threat.

And the only way of dealing with this or confronting these groups, if we don’t confront them and defeat them, they will eat the country. This is very Cuban. I don’t know how you translate it, but yeah. They will – they will just impact the society. And who will suffer the most? The working class, of course. They are being blackmailed, extortion – they are paying the price. But not only because of the sovereignty of a country; if your territory is controlled by criminal groups, by terrorist groups, how can you be protecting?

And I’m happy that you have an administration with President Fujimori that is committed to confront these delinquents, these criminals, and we will provide the support that she needs. This is not just simply to help Peru and help her. It is also to help ourselves, because these terrorist groups are a threat to Peru but are also a threat to the United States and to the North American people.

Without security, you don’t have prosperity. Obviously, there are a lot of things that we need to do for prosperity. There are companies that don’t like to invest in a country where you don’t feel safe. But also, you need to have security, legally due process – the due process. This is how you attract foreign investment. This is what we want to see. It’s logic that the United States and Peru have relations and very strong bonds and very close in terms of trade, and for us that is a priority as well. It is possible to work on security and at the same time work on trade, of course, and these are related.

And it is a priority for this administration, a priority for President Trump. He is a businessman; he is not a political man. He started, yeah, in politics 10 years ago, but clearly he’s not political. He is a businessman, and this is what he understands and he appreciates. And we want to see more trade activity between Peru and the U.S., and there are great opportunities in order to do so.

I’d like to tell you that what we give you are two things. Number one, unfortunately, well, political instability in Peru. As a Secretary, I think we have had to deal with three different administrations in a year and a half. And it’s impressive because usually you have two presidents in 10 years. But now we have stability, and I think that is important. But also, there has been some negligence from the government, from both political parties in the U.S., that have said, no, yeah, the hemisphere, South America, everything is important; the Americas are important for us. They all said this, but few do something about it. And we are doing something about this. For us, it is a priority. (Applause.)

Why? Why is it a priority? Well, first, because of geography. It is logic that we are going to have trade exchanges. I’d rather have those exchanges with countries that are close to our country. Obviously we’re going to have relations, but it is obvious that we will have these type of exchanges where we have so close – where we’re so close geographically.

Number two is logic because the reality is one of the things that is impacting manufacturing – access to critical minerals, access to all of these elements. It’s easy to have a source of these minerals that it is on the same hemisphere instead of bringing this from Africa. This doesn’t mean that we’re not interested in Africa or Asia, but the logic thing to do is to have access to these minerals, to production, and the production capability of countries that are close to our nation. Logistically speaking, it’s easier.

Number two, this is not a region that has a war. You’re fighting a war against criminals, but we – you don’t have global conflicts like other countries in the world.

Three, because our system and cultures are very similar. We have already connections at a banking level, at a transaction level, at a social level. And logically, because it supports the countries around the region to develop economically, and this is part of the interest of the United States.

So if we have economic issues, if we have political issues, if we have social issues, unfortunately, and insecurity, this has a direct impact on the United States, and we have seen this, right? If you study the situation in Mexico that nowadays, tragically, there is territory in Mexico controlled by cartel; they are the government. But it also has an impact on the border with the U.S. and threatens the U.S. directly. So for us, if there are problems of the hemisphere, this becomes our problem as well.

So for all of these reasons, it’s logic. And I know that you have representatives of many companies that for many years you have investing in the urban economy and have an American representation. We don’t only want you to continue doing this, but we want you to do more. We are coordinating very closely through the ambassador, through the embassy, with the government, and then the administration to make sure that any barrier that exists in the Peruvian system – that this has to be clear, so it makes your job easier. And then, of course, it’s part of our jobs to do more to be able to have more opportunities for the American companies in terms of the opportunity of trade and investment.

We need to also play that role to support, inform through our economic bureaus to U.S. companies that are seeking to invest around the world and most likely they are not aware of Peru because we were not focused on this side of the hemisphere. This is why it’s important to be here today to thank you for all the things that you have been doing for many years. You’re here because you have been working for many years. We want you to be able to more, and we want you to have new markets, new partners, and new tools available. And please be aware that you are a priority for us, for the Department of State and from our embassy to develop all these things. I think it’ll help Peru. Without a doubt, it’ll help the United States, it’ll help you, and it’ll help the entire hemisphere.

So for me, it’s been a very productive visit. I just come from the presidential palace where we had a meeting with the president and then we had a press conference. It went very well, and I hope to come back at least once before they kick out Bernie Navarro from here. I’m joking. But yeah, well, God willing, we will be able to come and we will have more things to discuss.

But during the last – well, the last 40 days for the new administration, we – they requested many things and we have agreed to cooperate in many topics and we have complied and we are in a good start. We need to continue. We need to follow up on this. We need to provide continuity.

We have Bernie Navarro here, focused 100 percent. He’s working every day. But he also has a direct connection with me and the White House that in a world that is experiencing so many things with Iran, with Ukraine, with Russia, with all the things that are taking place, it is important to know that you have in the U.S. system people in high positions that are focusing on this side of the hemisphere, but specifically on the relation with Peru that for many – well, more than 10 years was, like, kind of put aside. I don’t want to say abandoned. This will change.

And I’d like to thank you for being patient with us, and keep being steady, firm, because we’re starting a new era. And I think it’ll be the best era in the relation between both our countries. Thank you very much. (Applause.)

HHS Awards Nearly $25 Million to Strengthen Small Rural Hospitals and Preserve Access to Care
BIRMINGHAM, AL — September 10, 2026 — The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), today announced awards to 132 hospitals totaling nearly $25 million through the Rural Hospital Provider Assistance Program to help eligible small rural hospitals maintain their medical workforce, sustain essential healthcare services, and strengthen access to care for the communities they serve across 13 states.
“Every American should be able to reach a doctor or hospital when they need one, no matter where they live,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting these resources directly into rural hospitals so they can keep doctors and nurses on the job, protect lifesaving services, and deliver care close to home. President Trump and I are strengthening rural healthcare and giving communities across America the tools they need to become healthier, stronger, and more self-reliant.”
Rural hospitals are often the primary source of healthcare in their communities and face unique financial challenges. The Rural Hospital Provider Assistance Program provides direct financial assistance to help address these challenges and reduce the risk of avoidable hospital closures.
“Under the leadership of President Trump and HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., this Administration is committed to ensuring that rural Americans can obtain high-quality healthcare close to home,” said HRSA Administrator Tom Engels. “Rural hospitals are lifelines for their communities, supporting local families, healthcare workers, and economies. Through the Rural Hospital Provider Assistance Program, we are taking direct action to help hospitals continue delivering the care rural communities depend on.”
“Having played an active role in advancing this program in my position as Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies, I am excited to join Administrator Engels in announcing these awards and seeing these resources reach the rural hospitals who need them most,” said Congressman Robert Aderholt. “President Trump and his Administration have made strengthening rural healthcare a priority, and I’m proud to have worked with them to advance this important effort. Rural hospitals are essential to the health and well-being of our communities, and I look forward to seeing this investment help ensure Alabamians, and rural citizens across the country, can continue to receive quality healthcare close to home.”
Awarded hospitals may use this funding to retain physicians, nurses, and other healthcare providers, allowing hospitals to preserve essential services, including emergency, inpatient, and other critical healthcare services. This support helps ensure rural communities can continue to access affordable care when and where they need it.
A complete list of award recipients and more information about the program is available at Rural Hospital Provider Support Program FY 2026 Grant Awards.
Learn more about HRSA’s rural health programs.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Roberto Kury Pesantes, Ecuadorian Foreign Minister of Human Mobility

Palacio de Carondelet

Quito, Ecuador

September 10, 2026

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We are receiving Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America, and also Roberto Kury Pesantes, the Foreign Minister of Ecuador. Ladies and gentlemen, dear authorities, representatives from the press that are here with us today, please, everybody be welcome to this joint press release on behalf of Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America and Roberto Kury Pesantes, Foreign Minister of Ecuador. In this space we will be able to share the main findings of this day.

Now we would like to invite Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, Foreign Minister of Human Mobility of Ecuador.

FOREIGN MINISTER KURY: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon to all of the representatives of the press that are here with us today. For us it’s an absolute honor to be hosting you and hosting the second official visit on behalf of the Secretary of State of the United States, Marco Rubio. This visit is not only a very important diplomatic milestone, but it also reflects the excellent moment that Ecuador and the United States are undergoing jointly with our administrations; and overall, it is a very clear example that we are sharing a common vision – a vision that is focused on security; that is focused on liberty, on democracy, and overall on shared prosperity.

I would like to structure my presentation in three axes, which is something that we constantly work with the United States. One is the issue related to safety – our shared safety and security, focused on fighting against transnational threats, and also the threats that we are confronting right now are not only local; they know no boundaries. And in the same way we do need to tackle them in a way that is multinational and coordinated not only locally.

Ecuador has assumed a very firm, brave, and decisive role in the region to try to break down these criminal organizations and drug-dealing bands that try to cause harm to our families and to our peace and to our institutions. Therefore, technical operation and political support are fundamental parts of the puzzle for this effort, and today we want to restate that the institutional strength and the exchange of intelligence, the strengthening of our capabilities, are the only way forward in order to be able to bring back the absolute peace for our peoples.

Secondly, I would also like to mention the issue related to economy. Sustainable peace cannot be sustained only through security and safety, but it is also very necessary to have economic development, employment, and real opportunities for our people. Therefore, Ecuador has positioned itself as a strategic partner that is trustworthy, that opens the door for hemispheric trade in different sectors in order to be able to jointly work with the United States of America.

And finally, the third axis I would like to sum up: that this is a partnership not only at the diplomatic level, and it’s not a short-term partnership; our relationship with the United States is envisioned to be lasting because our nations go beyond a simple political moment. They share democratic values and the commitment for the well-being of our nations. This visit on behalf of Secretary Rubio allows us to create a pragmatic roadmap, and a very ambitious roadmap, for the upcoming years, ensuring that our political dialogue can be translated into tangible results for each and every one of our citizens and our region.

Dear Secretary, your presence here in our Ecuadorian soil really ratifies that not only are we working hand in hand, but also that we are working for a better future for both nations. Be confident that in us you will find a country that is a loyal ally, an active ally, and a decisive ally to be able to build a safer hemisphere, a free hemisphere, and prosperous hemisphere. Thank you very much.

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear Foreign Minister. Now we would like to invite the intervention of Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State of the United States of America.

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much for this opportunity to be here with you again. A year and three days ago I came; this is my second official visit as the Secretary of State, and my third visit, because I came as a senator before as well. And we will see ourselves in September for sure once again, or in – even closer than next September. And thank you very much for this opportunity.

The partnership between the United States and Ecuador – I’m going to share some words in English as well, just so that people don’t get offended with me, as well for my press, English-speaking press that we have from the United States.

But first of all I would like to say that this partnership between – of our countries is very important. We do not have a better ally in the region with regards to confronting the big threat of criminal transnational organizations. It’s criminal transnational organization that has changed over the last few years. We had been used to criminal groups that cooperated within a national boundary, but now we see networks of terrorist organizations. Let’s not call them criminal groups; they’re terrorist groups that are attacking country after country, threatening the state, the well-being, the health, and the safety of our people. And in order to be able to discuss transnational issues we have to create a coalition of countries. And one of the countries that has participated most actively and is doing the most to confront this is Ecuador, and that’s why we’re here with you today.

And we’re doing a lot of things together. Our elite forces are working jointly on a day-to-day basis in a way that has no precedence in order to try to dismantle these terrorist organizations which are causing so much harm to this country, to our country, and to plenty of other countries in our region. At the same time, we have worked – and I’m going to ask the United States Congress for 45 additional million dollars – to continue contributing towards this effort of dismantling these terrorist groups and finishing with them once and for all.

At the same time, we are launching a $10 million effort in order to be able to tackle illegal mining that is stealing the riches of your country. They should be towards the benefit of people, not towards the benefit of a terrorist group. And we will also start with that initiative. I want to announce that we are giving a fleet from the U.S. Coast Guard here to Ecuador so that they are able to use it. It’s a 110-feet vessel. And on top of that, we will transfer five more interceptor vessels in the upcoming months. We will have a total of 12 total vessels – 12 of them – over the last year.

And we also want to say that the results are evident. You have been able to have your interventions and have been able to see a historical numbers of seizures of drugs over the last year, which is something that was previously never before seen. I must say that as part of the effort, the administration of – President Trump’s administration has sanctioned 15 entities – criminal organizations, terrorist organizations, and also two individual people. And we have identified 10 commercial fishing companies, and we – that were also participating in illegal actions. And this is very important; we continue working on this.

And today, we have made the decision on behalf of the United States Government to designate Los Tiguerones as another terrorist group, and this is on top of the things that we have done with Los Choneros and with Los Lobos and other groups that are not coming up to my mind at this point in time. But yeah, it was the three additional groups, and today with the Tiguerones as well.

These criminal groups – and I’m going to repeat what I said before because it’s very important for us to highlight this. We’re not talking about mafia, normal mafia. We’re not talking about criminals. We’re talking about terrorists – terrorists that in many cases have weapons and equipment that is very similar to those from armies of certain countries. These are not common groups. They participate in common crime, of course, but they have capabilities beyond that. They’re terrorist groups. And that is something that we have to confront, we have to dismantle, and we have to beat them. And we are fully committed for that.

At the same time, we have also worked on economic issues. There’s huge economic opportunities. The number one responsibility of government is the safety of the people in the country, but beyond that we do need to have prosperity, economic opportunities. And there are huge economic opportunities. Your economy is growing. It’s growing at a very impressive level, but it could even take that step further. It could accelerate even further for the benefit of the people. And we are trying to find what opportunities exist, and we know that there’s plenty of them so that United States economy and Ecuadorian economy can participate jointly to create this prosperity, which would help both countries.

So with all of this, we are fully committed – 100 percent committed – and I wanted to come here as part of this official visit to add this and to keep on working on all of these things, and to have very concrete achievements like the ones we have obtained over the last year. Because oftentimes, when you come on these visits, we say and we talk about what we will do, but we have already done things, and we will even work harder. And hopefully next time we’re here we will have many more achievements that we can talk about, and also we will still have a lot to do.

So thank you very much for that, and I’m going to share a couple of words in English.

(In English) Just in English, first of all, I want to thank the foreign minister; I want to thank President Noboa and their administration. They’ve been incredible partners. They’re a key leader in the Shield of the Americas and in the Counter Cartel Coalition, the American – Americas Counter Cartel Coalition. In fact, they are the most involved and aggressive partner we have in that regard.

Our – as we speak right now, our elite forces are operating jointly, going after criminal groups, dismantling narco networks, and bringing people to justice that had never been brough to justice before. And I think it’s important to point for a second that the groups we are taking on, these are terrorist organizations. These are not just criminal organizations. These are not just narco organizations. These are terrorist organizations. They have to be confronted, and they have to be dismantled. And that’s what we’re working on together in a way that really has no precedent, and we’re going to be doing more.

For example, we’ll be asking Congress for another $45 million of new commitments to help Ecuador, working with us, to take this effort on. We’re going to be asking for $10 million as well, or we’re going to be launching an initiative – $10 million of approved projects to go after illegal gold mining and gang recruitment and illicit finance and land and maritime drug trafficking.

I’m pleased to announce today that, as part of this effort, we’ll be delivering a 110-foot U.S. Coast Guard cutter to Ecuador so that that will help strengthen their navy and their ability to stop maritime narcotic trafficking and weapons shipments and illegal fishing, and a range of other threats. And we’re going to do more than just that. Next month, we’ll be transferring five more interceptor vessels. That’ll bring to a total of 12 this year – 12 this year.

Again, the progress we’ve made on this relationship really has no historic precedent, and there’s so much more to do. And the results are there. You see it already. I was just told this before we got here today that the Ecuadorian navy has seized 2.5 metric tons of cocaine using these vessels that we were able to provide. They’re doing their part, and we’re going to continue to do ours.

By the way, we’ve sanctioned a network of 15 entities and individuals and identified 10 commercial fishing vessels as blocked property. These are things that were being used to facilitate narcotrafficking and other things. Now, today we’ll be designating a new group and another group as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, a group known as Los Tiguerones . And this comes on the heels of our designation of three other groups, including Los Lobos and Los Choneros, in July.

These are organizations – as I said, they’re not ordinary. These are violent, bloodthirsty terrorist organizations, and we have to make sure that we continue to pursue them. And as we dismantle these terrorist organizations, we also have to go after corrupt officials that collaborate and conspire with these terrorists. We’ll be announcing the designation of seven former members of the government here, officials, for accepting bribes and for betraying their most essential duties on behalf of – and they did this on behalf of these terrorist organizations, these dangerous criminal groups.

There was so much more for us to do. We’ve signed a bilateral critical minerals framework earlier this year to collaborate on price challenges and to spur development. We’re going to kick off our Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact with Ecuador. We’re providing a 12 million grant to the Government of Ecuador for this compact, which is going to benefit the electricity sector and your economy.

And in the end, obviously the most important obligation any government has is the safety and security of their people. But upon that foundation is where you build the foundation of prosperity and economic opportunity. Ecuador actually has economic growth, and it’s pretty impressive given some of the things that are going on around the world. But they can do so much more if the security situation gets solved – and it is being solved very aggressively – and if we work together to pursue these opportunities to jointly develop our respective economies in ways that are mutually beneficial for both countries.

So thank you very much. Muchísimas gracias .

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, Secretary. We would like to thank the presence of the authorities, the representatives of the press, and also of everybody that has been here with us today. We would like to specially request the press to please stay in your position until the authorities leave. Good afternoon, everybody, and thank you.

September 10, 2026: EMR USA CEO Joe Balzano (second from left) gives tour of Camden recycling plant to Rep. Norcross, Rep. Pallone, and Mayor Carstarphen (left to right)

CAMDEN — Congressmen Donald Norcross (NJ-01) and Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today met with representatives from EMR’s Camden recycling plant and local elected officials to discuss the nationwide issue of lithium battery fires.

Lithium batteries contain more power and charge faster than other batteries, but those efficiencies can also create a fire hazard if exposed to physical damage or excess heat. While these risks require special disposal processes, many consumers are unaware when they are disposing lithium batteries and recycling facilities are often underequipped to identify them in the waste stream. As such, there are an estimated 5,000 fires at recycling plants in the United States each year, with most being ignited by improperly disposed lithium batteries.

Without action the problem will only continue to grow: Lithium batteries are used in a large amount of modern products such as handheld electronics, e-cigarettes, medical devices, and the total amount of lithium consumption nearly quadrupled between just 2010 and 2021. Municipalities from coast to coast, including Camden, are increasingly being forced to respond to large battery fires.

“Lithium batteries aren’t going away, and communities are struggling to safely recycle them across the world. Reducing these fires will take a team effort, and the producers of these batteries need to play a more active role – especially since they know what happens to these batteries at the end of their lifecycle,” Norcross said. “There’s no one silver bullet solution, but my visit with Congressman Pallone and folks on the frontlines here in Camden certainly helps me feel that more people are taking this issue seriously.”

“Lithium-ion batteries shouldn’t be turning recycling facilities into fire hazards. When these batteries end up where they don’t belong, they can put entire communities at risk. I came to Camden with Congressman Norcross to see the problem firsthand and figure out what we can do in Congress to prevent these fires before they start,” said Pallone, the top Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, which has jurisdiction over the issue.

“Everyone wants to ensure that fires of this magnitude never occur,” Victor Carstarphen, mayor of Camden said. “I commend Congressman Norcross for looking at potential solutions to this issue and for working with local officials to help safeguard against the threat of a future event. Improving federal regulations and requiring standardized labeling of materials would be a positive step forward.”

“Recyclers everywhere are reckoning with the risks that lithium batteries pose to the waste stream, and no one has more stake in preventing these fires than the hardworking men and women staffing these facilities in their own communities,” Joe Balzano, chief executive officer of EMR USA said. “EMR appreciates the leaders who came to Camden today to see the issue up close – and for elevating the need for solutions about what can be done about this national problem.”

Multiple efforts have been launched this Congress to prevent lithium battery fires. In October, Norcross introduced the Battery Fire Prevention Act, which includes measures to boost recycling facilities’ access to battery detectors and create a lithium battery buyback fund. Earlier this month, the House Energy and Commerce Committee also advanced the Battery Recycling for America’s Competitive Economy (BRACE) Act – legislation that would modernize and clarify regulations and safeguards for lithium battery storage and recycling.
title: Norcross, Pallone, Camden leaders meet to discuss nationwide lithium battery fires

LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) joined a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to block President Trump’s executive order that would require states to provide a citizenship verification list to the Department of Homeland Security and give the Postal Service control over who can vote by mail. Millions of Americans utilize mail-in voting including deployed service members, seniors, and disabled Americans. Trump himself voted by mail last month.

“The right to vote is a critical pillar of our democracy,” said Schneider. “Every single American deserves the opportunity to cast their ballot how they wish – whether that is in-person or by mail. This executive order is a blatant attempt to sow doubt in the integrity of our elections and disenfranchise eligible voters.

“Trump’s continued attacks on mail-in voting are un-American and anti-democratic. I’m glad to join a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former lawmakers to urge the Court to stand up for the right to vote and stand against any and all attacks that undermine this sacred right,” Schneider concluded. “We will continue fighting to protect free and fair elections for everyone.”
title: SCHNEIDER JOINS BIPARTISAN GROUP OF OVER 250 CURRENT AND FORMER MEMBERS OF CONGRESS URGING THE SUPREME COURT TO BLOCK TRUMP’S EXECUTIVE ORDER LIMITING VOTING BY MAIL

CHICAGO — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), author of the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act and a Vice Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus, today joined Illinois Department of Human Services Secretary Dulce Quintero, The Trevor Project, NAMI Chicago, Equality Illinois, and other mental health and LGBTQ+ advocates for a roundtable and press conference calling on Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump Administration to restore specialized 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline services for LGBTQ+ young people.

“When an LGBTQ+ person reaches out for help in a moment of crisis, they should be able to reach a counselor trained to understand what they are going through,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “Press 3 provided that lifesaving support, and the Trump Administration shut it down. I worked with partners from both parties to secure $33.1 million for the program and directed the Administration to restore these lifesaving services. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. needs to turn Press 3 back on and make sure every LGBTQ+ person, including transgender young people, can get the help they need when they need it most.”

During the roundtable at NAMI Chicago, participants discussed efforts to restore Press 3 and strengthen crisis support in Illinois. The state is working with The Trevor Project to train general 988 counselors in LGBTQ+ crisis competency while the specialized federal service remains unavailable.

Congress directed $33.1 million in Fiscal Year 2026 funding toward restoring the specialized services. In June, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Department acknowledged in a response to a bipartisan request led by Krishnamoorthi that Congress had directed the services to be restored, but said it was still assessing implementation while seeking to comply with Executive Order 14168. Krishnamoorthi has also introduced the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act to permanently protect the specialized services and require HHS to reserve at least 9 percent of annual 988 funding for them.
title: Krishnamoorthi Joins Illinois Mental Health and LGBTQ+ Leaders in Push to Restore 988 “Press 3” Crisis Services

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Alma S. Adams, Ph.D. (NC-12), and Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced the Higher Education Oversight for Nonprofits Ensuring Standards and Transparency Act, or the HONEST Act, to establish new safeguards for IRS investigations of colleges and universities.

The bill comes as the Department of the Treasury and IRS move forward with new regulations affecting the tax-exempt status of private schools, including colleges and universities. Under the new proposal, as many as 18,000 schools could be affected, along with roughly 750,000 students who receive scholarships tied to race, ethnicity, or national origin. The rule would reach beyond admissions to scholarships, student programs, and other policies that colleges use to serve their students.

“I spent 40 years as a professor, and I know our colleges and universities should not have to worry about the IRS being used as a political weapon,” said Congresswoman Adams,Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development. “The HONEST Act does not prevent the IRS from enforcing the law, it simply ensures a fair and transparent process before the federal government investigates a college or university.”

“Like other institutions, colleges and universities in the United States are entitled to ‘Due Process,’ the two most beautiful words in the English language,” said Rep. Jamie Raskin (MD-08). “I am glad to partner with Representative Adams to introduce the HONEST Act, which preserves important federal tax investigation authorities while ensuring that colleges and universities get the same Due Process protection as houses of worship receive.”

The HONEST Act mirrors protections that already exist for churches and houses of worship, where the IRS must follow added procedures before opening certain tax inquiries. The bill would bring a similar process to colleges and universities, adding due process without taking away the IRS’s ability to hold schools accountable when they break the law.

The legislation is endorsed by the American Council on Education (ACE), the American Association of State Colleges and Universities (AASCU), the National Association of Independent Colleges and Universities (NAICU), and the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities (APLU).

“The American Council on Education, the major coordinating body for the nation’s colleges and universities, with nearly1,600 member institutions, related associations, and other organizations in America and abroad, strongly endorses the HONEST Act,” said a representative of the American Council on Education. “The HONEST Act creates strong guardrails to protect our nation’s colleges and universities, both public and private nonprofit institutions, from the misuse of federal tax-exempt oversight authority by the Department of the Treasury and the IRS. This bill would make important enhancements to protections already in law and we hope it will be swiftly taken up and passed by the full Congress.”

“Nonprofit organizations, including institutions of higher education, have had their tax-exempt status threatened for no more than failure to operate in accordance with prevailing administrative orthodoxy,” said Dr. Charles L. Welch, President & CEO of the AASCU. “Colleges and universities must be able to carry out their missions—advancing academic achievement, research, and workforce preparation—without concern that lawful operations could trigger punitive action. The HONEST Act provides important safeguards to ensure transparency, consistency, and fairness in oversight of nonprofit institutions.”

The HONEST Act would:

Protect academic decisions from being used as a reason for an IRS investigation: The IRS cannot target a school based solely on its curriculum, accreditation, or other academic policies unless there is a violation of federal law.

Make the IRS explain why it is investigating a school: A senior Treasury official must document evidence of a clear tac regulation violation an inquiry begins.

Give the school a chance to respond: Colleges and universities must be told what the IRS is looking at and have an opportunity to meet with the agency.

Put a time limit on investigations: IRS examinations generally must be finished within two years.

Stop the IRS from repeatedly reopening the same issue: After a clean review, the IRS generally cannot come back on the same issue for five years.

Require another level of review before serious action is taken: The IRS cannot revoke tax-exempt status or take certain other enforcement actions without additional internal approval.

Require Congress to be notified: Treasury must report these investigations to the House and Senate tax-writing committees.

Apply the protections to public colleges and certain university foundations and endowments.

A one pager for the bill can be found here.
title: Reps. Adams, Raskin Introduce HONEST Act to Protect Colleges from Politically Motivated IRS Investigations

HUD Announces Sponsors and Exhibitors for 2026 Innovative Housing Showcase
Showcase Returns to National Mall September 22–24 to Celebrate American Ingenuity
September 10, 2026
WASHINGTON – HUD today announced the sponsors and exhibitors for its sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, taking place on the National Mall from September 22–24. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlights American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, HUD is bringing the public and private sectors together to advance bold, practical solutions for housing affordability,” said Secretary Turner. “This Showcase is a powerful reminder of what is possible when free enterprise, American grit, and strong public-private partnerships come together to make the American Dream of homeownership a reality. I am grateful to our incredible sponsors and exhibitors for bringing this experience to the National Mall and giving Americans an opportunity to experience firsthand the innovation emerging across our nation.”
The 2026 sponsors include International Code Council (ICC), Manufactured Housing Institute (MHI), National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), Rocket, and Structural Building Components Association (SBCA).
“The Showcase highlights solutions that deliver the safe and affordable housing Americans need,” said John Belcik, Chief Executive Officer of the International Code Council (ICC). “The International Code Council is thrilled to support the Showcase again this year to demonstrate how building codes protect people, save money, drive innovation, and ultimately help families achieve the American Dream.”
“MHI is pleased to again partner with HUD for the 2026 Innovative Housing Showcase at a historic moment for manufactured housing,” said Dr. Lesli Gooch, Chief Executive Officer of the Manufactured Housing Institute (MHI). “As we celebrate the 50th anniversary of the HUD Code, the manufactured homes on display will showcase the next generation of housing innovation and the transformative potential of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, legislation that will help unlock greater design flexibility and expand housing supply. We are grateful for HUD's leadership and encouraged by Congress' embrace of manufactured housing as an essential part of the nation's housing supply strategy. Together, we are making homeownership attainable for more Americans and delivering high-quality housing options to communities across the country.”
“The National Association of Home Builders is proud to be a returning sponsor for the 2026 Innovative Housing Showcase,” said Bill Owens, Chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB). “This is an incredible opportunity to highlight the innovations happening in our industry. Our nation is facing a housing affordability crisis, and the technologies and products that are presented during this Showcase can be a part of the solution.”
“From Rocket Mortgage to Redfin, Rocket is committed to helping everyone home through innovation in homeownership,” said Hilary Halpern, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs at Rocket. “We are proud to support the Innovative Housing Showcase and especially encouraged by recent policy advances that recognize the important role manufactured housing can play in addressing affordability and supply.”
“SBCA is proud to again sponsor and exhibit at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase,” said Molly Butz, Managing Director of the Structural Building Components Association (SBCA). “We believe in the value of bringing the housing industry together in a setting where people can see solutions firsthand, exchange ideas, and better understand the many ways we can work together to address housing needs across the country. This year’s ‘Made in America’ theme makes that especially meaningful for our members, who manufacture structural building components, such as roof trusses, floor trusses, and wall panels, in communities nationwide and are part of the housing supply chain every day. The Showcase is a unique opportunity to connect that work with the broader conversation around innovation, affordability, and housing supply, and we’re pleased to continue supporting it.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase will spotlight American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The showcase will feature a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.

WASHINGTON, DC (September 10, 2026) — Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) and Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-04) sent a letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Administrator Sean McMaster opposing the removal of programs for road safety, specifically those mentioning bike safety.

In the letter, the Congressmembers wrote, “The U.S. is experiencing a roadway safety crisis, with more than 36,000 people killed on our streets in 2025. One in five traffic deaths is a person walking or biking. Since 2010, bicyclist fatalities in the U.S. have risen by 87 percent.”

“The removal of several PSCM related to protecting vulnerable road users coincides with the USDOT’s recent cancellation of grants that include bicycling facilities and stated intention to limit funding for bike lanes within the Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) Grant Program. Ignoring multimodal transportation networks, rejecting projects that prioritize the safety of people biking and walking, and eliminating funding for bike lanes goes against the express congressional intent for these funding sources. Furthermore, DOT’s actions only make our roads less safe for American families,” continued the lawmakers. “We therefore strongly urge you to restore all PSCM pages recently removed from the FHWA website, as well as funding eligibility for bike projects within BUILD and any other grant program for which they are eligible. Please provide us with a written response to explain the Administration’s rationale, your process for these actions, and how these actions support the Department’s mission to “Advance safety.””

The letter was signed by 28 Democratic lawmakers, including: Reps. Rick Larsen (WA-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Betty McCollum (MN-04), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Andre Carson (IN-07), Dina Titus (NV-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Dave Min (CA-47), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Jim Himes (CT-04), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) and Sara Jacobs (CA-51).

“My granddaughter Allie was just five years old when she was killed riding her bike through a crosswalk near her home,” said Philip Hart, a Durham resident and constituent of Rep. Foushee. “Every proven safety countermeasure removed from FHWA's website risks costing lives that could otherwise have been saved. Families for Safe Streets was founded by people who buried loved ones killed by dangerous road design — we know firsthand that these aren't abstract policy debates, they're the difference between a child making it home from school on a bike lane and a family getting a knock on the door. We're grateful to Representatives Thompson and Foushee for standing up for the data-backed tools that save lives, and we urge the Department of Transportation to restore this guidance and the funding that puts it into practice.”

“Bike lanes, road diets, and speed management are called Proven Safety Countermeasures because the evidence is clear: they work to improve safety for everyone. Whether you are walking, biking, taking transit, or in a car, these are safety interventions that save lives. Removing these Proven Safety Countermeasures from engineers' and planners' toolbox signals that this administration is putting political whims over the safety of Americans,” said Bill Nesper, Executive Director of the League of American Bicyclists.

“Rails To Trails Conservancy thanks Representatives Foushee and Thompson for their leadership organizing this letter and standing up for the vast majority of Americans who support trails, walking, and biking infrastructure. Removing the proven safety countermeasures endangers bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers, and denies decades of research and experience in all types of American communities. By limiting funding for bicycle projects through the BUILD program, USDOT is undercutting bipartisan Congressional intent and denying Americans the infrastructure they need to safely and affordably get where they need to go,” said Scott Goldstein, Senior Director of Government Relations of Rails To Trails Conservancy.

“One of The 6 E’s of Safe Routes to School is evaluation: using evidence-based strategies to improve safety and get kids and families where they need to go. Proven Safety Countermeasures have been rigorously evaluated to show they keep kids and families safe on our roadways,” said Marisa Jones, Executive Director of Safe Routes Partnership. “We encourage FHWA to follow the evidence on what keeps kids and communities safe, and reinstate all Proven Safety Countermeasures. No family should mourn the death of a child on our roadways over the politics of transportation modes. Communities need every tool available to them to make American streets safer for kids and families.”
title: Reps. Foushee, Thompson Lead Opposition to Removal of Bike Safety Resources and Bike Safety Project Funding

Today, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon issued a nationwide call to action, urging K-12 educators across the country to set aside time tomorrow to honor the victims and heroes of the September 11th terrorist attacks on its 25th anniversary.
In her message to teachers and education leaders, the Secretary highlighted the importance of ensuring younger generations understand the history, the profound loss, and the extraordinary courage that shaped the nation’s response. As today’s students were born long after the attacks, Secretary McMahon encouraged schools to help bridge this gap through thoughtful, age‑appropriate civic instruction.
“A quarter century has passed since that terrible day, but we must never forget what September 11th means for the United States,” wrote U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “This year, I call on American schools to educate students with moral clarity about the events of that day and its significance for the Nation’s history. Educators can achieve this by incorporating an age-appropriate lesson about 9/11, a moment of silence to mark the time the first plane struck the World Trade Center, or by asking students to share their own reflections about that tragic day.”
Secretary McMahon prompted educators to ground lessons in the real stories of individuals whose courage continues to define the legacy of 9/11 — such as the passengers of United Flight 93, Welles Crowther (the “Man in the Red Bandana”), and Lieutenant Colonel Marilyn Wills.
To bring classrooms across the country together in remembrance, the Secretary invited every school to participate in a moment of silence tomorrow. This observance honors the 2,977 victims, the heroic first responders, the service members who gave their lives in the years that followed, and the families who continue to carry their legacy forward.
title: Secretary of Education Linda McMahon Issues a Nationwide Call to Commemorate the 25th Anniversary of the 9/11 Terrorist Attacks with America’s Students

Hawaii Couple Sentenced to Prison for Roles in Nationwide Tax Refund Fraud Conspiracy
A Hawaii husband and wife were sentenced yesterday to 16 months and 24 months in prison, respectively, for their roles in a nationwide tax fraud scheme that involved deceiving the IRS into issuing a nearly $200,000 tax refund and then using shell bank accounts and frivolous legal filings to prevent the government from getting it back.
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, from approximately February 2015 through November 2018, Beverly Braumuller-Hawver and Scott Hawver, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii, engaged in a fraudulent tax refund scheme by paying a promoter a series of fees in exchange for fraudulent tax paperwork. Armed with those materials, the Hawvers filed an amended 2014 tax return attaching a fabricated IRS Form 1099-MISC — a document that falsely claimed a mortgage company had paid Hawver $749,163 in income and withheld $424,163 of that amount in federal taxes. The fictitious withholding claim prompted the IRS to issue the Hawvers a tax refund for $192,845 that they were not entitled to receive.
The Hawvers moved quickly to put the money out of the government’s reach. They deposited the U.S. Treasury check into a newly opened bank account. Within days, they transferred $170,000 into a separate account held in the name of BeverlyB Music LLC, an unrelated music business the Hawvers operated. On that same day, the Hawvers paid co-conspirators more than $70,000 from the BeverlyB Music account for their roles in the scheme. Braumuller-Hawver later wired $22,000 from that account to a jeweler to purchase gold and silver coins. When the IRS began seeking to recover the fraudulent refund, the Hawvers did not simply ignore the notices. Instead, they sent scripted, frivolous correspondence to the IRS, filed a petition in U.S. Tax Court to thwart collection and participated as plaintiffs in multiple frivolous civil RICO lawsuits against IRS employees who were doing their jobs.
In March 2026, a federal jury convicted Braumuller-Hawver and Hawver of conspiring to defraud the IRS. The jury also convicted Braumuller-Hawver of filing a false tax return and money laundering.
In addition to the term of imprisonment, Chief District Judge Derrick K. Watson ordered Beverly Braumuller-Hawver and Scott Hawver to jointly and severally pay $182,438.37 to the United States in restitution.
Along with the Hawvers, the Department of Justice has prosecuted a number of other defendants involved in a nationwide tax fraud scheme that drew in more than 200 participants across at least 19 states. In 2022, the main promoters of the scheme were sentenced to 11 years in prison, more than 8 years in prison, and 51 months in prison. In Hawaii, the scheme was organized and led by Rosemarie Lastimado-Dradi, who marketed the operation as the “Escrow Trust Refund” program, recruited clients (including the Hawvers) and directed her cut of their fraudulent refunds — between 25 and 40 percent — into accounts held in the name of fictitious business entities and purported trusts. In January 2026, Lastimado-Dradi was sentenced to a total of 9 years in prison. Other Hawaii participants in the scheme have also received significant sentences, including Elvah Miranda (48 months in prison), Marciaminajuanequita Dumlao (33 months in prison), Daniel Miranda (30 months in prison), Brigida Chock (27 months in prison) and Lazerrick Lawrence (20 months in prison).
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Kenneth M. Sorenson for the District of Hawaii made the announcement
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case.
Trial Attorney Megan L. Jones and former trial attorney Sarah A. Kiewlicz of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Hawaii Couple Sentenced to Prison for Roles in Nationwide Tax Refund Fraud Conspiracy

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Celebrates Launch of Federal eVTOL Pilot Program in Texas to Unlock the Future of Flight
Experimental commercial flights were made possible by the Department’s first-of-its-kind testing initiative
FORT WORTH, TX — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy was in Texas today to celebrate the state’s first demonstration of its next-generation aircraft under USDOT’s Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program (eIPP)–making Texas the sixth location to launch under the Department’s initiative.
Under Secretary Duffy, USDOT has created one of the nation’s largest real-world environments for testing electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOLs), air taxis, and autonomous planes.
The first-of-its-kind testing initiative has the potential to create jobs, connect communities, and strengthen American leadership in aviation. Data from the pilot projects will be used by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale.
Federal officials, industry stakeholders and state leaders gathered to watch demonstrations of BETA Technologies’ ALIA electric aircraft and Joby Aviation’s S4 eVTOL
“Under President Trump, we are unlocking the future of flight and empowering innovators to build and test these exciting aircraft here in the U.S.,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “Today marks another critical step in our work to reshape how people and products move faster and more efficiently.”
The demonstrations at Perot Field Fort Worth Alliance Airport (AFW) were the first in Texas sponsored under eIPP, which partnered BETA, Joby, and the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) to develop regional air taxi flights connecting Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, and eventually Houston.
On Saturday, Joby’s aircraft will fly a roundtrip flight from AFW to Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) to test flight operations between major airports. TxDOT and other eIPP participants are planning additional test flights through the rest of the year.
“Advanced Air Mobility vehicles are the future of aviation and these demonstrations in Texas are critical to getting us there,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “The FAA is leveraging data from test flights in Texas and across the country to ensure these new aircraft integrate safely into the airspace.”
"In Texas, we don't wait for the future to arrive, we build it. The Lone Star State is pushing the boundaries by testing the next generation of aircraft through Project Nexus. I want to thank President Trump and Secretary Duffy for their leadership and decisive action,” said Senator and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation Ted Cruz (R-Texas). “These technologies will connect communities, expand access to jobs and services, and strengthen supply chains. What starts in Texas will help shape the future of aviation throughout the entire country."
“We’re proud to lead the way in transportation innovation as we look to find new ways to connect the people of Texas,” said TxDOT Executive Director Marc Williams. “Project Nexus is a first-of-its-kind opportunity to gather real-world data, improve safety and build a framework for how electric aircraft could one day connect people, goods and communities across the state.”
“We began pursuing our vision at Joby in 2009. After thousands of hours of flight testing, and with the eIPP program supporting us, we’re now ready for our industry to take off,” said Joby Aviation Founder and CEO JoeBen Bevirt. “We’re grateful to the White House and Department of Transportation for bringing government, industry and communities together as we make electric vertical flight a reality. We’re proud to be demonstrating the future of flight here in Texas and bringing American innovation to communities across our nation.”
“eIPP is about putting these aircraft to work and learning from real operations,” said BETA Technologies Founder and CEO Kyle Clark. “In Texas, we are working with our partners to move cargo and medical supplies, support disaster response and offshore operations, and understand what it takes to make these missions work at scale. The best way to build this industry is to get out there and fly. Programs like this are how we prove the technology, build the infrastructure around it, and make sure the U.S. continues to lead in aviation.”
"eIPP is how we turn years of flight testing into real-world operations, and Texas is a critical part of that path for Archer as we prepare to bring Midnight to communities across the country," said Founder and CEO of Archer Aviation Adam Goldstein. "We're grateful to Secretary Duffy and the FAA for building a program that lets industry and government move at the same speed."
Additional Information:
In March, Secretary Duffy unveiled the eIPP program to begin testing advanced air mobility vehicles and their real-world applications. The eight selected projects span 26 states and partner with leading aircraft manufacturers, operators, and state partners, including:
- Urban air taxi services
- Regional passenger transportation (including short Takeoff and Landing aircraft)
- Cargo and logistics networks
- Emergency medical response operations
- Autonomous flight technologies
- Offshore and energy-sector transportation
The eIPP is a first-of-its-kind initiative outlined in President Trump’s Unleashing Drone Dominance Executive Order. It creates one of the nation’s largest real-world testing environments for next-generation aircraft with the potential to create jobs, connect communities, and strengthen American leadership in aviation.
Together, these pilot projects will create one of the largest real-world testing environments for next generation aircraft in the world. In addition to offering the American people an exciting window into the future of aviation, data from the pilot projects will be used by the FAA to develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale.
Last year, Secretary Duffy and the FAA launched the nation’s first-ever advanced air mobility (AAM) strategy to unlock the future of flight. The Strategy and accompanying action plan outline 40 recommendations to safely and efficiently support AAM operations.

Letter Comes Amidst Alarming Spike in Possible Modern-Day Lynchings

“Inaction by the federal government is tantamount to complicity. This is part of the legacy of racial terror in the United States, and this neglect has long-term consequences.”

Text of Letter (PDF)

BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) led 59 colleagues in writing to the Department of Justice (DOJ) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) demanding a thorough, transparent, and comprehensive federal investigation into the numerous incidents of Black people found hanging across the country. The Congresswoman’s letter follows a series of deaths which raise suspicion of foul play given the role of lynching in American history.

The growing number of Black people found hanging in public is a national crisis. A recent report documented more than 70 modern-day lynchings in the United States between 2000 and 2025. In 2026 alone, there have already been at least 10 reported hangings of Black people. They were as young as 18 years old and lived in different parts of the country, including Mississippi, Michigan, and New York. Many families have publicly questioned the conclusions of local and state investigations.

“Inaction by the federal government is tantamount to complicity. This is part of the legacy of racial terror in the United States, and this neglect has long-term consequences,” the lawmakers continued. “Not only are innocent lives lost, but lynching inflicts deep traumatic and psychological wounds on family members, neighbors, and the entire Black community.”

“Congress enacted the Emmett Till Antilynching Act in 2022 to ensure the DOJ and FBI are empowered to fully investigate suspicious deaths and hold individuals accountable,” the lawmakers continued. “It is incumbent upon you to do just that.”

This letter demands a thorough, transparent, and comprehensive federal investigation into every hanging death of a Black individual across the United States. At a minimum, each investigation, with permission of the decedents’ families, should include an independent autopsy, an audit of local and state law enforcement investigations, review of physical and testimonial evidence, and a final report submitted to Congress explaining the agency’s findings. The letter also calls for robust data collection that tracks the hanging deaths of Black people in a transparent and systematic manner.

Joining Congresswoman Pressley in sending the letter are Representatives Alma Adams, Yassamin Ansari, Becca Balint, Nanette Diaz Barragán, Joyce Beatty, Wesley Bell, Sanford Bishop, Everton Blair, Brendan Boyle, Shontel Brown, Janelle Bynum, André Carson, Troy Carter, Yvette Clarke, Jasmine Crockett, Mark DeSaulnier, Sarah Elfreth, Jesús “Chuy” García, Sylvia García, Jimmy Gomez, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Jahana Hayes, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Robin Kelly, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Summer Lee, Jennifer McClellan, LaMonica McIver, Gregory Meeks, Analilia Mejía, Christian Menefee, Kweisi Mfume, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Frank Pallone Jr., Mark Pocan, Stacey Plaskett, Delia Ramírez, Terri Sewell, Lateefah Simon, Haley Stevens, Marilyn Strickland, Shri Thanedar, Bennie Thompson, Rashida Tlaib, Ritchie Torres, Lauren Underwood, Nydia M. Velázquez, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Maxine Waters, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Nikema Williams, and Frederica Wilson.

Full text of the letter is available here.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) reintroduced the Maximizing Opioid Recovery Emergency (MORE) Savings Act to lower costs for the more than 20 million Americans seeking treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD), including life-saving medications and outpatient treatment services. This legislation would eliminate cost-sharing for opioid treatment and recovery support services for people with private insurance, Medicaid, and for people enrolled under a new Medicare pilot program.

“Every family, every community has been scarred by the disease of addiction — and as the Trump Administration systematically strips away affordable healthcare, it is critical that we expand access to treatment and recovery,” Rep. Dean said. “Because of the so-called Big Beautiful Bill, 100,000 Pennsylvanians struggling with substance use disorder, including OUD, lost coverage. The MORE Savings Act will help lower costs so that the more than 20 million Americans seeking treatment can find hope and joy in recovery.”

The MORE Savings Act would require individual and group health insurance plans to cover medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), overdose reversal medications, treatment in outpatient settings, and recovery support services with no cost-sharing for patients. The bill would also establish a 5-year pilot program in 15 states to eliminate cost-sharing under Medicare and provide an enhanced federal match under Medicaid for people accessing treatment and recovery services.

Congresswoman Dean previously introduced the MORE Savings Act in the 118th Congress.

Read the full text of the bill here.

Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.
