WASHINGTON, DC — Como parte de su agenda para priorizar lo básico y atender la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico, el Comisionado Residente, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó al Senado que mantenga en la versión final de la legislación federal de infraestructura de agua varios proyectos y prioridades para Puerto Rico que ya fueron aprobados por la Cámara de Representantes.

Las prioridades ya están incluidas en la versión de la Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos, conocida como el Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) de 2026 de la Cámara de Representantes, que avanzó en comité, y Hernández está trabajando para que se mantengan durante las negociaciones con el Senado y lleguen a la versión final.

“Mi agenda de priorizar lo básico se trata de conseguir resultados en los problemas que afectan a nuestra gente todos los días. Puerto Rico necesita mejor infraestructura de agua, comunidades más protegidas de las inundaciones y acción para nuestras costas. Ya estamos avanzando estas prioridades en la Cámara y ahora estoy trabajando para asegurar que lleguen a la meta,” expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Entre las medidas que el Comisionado Residente busca asegurar se encuentran hasta $75 millones para proyectos de infraestructura de agua y ambiental en Puerto Rico, $10 millones para agua y alcantarillado en Corozal y nuevos estudios de impacto para el proyecto de control de inundaciones del Río Puerto Nuevo en San Juan, de manera que se puedan atender las preocupaciones de las comunidades aledañas.

También está defendiendo nuevos estudios para proyectos de control de inundaciones, protección costera y daños por tormentas en Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja y Yabucoa.

###

Rep. Hernández Pushes Water Projects for Puerto Rico

Resident Commissioner seeks to secure projects for Corozal, San Juan, and seven municipalities as part of his agenda to prioritize the basics

WASHINGTON, DC — As part of his agenda to prioritize the basics and address the water crisis in Puerto Rico, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández asked the Senate to maintain, in the final version of federal water infrastructure legislation, several projects and priorities for Puerto Rico that have already been approved by the House of Representatives.

The priorities are already included in the House version of the Water Resources Development Act, known as the 2026 Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), which advanced in committee, and Hernández is working to ensure they remain during negotiations with the Senate and make it into the final version.

“My agenda to prioritize the basics is about delivering results on the problems that affect our people every day. Puerto Rico needs better water infrastructure, communities better protected from flooding, and action for our coasts. We are already advancing these priorities in the House, and now I am working to make sure they reach the finish line,” said the Resident Commissioner.

Among the measures the Resident Commissioner seeks to secure are up to $75 million for water and environmental infrastructure projects in Puerto Rico, $10 million for water and sewer infrastructure in Corozal, and new impact studies for the Río Puerto Nuevo flood control project in San Juan, so that the concerns of neighboring communities can be addressed.

He is also advocating for new studies for flood control, coastal protection, and storm damage projects in Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja, and Yabucoa.

Washington D.C. - New Dem Members hosted a roundtable with housing policy experts and industry representatives to solicit ideas on what Congress’s next steps should be to address the affordable housing crisis. New Dem Housing, Infrastructure, & Transportation Working Group Chair Norma Torres (CA-35), New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach Salud Carbajal (CA-24) and Housing Task Force Chair Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted the roundtable. They were joined by 14 additional New Dem Members and eight stakeholders for the discussion.

“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was an important step forward, but the lasting impact of this law will depend on how effectively we put it into practice," said Rep. Norma Torres. "It's also critical that we look at what's next, which is why we put together this roundtable to hear from experts, stakeholders, and Coalition Members to kickstart work on further policy changes we need to make homes more affordable for our constituents."

“New Dems are leading the charge to address our nationwide housing crisis. In the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, roughly half of the provisions were sponsored by New Dems or priorities from our Housing Affordability Agenda. While this law represents significant progress, our work is far from complete,” said Rep. Salud Carbajal, New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach. This week’s roundtable gave us an opportunity to engage with housing stakeholders and map out the next steps needed to build on the momentum we’ve created.”

"As Chair of the Housing Task Force, I've seen firsthand how the affordable housing crisis touches every part of our country," saidRep. Emilia Sykes. "We achieved great wins in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, including provisions from my HOMES Act to rein in corporate investors who are pricing working families out of their own neighborhoods. But there's more to do. This roundtable was about listening to the people building, financing, and studying housing every day, so we can turn their expertise into the next set of solutions Congress delivers."

This roundtable continues the discussion around affordable housing solutions following successful passage of the 21st Century Road to Housing Act earlier this year. This landmark housing package contained provisions from 22 New Dem Member-led bills and two New Dem proposals and delivered on many of the key objectives laid out in the New Democrat Coalition’s Housing Affordability Agenda.

New Dem Members’ work to address the affordable housing crisis has become a cornerstone of our efforts this Congress. This roundtable expanded these efforts and was an opportunity for Members and guests to discuss what Congress needs to do next to build more homes quickly, expand access to affordable housing, make it easier for families to finance their homes, and more.

Roundtable guests included:

Lake Coulson, Senior Vice President for Government Affairs and Chief Lobbyist, National Association of Home Builders

Nicole Upano, Assistant Vice President, Housing Policy and Regulatory Affairs, National Apartment Association

Mike Kingsella, Chief Executive Officer, Up for Growth

Dr. Lesli Gooch, CEO, Manufactured Housing Institute

Libby O’Neill, Senior Policy Analyst, National Low Income Housing Coalition

Tina Lee, Manager of Housing Policy, Economic Innovation Group

David Garcia, Deputy Director of Policy, Terner Center at U.C. Berkeley

Elayne Weiss, Senior Policy Advisor, National Association of Realtors

###
title: New Dems Host Stakeholder Roundtable to Address the Affordable Housing Crisis

CHICAGO — Hoy, los miembros del Congreso Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05) y Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) —acompañados por una coalición de funcionarios electos locales, entre ellos la senadora estatal Celina Villanueva, el representante estatal Edgar Gonzalez Jr., la comisionada del condado de Cook Alma Anaya y los concejales Michael Rodriguez y Jessie Fuentes, así como organizaciones defensoras de los inmigrantes como Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) y The Resurrection Project (TRP) — ofrecieron una conferencia de prensa para marcar un año de resistencia frente a la Operación Midway Blitz.

La coalición instó a tomar medidas en materia de reforma migratoria, incluyendo la exigencia de una votación sobre la Ley Sueño y Promesa (Dream and Promise Act), y reclamó plena rendición de cuentas por parte de las autoridades locales y federales —incluida la Fiscal Estatal del condado de Cook— ante la brutalidad y el terror que las acciones de control migratorio del gobierno federal han infligido a las comunidades de toda la región.

“Hace un año, la administración Trump intentó quebrantarnos y arrebatarnos la dignidad enviando a agentes federales enmascarados a nuestra ciudad mediante la Operación Midway Blitz. Fracasaron; en su lugar, nuestra comunidad se unió, alzó la voz y desafió su abuso de poder”, declaró el Congresista Jesús “Chuy” García. “Un año después, estamos más unidos que nunca. Pero la lucha no ha terminado. Los agentes federales enmascarados siguen operando en nuestros vecindarios, y continuaremos exigiendo que se marchen y que los responsables de sus crímenes rindan cuentas. Y lo que es más importante: seguiremos luchando por una reforma migratoria significativa para que ninguna comunidad tenga que volver a sufrir las consecuencias de nuestro sistema migratorio fallido”.

“Conmemoramos el primer aniversario de Midway Blitz, cuando el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) inició una campaña de terror en Chicago. Quienes vivimos ese terror lo tenemos claro: el DHS SIGUE SIENDO la mayor amenaza para nuestra seguridad colectiva”, afirmó la Congresista Delia Ramirez. “Al recuperar la mayoría en el Congreso el próximo año, nuestro dolor, nuestra indignación y nuestras exigencias de justicia deben impulsarnos a una acción que honre a todos aquellos que el DHS nos arrebató; debemos hacer rendir cuentas a CADA fascista que haya permitido la violencia del DHS y se haya beneficiado de ella, así como abolir el ICE y desmantelar el DHS”.

"La 'Operación Midway Blitz' de Donald Trump tenía un único objetivo: aterrorizar a Chicago. Los agentes del ICE y la CBP no fueron tras los peores delincuentes; secuestraron a personas en plena calle, lanzaron gases lacrimógenos contra escuelas primarias y mataron a un padre de dos hijos", declaró el Congresista Mike Quigley. "Lamentablemente, el horror de las políticas migratorias de Trump no terminó con la Operación Midway Blitz. Apenas el mes pasado, asistí a una audiencia de deportación donde vi a niños ante la corte sin sus padres, enfrentándose a una barrera idiomática y teniendo que explicar por qué merecen quedarse en este país. Hay que poner fin a esta crueldad. Estoy más comprometido que nunca a trabajar con mis colegas y con los defensores de derechos para proteger a nuestros vecinos inmigrantes y poner un alto al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) de Trump antes de que causen más daño".

"Un año después de la Operación Midway Blitz, recordamos el daño causado por esta operación autoritaria, pero también honramos a los líderes religiosos, organizadores comunitarios, abogados, educadores y ciudadanos de Chicago que dieron un paso al frente para proteger a sus vecinos y defender los valores que fortalecen a nuestra ciudad", afirmó el Congresista Jonathan Jackson. "Seguiré exigiendo que se rindan cuentas por los abusos cometidos contra los inmigrantes y nuestras comunidades. Me uno a mis colegas del Congreso para reiterar nuestra exigencia de una reforma migratoria integral, basada en la convicción fundamental de que toda persona merece dignidad, equidad y el debido proceso".

“Esta semana se cumple el primer aniversario de la Operación Midway Blitz, y los residentes de Chicago aún se encuentran conmocionados por los horrores que nuestras comunidades se han visto obligadas a enfrentar, mientras agentes enmascarados continúan sembrando el caos en toda la ciudad, deteniendo a innumerables residentes y desmantelando familias sin miramientos”, declaró la Senadora Estatal Celina Villanueva. “Desde que se lanzó la operación el pasado mes de septiembre, las comunidades latinas —especialmente aquellas a las que yo represento— han vivido con miedo constante: temor a salir de sus hogares y a enviar a sus hijos a la escuela. Tras un año de agresiones brutales contra manifestantes, patrullajes en las calles, redadas en nuestros vecindarios y daños a nuestros residentes, ya es hora de exigir rendición de cuentas y justicia a esta administración, no solo para los latinos de Illinois, sino también para todos aquellos afectados por estos actos de odio sin sentido”.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no quebrantó a nuestra comunidad; fortaleció nuestra determinación. Durante un año, nuestras familias inmigrantes, vecinos y organizaciones comunitarias se han mantenido unidos frente al miedo y la intimidación. Seguiremos defendiendo a cada familia y protegiendo el espíritu acogedor que define a nuestra comunidad”, afirmó el Concejal del Distrito 22, Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Ya sean las redadas en apartamentos de South Shore, el tiroteo contra Marimar Martínez en Brighton Park o el asesinato de Silverio Villegas González, ha quedado demostrado que ICE NO nos protege; su función es intimidar a las comunidades de color y deportar a tantas personas como sea posible. Los líderes locales y los políticos deben apoyar a los inmigrantes y hacer cumplir las leyes y políticas por las que nuestras comunidades lucharon para convertir a Illinois en un lugar que dé la bienvenida a todos”, afirmó Lawrence Benitio, director ejecutivo del ICIRR.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no ha terminado; todavía sufrimos las consecuencias de ver cómo miles de vecinos fueron arrancados de nuestra comunidad. Familias separadas. Empleos perdidos. Comunidades desestabilizadas. Sin embargo, a pesar de todo, nuestra comunidad sigue dando la cara y luchando. Nos negamos a permitir que se normalice este terror”, declaró Any Huamami, directora de organización del Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“Hace un año, por estas fechas, nuestras comunidades sufrían el terror provocado por agentes enmascarados; hubo personas secuestradas sin explicación y familias separadas a la fuerza debido a la campaña de control migratorio de esta administración federal. El año pasado nos demostró que todos corríamos el riesgo de ser detenidos simplemente por nuestra apariencia. Las detenciones ilegales se convirtieron en la norma, pero seguimos aquí denunciando esas acciones y recordando a la gente que ICE continúa operando en nuestras comunidades. Es nuestro deber mantenernos alerta y protegernos mutuamente”, afirmó Antonio Gutiérrez, cofundador y coordinador estratégico de Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“El noroeste de Chicago fue uno de los puntos clave de la Operación Midway Blitz. Los miembros de la comunidad local se unieron para resistir este ataque, formando parte de la red estatal de respuesta rápida coordinada por ICIRR. Nuestra labor no terminó cuando concluyó la Operación Midway Blitz; a la fecha, seguimos presenciando secuestros y agresiones por parte del ICE en nuestros vecindarios. Los miembros de la comunidad seguirán haciendo su parte para mantenernos a salvo. Ya es hora de que los departamentos de policía locales cumplan con su deber e investiguen las acciones de estos agentes para que podamos exigirles responsabilidades. Es lo mínimo que merecen los miembros de nuestra comunidad y los vecinos que sufrieron ataques con gases lacrimógenos y gas pimienta, además de agresiones y violencia por parte del gobierno federal”, declaró el pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, presidente de la junta directiva de PLSNA.

“El miedo que recorrió nuestras comunidades es real, pero este año no estuvo definido por el miedo, sino por la belleza y la resiliencia de nuestra comunidad. La administración Trump se propuso dar un ejemplo con Chicago. En cambio, nosotros dimos el ejemplo: construimos una respuesta coordinada a nivel estatal que ha conectado a decenas de miles de miembros de la comunidad con asistencia legal, así como una red de respuesta rápida que demuestra que los inmigrantes de todo Illinois nunca están solos”, afirmó Eréndira Rendón, vicepresidenta de Justicia para Inmigrantes de The Resurrection Project.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representative Val Hoyle (OR-04), released the following statement after joining a bipartisan, bicameral coalition of over 250 lawmakers in a court filing challenging the legality of the President’s Executive Order attempting to control mail-in ballots ahead of the election.

“The Constitution is clear: States have the authority over time, place and manner of our elections. Not the President,” said Rep. Hoyle. “This Administration must stop their unconstitutional attempts to limit vote-by-mail, create a 'citizenship verification list’ and attempt to take over our elections.”

More information on the Amicus brief can be found here. This action comes just days after Rep. Hoyle joined nearly one hundred Members of Congress in calling on the U.S. Postal Service to not implement its rule restricting mail-in voting.

Following the Learning Agenda Playbook (the Playbook) release this morning, state leaders from the eight pilot states praised the framework as a resource to improve state education policies, programs, and student outcomes. The Playbook marks a pivotal milestone in returning education to the states and driving improvements at the state and local levels.
Click here for more information about the Playbook.
Click here to view the Playbook.
- Arkansas Secretary of Education Jacob Oliva: “Arkansas is proud to partner with the Department, alongside other states, to identify problems of practice and develop lasting solutions. This Playbook will help drive improved outcomes for all students by advancing a unified accountability approach and strengthening coordinated support across our education system.”
- Georgia State School Superintendent Richard Woods: "Too often, states are asked to do 'just one more thing,' adding paperwork and administrative burdens that do little to improve outcomes for students. What makes this work different is that it helps us focus on the 'one thing' that matters most. In Georgia, this project is helping us build better systems and connect more meaningfully with those closest to the work — our teachers, students, families, and other stakeholders — as we implement our core goals. We appreciate the U.S. Department of Education's commitment to investing in states as they implement their strategic priorities. Ultimately, we know this work will help us ensure that every action we take as an agency has the greatest possible impact where it matters most: in the classroom."
- Idaho Superintendent of Public Instruction Debbie Critchfield: “The development of Idaho’s Learning Agenda has provided a framework for evaluating the impact of our initiatives and priorities while strengthening our data-driven decision-making. This pilot has also improved communication across our teams and better aligned our efforts around our student outcome goals. That connection helps ensure the work we do is focused, coordinated and ultimately making a difference for Idaho students.”
- Kansas Commissioner of Education Dr. Jake Steel: “We are grateful for the opportunity to participate as a pilot state in the Learning Agenda Initiative. This work gave Kansas dedicated time and support to bring people together around a coherent approach to school improvement and better align our priorities, resources, research and evaluation. Learning alongside other states strengthened our work and will help us make evidence-based decisions, continuously improve our efforts and achieve better outcomes for Kansas students.”
- New Hampshire Commissioner of Education Caitlin Davis: “The Learning Agenda process has been an important part of our work at the New Hampshire Department of Education. As a pilot state, it gave us a structured opportunity to step back, ask the right questions, and use evidence to sharpen our priorities and direction. This has been especially helpful as we develop New Hampshire’s new statewide literacy plan and identify the strategies that will have the greatest impact on student achievement. Through this work, we have also connected with partners in other states that have undertaken similar efforts and learned a great deal from their experiences. The Learning Agenda has helped us better align our work and establish a strong foundation for improving outcomes across the state. We appreciate the U.S. Department of Education for giving New Hampshire the opportunity to participate.
- Tennessee Commissioner of Education Lizzette Reynolds: “Tennessee’s participation in the Learning Agenda initiative is an exciting opportunity to ensure we have the right information aligned with TDOE priorities and to identify practical solutions to current challenges. By highlighting powerful stories of impact and effective practices across our state, we can motivate educators and stakeholders to replicate what works best for students nationwide. This commitment to continuous improvement will help drive sustained progress in education.”
- Utah Superintendent of Public Instruction Dr. Molly Hart: "Developing data-driven solutions is essential to meeting the unique needs of our students and schools. Partnering in the development of the Learning Agenda Playbook has helped strengthen our state's capacity to turn research into actionable, impact-focused strategies. We are proud to support this tool to help education leaders nationwide use evidence to strengthen student success."
- Wisconsin Superintendent of Public Instruction Dr. Jill Underly: “The learning agenda presented Wisconsin with an opportunity to add capacity to our state's existing strategic plan, specifically around early childhood. We were able to map data and systems to plan for change that better aligns the multiple agencies and partners working to serve young children. It also reinforced alignment with all of Wisconsin's technical assistance partners.”

These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

Scam centers in Southeast Asia steal billions of dollars from American victims each year. Xinbi Guarantee operates a large illicit online marketplace that is used to support cyber scams, fraud, money laundering, and other criminal activity targeting Americans. The Trump Administration will not let insidious criminal networks prey on the American people—cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes end here.

Today’s actions were taken in furtherance of Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens” and pursuant to E.O. 13581 “Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations,” as amended by E.O. 13863.

GRANITE CITY, IL — Yesterday, Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) met with leadership at Gateway Regional Medical Center to address serious concerns surrounding patient-safety and the hospital’s ongoing financial crisis. In an exclusive interview with KMOV David Amelotti, Budzinski shared what was discussed in the closed-door meeting and emphasized what must be done to ensure the community continues to have access to quality care and hospital staff have the resources they need.

Watch the full interview HERE.

In August, reporting from KMOV raised serious concerns around billing and staffing issues at Gateway that were impacting patient care. Budzinski immediately sprang into action, reaching out to the state and ultimately sending a four-page letter to American Healthcare Systems CEO and Gateway Regional Medical Center CEO, Michael Sarian and Joe Ottolino, demanding clear answers on Gateway’s finances, employee benefits, and staffing stability.

In response to the letter, hospital leadership agreed to meet with the Congresswoman in person. Budzinski visited the hospital to hear directly about the challenges facing the facility, and discuss a path forward to address concerns about patient care and the hospital’s financial stability. Going forward, Budzinski is pushing Gateway to make serious and meaningful improvements to adequately serve patients in the community and remain in a position to provide the quality care patients deserve and continue receiving critical Medicare and Medicaid funding.

“Exercising your right to worship should not require you to exhibit particular courage as you enter your synagogue, church, mosque, temple, mandir, or gurdwara,” said Congressman Suozzi. “I will always stand up for people’s right to protest peacefully, but attendees of religious services should not be harassed, threatened, intimidated, or targeted for practicing their faith. I am proud to lead this bipartisan and bicameral Right to Worship Act that both protects free speech and the freedom to worship.”

“The breadth of support for the Right to Worship Act is very gratifying. So many groups recognize the horrifying reality that the threat to the freedom to not unique to any one faith or congregation. Every religious community feels it, which is why this bill will protect everybody,” Suozzi continued. “I’m proud to stand with such a broad coalition of faith leaders united behind this essential legislation to safeguard the right to worship for every religious community on Long Island, in Queens, and across America.”

Congressman Suozzi’s Right to Worship Act follows his earlier introduction of the SACRED Act in April 2026. Suozzi worked with colleagues in both parties and chambers to build bipartisan, bicamerical support for his buffer zone legislation, introducing the Right to Worship Act in the House with Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC) last month alongside a companion measure in the Senate by Senators Cruz (R-TX) and Slotkin (D-MI). Suozzi also expanded the coalition of organizations supporting the legislation, securing the endorsement of more than 20 national groups across faiths for the Right to Worship Act.

Suozzi was introduced today by Alan Mindel, Chair of the Board of Directors for the Holocaust Memorial and Tolerance Center.

“We at HMTC at our core believe in the religious freedom of all citizens and recall the words of Goerge Washington that “The Government of the United States… gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance,” said Alan Mindel. “This bill grants necessary protections to houses of worship so as to protect the constitutional rights of freedom of religion granted to all Americans. In the current climate where people have been obstructed from entering their house of worship, this new law will allow each American, regardless of faith, to freely enter their church, synagogues, or mosque for their constitutionally protected right to pray, without obstruction or harassment. We applaud Congressman Suozzi and all the sponsors of this important piece of legislation.”

In addition to Mr. Mindel, Suozzi was joined by ADL (Anti-Defamation League) New York/New Jersey Deputy Regional Director Brandi Katz Rubin, American Jewish Committee Long Island Director Eric Post, UNITED SIKHS community advocate Inderjeet Singh, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha representative Girish Patel, and Bishop Lionel Harvey. Additional organizational and congregational leaders, including rabbis and synagogue presidents, attended as well to show their support for the legislation.

The Right to Worship Act would establish a 100-foot, protest-free buffer zone around houses of worship during religious services, making it unlawful to knowingly disrupt or impede people from attending. The bill prohibits conduct that knowingly “hinders,” “deters,” “threatens,” or “intimidates” worshippers trying to enter religious services and would impose civil fines for violations. It authorizes individuals, the U.S. Attorney General, and state attorneys general to sue violators. Peaceful expression protected by the First Amendment is excluded from the bill’s prohibited activities.

The legislation is endorsed by a broad coalition of groups representing a variety of faith communities, including:

Anti-Defamation League (ADL)

Agudath Israel of America

Union for Reform Judaism

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

U.S. Embassy Quito

Quito, Ecuador

September 9, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO: All right, let’s go. Hold on.

QUESTION: Secretary Rubio —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

QUESTION: Can I – are you worried at all that U.S. partnership with Ecuador and some of the accusations of human rights abuses or disappearances will undermine and – the U.S. partnership with Delcy Rodríguez in Venezuela, Bukele and some of his accused abuses – will undermine the goodwill that you guys are —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, but all these governments are – for example, Ecuador is going to get attacked by left-wing groups that have ties to terrorists. These groups – you know the brutal – the real human rights violations happening in this part of the world is on behalf of narcoterrorists and this web of narcoterrorists who, like – they cut people’s heads off; they decapitate people. They go through and they extort people, like small vendors, in these towns, in these cities, in these countries. These vendors – that used to happen – in El Salvador you couldn’t even run a small coffee shop. They’d come in an extort you for money or they’d kill your children. These are the real human rights violator; these are the real terrorists. And these are the people that are being dealt with.

And you have to deal with these people in a very strong way, and that’s who we’re aligning with. We are aligning with governments and leaders that are willing to be serious about taking these groups on, as opposed to leaders who in the past, like we had with Petro in Colombia, are actually on the take or aligned with these terrorist organizations and these narco groups and so forth.

So you have to make a choice here. We’re going to choose on the side of leaders that are going to be serious about taking these groups on and eliminating them once and for all. Otherwise, those groups – those terrorist groups – will eat these countries up. They will become stronger than the governments in these countries. They will run over these countries. So I’m glad we have leaders in the region that are willing to be strong and take these groups on.

QUESTION: What about —

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, there’s a sense out there – an impression, I guess – that the strategy, the actual strategy towards combating these groups, and especially on the water, has changed a bit from where, when it began, it was just you blew the ships out of the water. And now it seems that you intercept them first, stop and get the people off, and then —

SECRETARY RUBIO: It depends.

QUESTION: Then sink them. So (inaudible).

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, it depends. So it depends on the country. So for example, with – no, because in many of these, these are bilateral operations. They’re – they’re occurring, for example, in territorial waters. So when you cooperate with Ecuador – they’ve been very cooperative – we’re jointly operating with them. So it depends on the vessel; it depends on the threat it poses; it depends on where it’s located. But these are part of the bilateral agreements we have with these countries, which is an – I think an incredible advance for the first time to have countries that are willing to participate in these efforts in their territorial waters. And then obviously we have to operate according to their laws in their territorial waters or their systems and protocols that they set in place. The important point is that these routes are being disrupted. These routes are being ended.

QUESTION: Right. But does that mean that these countries – it’s more palatable or legal for these countries to do it in this way, stopping the ship, getting the people off, and returning them to the —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, again, it depends – and we still blow-up ships if need be.

QUESTION: No, I know, but they’re empty now.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, again, it depends. Every target is selected. Obviously it goes through all the lawyers at the Department of War. But it’s also – these are joint operations, so you’re operating in conjunction with another nation-state. And so when you’re conducting a joint operation in territorial waters, you have to reach an understanding as to how those operations are going to occur, and every one of these countries have their own laws, they have their own systems that they have to comply with. Some can be more aggressive than others.

So I think, really, it’s a strike-by-strike or operation-by-operation determination, but again, understand the difference between that and what you saw early last year is those were unilateral operations in international waters. These are combined operations in territorial waters, where we are working with sovereign nations in their own territorial waters. And when you do that, you have to do it based on the understandings that you have with them, and they have to comply with their own laws, their own systems, their own protocols.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary —

QUESTION: (In Spanish.) Ecuador has high expectations regarding its trade relationship. We Ecuadorians have high expectations regarding what will happen with the trade relationship. We still have surcharges, and you pointed out yesterday in your column which was published in various media outlets that, as you continue to work on security issues, the scope of security measures will expand. Could we expect to have a trade agreement in the near future?

SECRETARY RUBIO: (In Spanish.) We are working on it. And keep in mind that the tariffs aren’t specifically directed against Ecuador, they apply to all countries around the world. And the way to deal with that is through a bilateral agreement – and we’re making good progress in those negotiations. We’ve made significant progress, and I expect good news soon. That’s related, but it’s not a condition for continuing our cooperation. In terms of security – and beyond tariffs – there’s a whole range of investment opportunities. Bringing investment into this country creates jobs and at the same time, helps revive industries that were being plundered by these groups and gangs – these bandits, criminals, and terrorists who are stealing the gold, stealing the copper, stealing everything. This country’s wealth isn’t benefiting the people; it’s benefiting people who don’t even live here. And that’s also part of the economic recovery.

(In English) The question was about – look, we’re engaged – it’s important to understand our tariffs on Ecuador and – it’s not on Ecuador. We have tariffs on everybody because of the 302 process. But we are engaged in talks. We’ve – they’ve progressed very well. I hope we’re going to have very good news soon. But the tariff situation is not a condition of closer economic cooperation.

As an example, this is a country that has incredible critical mineral reserves. They have some of the largest copper mines in the region. They have illicit gold mining going on right now. None of this money is benefiting the people of this country. All of that is being stolen by these terrorist organizations, and the money is going into the pockets of people many of whom don’t even live in this country. They live in Spain. They’re hiding in Mexico. They don’t even live here.

So part of our cooperation with them is ensuring that they can recapture and retake what belongs to the people of this country, and have professionalized operations in these mines that are environmentally sensitive, that pay the workers what they should be paid, and that the revenues from that benefit the people of this country and create jobs for the people of the country, not for a bunch of terrorists and not for a bunch of criminals who have long run roughshod – not just in Ecuador but all these other countries – oftentimes, sadly, with the cooperation of elected officials and government officials in these countries. And this administration here is putting an end to that.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary —

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, there have been three attacks on U.S. ships in – some have been very close calls, and officials —

SECRETARY RUBIO: On what, naval vessels?

QUESTION: On naval vessels, sorry, yeah.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

QUESTION: And officials have been telling us that they’re certain that Iran is getting help. Who’s it coming from, and what is the U.S. going to do about it if they’re getting help?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I don’t know what official told you that.

QUESTION: Some other official in the administration —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I don’t know. I mean, these are anonymous people. They make stuff up all the time. The truth —

QUESTION: So you don’t think Iran is getting help?

SECRETARY RUBIO: We don’t believe anybody is giving Iran anything that’s changing the dynamics or the parameters of what we’re seeing. At the end of the day is they continue to fire at our naval ships, and when they fire at our naval ships, they pay a price in tankers. They lose a lot of tankers. They don’t hit our ships, but they lose five tankers. They lost five more last night – four were damaged; one was sunk – so they’ll continue to pay price for that. In the meantime, we’re going to continue to strangle them economically.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, returning to the issue of boat strikes in Latin American waters, the United States has been very open about these boat strikes; it’s released videos of most of them.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Mm-hmm.

QUESTION: But there were three earlier this year, three boats that were blown up earlier this year, near Galapagos in Ecuadorian waters. Our reporting has found that that was a CIA covert program. Why has the United States not publicly acknowledged that, and is there any more you can say about these three (inaudible) strikes?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I don’t – I’m not going to comment on your reporting. I don’t even know if your reporting is accurate when you say that. I can tell you that we have – we – but I’m not talking about that incident. In general, we haven’t hidden the fact that we are going to go after narco-trafficking boats. We’ve been doing it now for over a year, and now the difference is that we’re doing it in collaboration and in cooperation with – working alongside countries in the region, in their territorial waters. And in fact, some of these countries are taking the strikes themselves.

So that’s what I can tell you. We’re going to continue to do it. And we’re not just going to continue to do that. These terrorist groups have to be dismantled – not just by blowing up their boats and taking their boats; they have to be dismantled financially. I don’t know if you guys fully comprehend how deeply rooted into societies these criminal bands have become. I mean, you had people in governments here that are complicit with them and what they were doing. It’s illegal mining, but it goes all the way down to the street level – murder, extortion, murder for hire, you name it. I mean, these groups became more powerful than governments in many cases. And if you don’t confront these groups, they will eat these countries alive. It’s like a cancer that continues to grow until you don’t literally have a state anymore. You become an ungovernable territory. And we don’t want to see that, they don’t want to see it, and I’m glad that we have leaders in this region that are serious about going after these groups, because if we didn’t, we would have failed country after failed country in the region. And so we’re very happy that we have partners now in this region, in Colombia, in Ecuador, in El Salvador, and in other places that are being very aggressive about taking these groups on and dismantling them before it’s too late.

QUESTION: (Inaudible.)

QUESTION: Did President Noboa express any concern, though, about fishermen who have been caught up in this, who have been killed or arrested?

SECRETARY RUBIO: I mean, I didn’t discuss it with him. I think at the end of the day these are joint operations. We’re conducting them in coordination with them. And as I said, our goal is not to go after fishermen; our goal is to go after drug traffickers. Our goal is to go after drug boats. Our goal is to go after illegal fishing and stop those from going out there. There are – there is illegal fishing. They’re raping the Galapagos. I mean, they are destroying that part of the world with illegal fishing vessels that are out there. We don’t bomb them, but we certainly want to arrest people that are involved in illegal fishing. Because again, those fisheries belong to Ecuador; they don’t belong to illegal narco-trafficking groups and these terrorist organizations.

QUESTION: (In Spanish.) I don’t know if you’re concerned that, as a result of the Monroe Doctrine, there is a possibility that leftist movements might begin to emerge in Latin America.

SECRETARY RUBIO: (In Spanish.) The thing is that leftist movements exist in Latin America; they have existed for a long time and have ruined the countries. What have leftist movements done in this hemisphere? Nothing but misery – misery in Venezuela, misery in Cuba, misery in Nicaragua, in this country. How did all these criminal gangs get in here? In collaboration with whom? With the left, with the leftist movement. What happened with Petro in Colombia – a country that for four years was unable to fight against these criminal groups as it should have? They even have ties to those groups. So those movements already exist. What we’re not going to allow is to live in a region that eventually threatens the United States’ national security – a region with transnational groups that are more powerful than the government, armed with government weapons, drones, and a range of military technology that threatens the State and will eventually threaten the United States.

(In English) The question was whether I was worried about left-wing groups or left-wing movements rising in – as a result of U.S. policy. Left-wing groups have already been here, and they’ve destroyed the hemisphere. The left wing destroyed Venezuela, the left wing destroyed Cuba, the left wing destroyed Nicaragua. The left wing has basically destroyed every country they’ve gotten a hold of in the hemisphere. Not only have they done that here in Ecuador as well, not only have they done that in Bolivia – look what Bolivia has suffered for 25 years because of left-wing governance. On – and in fact, not only did these groups destroy these countries because of bad economic policies in places like Ecuador and in Colombia over the last four years; these left-wing groups are actually in alliance with these criminal narco-trafficking organizations. They are aligned with them. They are allied with them. They permit them to conduct these activities in a nefarious alliance between them.

So I’m glad that’s being confronted. And by the way, these groups are not just threats to these countries; they ultimately become threats to the United States. I work for the United States of America. And if a threat in this region is emerging to the national security and national interest of our country, we are going to address it. And what we’re very happy about is that we can now address it in partnership with other presidents and other leaders in this region that feel the same way.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary —

QUESTION: Secretary Rubio, if you’re talking about groups that are stronger than the state and fracturing the states, it sounds like a pretty similar situation to Mexico. What’s – what —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, Mexico’s bad. It’s a bad situation.

QUESTION: So what’s the – given the fact that the Mexican Government isn’t welcoming, or draws a pretty bright line about what it will accept in terms of U.S. military involvement, how – what is the plan for that? How can you overcome that and have this kind of more tough approach that you’re describing?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, that’s a – yeah. The case of Mexico’s a – it’s an even graver challenge because of the size of the country, because of the power of the cartels that are there. I don’t think it’s any mystery to anybody that there are territories, vast territories in Mexico that are not governed by the state; they are controlled by these narco-terrorist organizations.

Now, I will say this: In fairness, the Mexicans have done more than they’ve ever done before to go after these groups. But it is still not nearly enough. They know that; we’ve expressed that to them. And we hope to work cooperatively with them to do more. Because at the end, the head of the snake are these cartels in Mexico. And they are a threat to the Mexican state, and the people of Mexico will tell you that. The number one issue in Mexico, poll after poll shows, is security. Political candidates are routinely assassinated in Mexico; judges routinely assassinated; journalists who report on the cartels routinely assassinated by these groups. So these groups pose an enormous threat right on our border. They have drones now. They’re using drones to try to traffic drugs and people across the border.

These groups are very dangerous, they’re very well financed, they need to be confronted. Our hope and our intent is to do it in partnership with Mexico. That’s the ideal. But eventually, that threat will have to be confronted, one way or the other. But our hope is to do it cooperatively with Mexican authorities.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary —

QUESTION: (In Spanish.) Ecuador is taking action against criminal groups with support from the United States. Is there no risk of mistakes being made – for example, with the interceptions of vessels that have occurred in recent weeks in the Pacific, which have raised concerns that fishermen engaged in their work could die?

SECRETARY RUBIO: (In Spanish.) Nobody is looking to kill fishermen here. But the greatest risk is that these groups will continue to operate, because they are killing people. While some cities here are very safe, there are others with murder rates higher than any other city in the region and that poses a danger to the people. I imagine that those listening to me are familiar with some of these cities, either personally or through people they know who have been threatened, murdered, had their businesses taken away, or have suffered at the hands of these criminal gangs. We must stand up to these people; we must do something. And I’m glad there’s a President here who’s willing to take action. That is the greatest risk we face.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary —

SECRETARY RUBIO: All right. We got to wrap up. Quick, go.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, will you meet with Delcy Rodríguez if she comes to New York for the United Nations General Assembly?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Maybe, maybe. We’ve talked quite a bit. Maybe. She’ll be there in New York. I don’t know if she’s actually going, but if she does, that probably will happen. But we haven’t scheduled anything yet. But sure, we’ve talked a bunch of times.

QUESTION: Ecuador rejected foreign bases here, I think last year. Did you discuss expanding the U.S. military presence? How far would you like to – did you discuss that with Noboa today or —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we’re conducting joint operations now. We don’t necessarily need to have a base here in order to do that. They had a referendum vote last year. We didn’t discuss that today. I’m aware of the vote that they had. But the most important thing is not having a base or not having a base. We’re open to it if they change their mind. But in the interim, we’re operating – our elite forces are operating alongside one another going after these groups, and I think that’s an incredible development, and that’s an important development. That’s the only way you’re going to beat these narcotrafficking terrorists.

All right. One more, and then we got to go, because —

QUESTION: (In Spanish.) Ecuador has signed an agreement with the United States as a third country to receive migrants. And, as I understand it, a group from Ecuador is coming. How does that agreement work? Where will they arrive, what kind of migrants are they, and what nationalities do they have?

SECRETARY RUBIO: (In Spanish.) Well, first of all, obviously, when you make an agreement with a country, that country has the right to see a list. We send them a list of names with their backgrounds and all that information, and they decide who gets in and who doesn’t. They can veto any name. “No, I don’t accept this person.” They even control the number: 50, 20, 10. That’s up to the governments. That’s the agreement. It’s a bilateral agreement. We’re not going to send a plane full of people they don’t know and with as many people as we want. It’s a bilateral agreement. And most people who are in the United States illegally, when given the option to go to a third country or return to their own country, they return to their own country. The vast majority do so, and that is really the most important function you have in those agreements.

QUESTION: (In Spanish.) Where do people who are deported to a third country go? I mean, Ecuador, for example, where?

SECRETARY RUBIO: (In Spanish.) We provide funding and assistance to help these people get settled. Eventually, I imagine these individuals will seek to return to their own countries, which, at the end of the day, is the goal. And they have the right to do so immediately. If they decide tomorrow that they’re going to return to their country, they aren’t sent to a third country; however, the countries with which we have these agreements always have the right to say, “I don’t want this person,” or “It can’t be 20, it has to be 10.” They always have that option. All right, one more and we go.

(In English) All right. One more and we go. Okay, I will – all right.

QUESTION: No, I have – I have one question. Yesterday, President De La Espriella was talking about his plan to expand investment and have this kind of reciprocal economic growth and investment between the United States and Colombia.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

QUESTION: But oftentimes, the U.S. companies haven’t invested as much as U.S. governments would have liked for – maybe because of internal regulations or for whatever reason. Do you think that the United States, the Trump Administration, can actually make the investment happen? Because I think one of the things we saw in Venezuela was that this deal that you all just finalized came after the U.S. oil majors weren’t willing to go in in the same way. What’s your thought regarding company —

SECRETARY RUBIO: No. Well, first of all, that’s an inaccurate description. And these people that have reported it, they don’t know what they’re talking about. The problem is that we moved faster than the private sector on the investments in Venezuela because we had a very unique opportunity. But there are – Chevron’s already expanded their operations. There are other smaller operations that are going in. And then there are companies like Exxon that, so far, have decided not to go in because they have a long history of expropriation, and frankly, they don’t like the fields that are being offered to them, so they’d prefer not to go in. Someone else will go in.

So – but the deal had nothing to do because of American companies weren’t moving fast enough. We just had a very unique opportunity to be involved in something that was beneficial to the country of the United States, who I work for, but also beneficial, in the long term especially, for the people of Venezuela.

In the case of Colombia, look, attracting investment there – obviously, there’s always going to be security concerns. If you don’t have security, no one’s going to invest in the country – security meaning physical security, but also legal security. Is the government stable? Are the laws going to be applied? That’s always important. And I think with a new president and a new administration a lot of that is going to be solved. And then there’s just the mechanisms – identifying investment opportunities and pairing the investment opportunity with the American company.

I think in the case of Colombia it’s going to be less problematic, because there has been a long history of American investment in Colombia already. And I think the only thing we’re working through is there are some programs – whether it’s Millennium Challenge, whether it’s some of our investment funds – that can serve as a catalyst for some of that investment to happen. So we’re trying to identify whether some of these programs can be used to serve as a catalyst to speed up that investment and that economic recuperation, especially in areas that involve critical minerals and energy.

Okay?

QUESTION: Thanks.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Natural gas – natural gas is important. Okay, guys. Thank you.

QUESTION: Thank you.

Tags
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to Press

WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Robin Kelly (IL-02), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), and Emily Randall (WA-06) led 49 Members of Congress in sending a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz calling for an immediate end to the sharing of Medicaid enrollee data with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Despite a federal preliminary injunction limiting data transfers, CMS continues to share private data belonging to millions of enrollees—including U.S. citizens and lawful residents—beyond court-approved limits. Reports also reveal ICE improperly mishandled the data across internal channels and shared it with third-party analytics contractors like Palantir Technologies.

"The role of HHS should be to protect the health of all those living in this country and provide essential human services, not to be a watchdog for DHS or act as immigration enforcement," the Members stated in the letter.

JERSEY CITY, NJ – El miércoles, los Representantes Rob Menendez (NJ-08), el Presidente del Caucus Hispano del Congreso, Adriano Espaillat (NY-13) y Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) realizaron una visita de supervisión en Delaney Hall, operado por GEO Group, tras las repetidas denuncias sobre las condiciones dentro del centro de detención, incluyendo reportes de comida en mal estado, aire acondicionado inadecuado o no funcional y graves preocupaciones sobre el acceso a atención médica oportuna y adecuada.

Tras la visita, los miembros emitieron la siguiente declaración conjunta:

"El ICE y GEO Group tienen una responsabilidad con las personas que mantienen bajo custodia federal. Lo que escuchamos y observamos hoy deja en claro que quienes se encuentran en Delaney Hall continúan siendo peligrosamente desatendidos.

Nos reunimos con personas que detallaron la demora o negación de atención médica cuando las personas están enfermas o con dolor, la entrega de alimentos en mal estado e inseguros, y un aire acondicionado inadecuado que obliga a las personas a soportar condiciones peligrosas. Esto es un fracaso de atención y supervisión financiado con fondos federales.

Seguiremos exigiendo respuestas claras sobre lo que está ocurriendo dentro de esta instalación, incluyendo las muertes de personas detenidas en Delaney, qué está haciendo el DHS para abordar estas condiciones y por qué las personas bajo custodia federal se han visto obligadas a soportarlas en primer lugar."

Los miembros continuarán revisando la información recopilada durante la visita de hoy y llevarán a cabo una supervisión adicional según sea necesario, incluyendo la búsqueda de respuestas de los funcionarios federales y los operadores de la instalación con respecto a las condiciones reportadas en Delaney Hall.
title: Los Reps. Menendez, Espaillat y Mejia realizan visita de supervisión en Delaney Hall tras reportes de condiciones negligentes

Today, U.S. Representative Sharice Davids announced that she secured $8.3 million for the Kansas State Department of Education through the U.S. Department of Education’s Teacher and School Leader Incentive Program (TSL). The program strengthens teacher and school leader recruitment, retention, professional development, and leadership opportunities across the country.

“I went to Kansas public schools and became a first-generation college student, so I know firsthand how much a good teacher and a strong education can change a student’s trajectory,” said Davids. “This new investment will help Kansas continue to build the kind of schools where students can thrive by supporting the teachers and school leaders who show up for our kids every day.”

The TSL program helps schools recruit and keep quality teachers and school leaders. The funding can help schools provide teachers with additional training and coaching, create opportunities for experienced teachers to take on leadership roles, and offer incentives for educators who take on more responsibility. The program also helps schools attract and keep strong educators in low-income and rural communities where they are needed most.

A U.S. Department of Education evaluation of the program’s predecessor found that performance-based incentives led to student achievement gains equivalent to roughly three to four additional weeks of learning. The TSL program has since funded 160 projects serving more than 2,000 schools in 36 states and Washington, D.C.

Last year, Davids spoke out against the Trump Administration’s plan to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education, warning that eliminating the department could put critical education funding and services at risk for students, teachers, and families. She has continued pushing for federal investments that support Kansas classrooms, including securing funding for early education, STEM programs, and apprenticeships.

This award includes $2,903,167 in base funding and $5,483,666 in additional frontloaded funding, bringing the total FY 2026 award to more than $8.3 million. The FY 2026 TSL program is expected to provide approximately $60 million nationwide through competitive grants to eligible state agencies, school districts, and other organizations.
title: Davids Secures Major Federal Award to Recruit, Support Kansas Teachers

Joint Investigation by the U.S. Justice Department and U.S. Department of Education Finds U.C. Berkeley Law School Discriminates Based on Race in Admissions
The U.S. Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division (DOJ) and the U.S. Department of Education (ED) announced today joint investigative findings that the University of California, Berkeley School of Law (Berkeley Law) deliberately discriminates against white and Asian students in its admissions process. Berkeley Law’s discriminatory conduct violates Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of race or color, and the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2023 decision in Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard (SFFA), which banned race discrimination in higher education.
“Berkeley Law School’s deliberate efforts to circumvent the Supreme Court’s decision in SFFA demonstrate a complete disregard for the rule of law,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “The Department will continue to aggressively pursue compliance from schools who attempt to racially manipulate their student bodies in violation of federal law.”
“Title VI is clear: no student should be advantaged or disadvantaged in admissions because of the color of their skin,” said U.S. Department of Education Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey. “The Supreme Court made equally clear that universities cannot evade the law by finding new ways to make race a factor in admissions decisions. Today’s findings demonstrate that the Trump Administration will work to hold institutions accountable and ensure students are judged on their individual merit, not their race.”
The Department’s investigation found that post-SFFA, Berkeley Law uses race, essay prompts, and other tactics to further its admissions diversity goals. For instance, Berkeley’s application asked applicants to specify their racial identity, so that admitted students could be “grouped” with others of the same “primary identity” in class. In other words, Berkeley Law intentionally separates admitted students by race.
The data produced by Berkeley Law demonstrates a strong bias against Asian and white applicants, with a corresponding bias in favor of black applicants. In 2024 and 2025 (combined), half of Berkeley Law’s admitted black applicants had LSAT scores that were below 95% of the admitted white applicants. Worse, more than one-third of admitted black applicants (37%) had LSAT scores below 99% of admitted white applicants. The Department’s analysis further revealed that in 2025, black applicants had 5.8 times higher odds of admission than comparable white applicants.
As recipients of federal financial assistance, law schools are subject to federal non-discrimination laws. The Department will continue to investigate their compliance with Title VI, as interpreted by SFFA’s prohibition on race-conscious admissions. Where a violation has been found, the Department will engage in settlement negotiations to ensure the school’s admissions practices are brought into compliance. If those efforts fail, the Department will file suit.
Members of the public may report possible civil rights violations at www.civilrights.justice.gov/.
Note: Read the Department’s Findings Letter here.
title: Joint Investigation by the U.S. Justice Department and U.S. Department of Education Finds U.C. Berkeley Law School Discriminates Based on Race in Admissions

Maryland Woman Sentenced to Prison for $1.1M Tax Refund Fraud
A Maryland woman was sentenced today to 12 months and one day in prison for attempting to steal more than $1.1 million from the IRS by filing false tax returns.
According to court documents and statements made in court, between December 2019 and March 2020, Kendra Scarborough, of Oxon Hill, filed three false tax returns in the names of purported trusts that she controlled. In total, these tax returns sought more than $1.1 million in refunds that the trusts were not entitled to receive. Scarborough’s scheme resulted in the IRS issuing a refund of $412,000 to one of the purported trusts. Scarborough used these funds to pay for, among other things, the mortgage on her personal residence and other creditors.
Scarborough pleaded guilty to one count of theft of government funds. In addition to the term of imprisonment, U.S. District Judge Debrorah L. Boardman ordered Scarborough to pay $410,117.44 in restitution to the IRS and forfeit to the government the proceeds from the tax refund that remain in her bank account.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case.
Trial Attorney Melissa Siskind of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Maryland Woman Sentenced to Prison for $1.1M Tax Refund Fraud

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

September 9, 2026

The United States is exposing corruption at the highest levels of Ecuador’s justice system. The Department of State is publicly designating seven former Ecuadorian officials for their involvement in significant corruption linked to Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) designated by the Trump Administration last year. These actions render all seven individuals and their immediate family members generally ineligible for entry into the United States.

Pablo Ramírez Erazo, former director of Ecuador’s Prison Authority; Wilman Terán Carillo, former judge on Ecuador’s National Court of Justice; and Ronaldo Xavier Guerrero Cruz, former criminal judge on Ecuador’s Judicial Council, each significantly abused their former government positions by accepting bribes from gangs linked to narco-terrorist organizations. In exchange for bribes, these officials interfered with judicial, electoral, or public processes on behalf of Ecuadorian gangs linked to designated FTOs Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), Los Choneros, and Los Lobos.

Pablo Bolívar Muentes Alarcón, former member of the Ecuadorian National Assembly; María Fabiola Gallardo Ramia, former President of the Guayas Provincial Court; Johann Marfetán Medina, former criminal judge of the Guayas Provincial Court; and Mayra Carolina Salazar Merchán, former public relations officer of the Guayas Provincial Court, each abused their former public positions by accepting bribes in exchange for interfering with judicial processes to benefit narco-terrorist organizations like Los Choneros and the Sinaloa Cartel, and their criminal facilitators.

The former Ecuadorian officials’ actions constituted significant corruption and had serious adverse effects on the security of the United States, fueling drug trafficking and poisoning American communities. The United States will continue using every available tool to protect our country and deny entry to narco-terrorists, their corrupt facilitators, and their immediate family members. To any foreign officials corruptly abusing their public position for personal financial gain: the United States will find you and expose you.

These public designations are made under the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (Div. F, P.L. 119-75) (“Section 7031(c)”). Section 7031(c) requires the Secretary of State to publicly or privately designate foreign officials and their immediate family members about whom the Secretary has credible information of involvement in significant corruption or a gross violation of human rights.

WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of the Treasury today announced that its Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has identified approximately $17.5 billion in suspicious financial activity potentially linked to health care fraud, underscoring the Trump Administration’s commitment to eliminating fraud, protecting taxpayers, and safeguarding the integrity of federal health care programs.
“By identifying and reporting this suspicious activity, financial institutions have given law enforcement critical insight into the illicit actors who deliberately exploit U.S. health care benefits programs,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue working alongside our law enforcement partners to disrupt fraud wherever it occurs, protect Americans, and safeguard the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs.”
A new FinCEN Financial Trend Analysis finds that, over a one-year period, financial institutions filed more than 5,700 Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) reports flagging activity potentially connected to health care fraud. The findings provide law enforcement with critical financial intelligence to identify, investigate, and disrupt illicit schemes that exploit taxpayer-funded health care benefits.
Health care fraud drains resources from the Americans who rely on these programs, drives up health care costs, and can put patients at serious risk. Treasury is using every available tool to support President Trump’s agenda to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse across the federal government.
Working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud led by Vice President Vance, Treasury is encouraging whistleblowers to report credible information related to fraud, money laundering, sanctions violations, and tax-law violations. Tips from whistleblowers, combined with financial institutions’ BSA reporting, can help Treasury and its law enforcement partners uncover criminal networks, recover taxpayer funds, and hold bad actors accountable.
Treasury will continue to leverage financial intelligence, strengthen coordination across government, and pursue those who seek to profit by defrauding American taxpayers and endangering patients.
FinCEN analyzed 5,702 BSA reports filed by financial institutions between March 1, 2025 and February 28, 2026, and found the following prominent trends:
DEPOSITORY INSTITUTIONS ACCOUNTED FOR MAJORITY OF HEALTH CARE FRAUD-RELATED BSA REPORTS
- Depository institutions filed approximately 89 percent of reports in the dataset and accounted for nearly 87 percent of the reported suspicious activity amounts.
POTENTIAL HEALTH CARE FRAUD SCHEMES SPANNED MEDICARE, MEDICAID, AND PRIVATE INSURANCE
- Potentially fraudulent funds were often received from a combination of federal and state programs, as well as private insurance companies.
- Medicare payments frequently originated from Medicare Administrative Contractors whereas Medicaid payments originated from state-level administrators.
AN OVERWHELMING MAJORITY OF SUBJECTS WERE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES
- Filers identified subjects located in every U.S. state, as well as Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
- Of the approximately 13,000 subject addresses in the dataset, approximately 1.5 percent had a foreign address.
HOME HEALTH CARE BUSINESSES ACCOUNTED FOR THE LARGEST SHARE OF SUSPECTED FRAUDULENT PROVIDERS
- Home health care businesses were identified as the suspected fraudulent provider in 20 percent of all health care fraud-related BSA reports.
- Other frequently identified providers included hospice care companies, mental and/or behavioral health and addiction treatment providers and companies, medical equipment providers, and adult or child daycares.
SUSPECTED FRAUD PROCEEDS FUNDED PERSONAL SPENDING, LUXURY PURCHASES, AND OVERSEAS TRANSFERS
- Suspected perpetrators employed a range of money laundering techniques before spending the suspected fraudulently obtained health care payments.
- In many cases, proceeds of suspected health care fraud that did not appear to go through a complex funds transfer process were used on personal expenses and luxury goods, with some funds being sent internationally.
SOME SUSPECTED HEALTH CARE FRAUD PERPETRATORS WERE POTENTIALLY INVOLVED IN CRIMINAL NETWORKS
- A small percentage of filers reported suspected health care fraud activity potentially involving large fraud rings or criminal networks, as well as some potential connections to foreign entities.
Today’s FTA is FinCEN’s second health care fraud-related product issued this year. In March, FinCEN issued an Advisory on Health Care Fraud Schemes Targeting Medicare, Medicaid, and Other Federal and State Health Care Benefit Programs. Although BSA reports filed after the issuance of the Advisory were not included in the scope of this FTA, the typologies and trends in the post-Advisory BSA filings are consistent with the trends reported in the FTA.
FinCEN’s analysis of threat pattern and trend information derived from BSA data on additional topics can be found on its Financial Trend Analyses page.

EPA Inspections at Pembina, North Dakota, Land Port Expands National Crackdown on Illegal Imports
DENVER – Last week, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) joined U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to conduct inspections of imports coming from Canada and train CBP agents at the Pembina, North Dakota port of entry. This effort represents the first targeted inspection effort at a land port under the Trump Administration’s reorientation toward stopping illegal and harmful imports.
EPA is significantly expanding its imports investigative capacity and enforcement presence. In partnership with CBP, EPA inspects cargo at air, land, and seaports of entry throughout the United States. EPA works with CBP to block the importation of illegal chemicals, banned pesticides, and dangerous consumer products that threaten Americans’ health, food supply, economic stability and national security.
At land ports like the Pembina port of entry, cargo arrives on trucks, railcars, passenger vehicles and via pipeline. EPA discovered that foreign entities may obscure their cargo’s legitimate country-of-origin and route it through Canada in a practice known as transshipment, taking advantage of lower tariffs established under the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement. Inspections at land borders are critical to catching importers attempting to evade scrutiny through transshipments and preventing the importation of products that Canada may allow through.
“With this latest targeted inspection effort at the U.S.-Canada border, EPA is protecting Americans from illegal and harmful products and chemicals that Canada would allow through and strengthening its partnership with CBP to fortify America’s longest border,” said EPA Assistant Administrator Jeffrey A. Hall for the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. “This year’s inspection push at U.S. ports of entry has resulted in smarter, more coordinated inspection and enforcement efforts and reflects the Trump administration’s commitment to ensuring international commerce works for the American people.”
“This North Dakota inspection is the first of EPA’s 2026 national border enforcement pushes occurring at a land port,” said EPA Region 8 Administrator Cyrus Western. “By leveraging our decade-long partnership with Customs and Border Protection at Pembina, we’re expanding the types of products the agencies monitor for compliance and helping protect Americans at all points of entry into the U.S.”
Building on EPA and CBP inspection efforts over the past year, broader investigations are targeting toxic and polluting chemicals, illegal pesticides and products and materials containing substances that are dangerous to the health of American families. Dangerous consumer products include composite wood with formaldehyde, non-compliant vehicles and engines, plumbing products that may contain lead and more. This multi-statute, multi-sector inspection approach is conducted under the statutory authorities granted to EPA by the following:
- American Innovation and Manufacturing Act
- Clean Air Act
- Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act
- Safe Drinking Water Act
- Toxic Substances Control Act
EPA’s national and regional programs work alongside CBP officers and other federal partners to ensure that imported goods comply with environmental statutes before they enter the United States. CBP is partnering with EPA to streamline inspector access and strengthen the identification of products that may pose risks to human health or the environment. This cross-agency partnership enables EPA to make a final compliance determination, enforce the law and protect Americans.
title: EPA Inspections at Pembina, North Dakota, Land Port Expands National Crackdown on Illegal Imports
